Peel the cucumber and cut in half lengthways. Scoop out the seeds and slice into thin crescents. Place the fish on the serving dish and arrange the cucumber around the outside. Pour the sauce over and serve.

recipes.Title: Kai Phenang (Chicken in Peanut/Coconut Sauce)
recipes.Ingredients:
500g Chicken
1 tsp Salt
½ tsp Black pepper
1 tsp Crushed garlic
300 ml Coconut milk
1 tbsp Cumin seeds
½ tbsp Coriander seeds
2 Red chillies, chopped
1 tsp Shrimp paste
1 tbsp Light soy sauce
1 tsp Sugar
25 g Roasted peanuts
50 ml Coconut cream
Juice of a lime

For the garnish:
Chopped cilantro leaves
Finely shredded fresh red chilli
recipes.Preparation:
Cut chicken into serving portions and season well with salt and pepper. Fry in oil until browned. Place in coconut milk and bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the chicken from the coconut and set aside.
Toast the cumin and coriander seeds, chillies and shrimp paste in a dry pan, then grind into a smooth paste. Add the soy sauce and sugar and stir into the coconut sauce. Very finely grind the peanuts and add to the saucepan. Bring to the boil and simmer for 2 - 3 minutes. Add the coconut cream and simmer for 5 minutes. Return the chicken to the pan and simmer for 10 - 15 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and transfer to a serving dish. Flavour the sauce with lime juice and pour over the chicken. Serve garnished with the chopped cilantro and red chilli slivers.

recipes.Title: Moo Thod Katiem Prik (Pork with Hot Sauces)
recipes.Ingredients:
375 g Pork tenderloin
½ tsp Salt
¼ tsp Black pepper
1 tbsp Butter
1½ tbsp oil
1½ tsp Crushed garlic
1 tsp Minced, fresh ginger
1 Red chilli, finely chopped
1 Lemon grass root, finely minced

For the sauces:
1. Fresh red chillies, fresh ginger, spring onions and salt. Grind all to a smooth paste.
2. Tomato, finely chopped, garlic, salt, sugar, chilli, nam pla. Mix together.
3. Fresh red chillies, onion, minced, nam pla, lime juice, crushed, roasted peanuts.
recipes.Preparation:
Rub the whole pork tenderloin with salt and pepper, heat the butter and oil together and sauté the pork until evenly coloured. Remove the pork.
Add the garlic, ginger, chilli and lemon grass and fry briefly. Return the pork and roll in the seasonings until thickly coated. Continue to cook for about 8 minutes until tender.
Remove from the pan and allow the pork to cool. Cut into wafer thin slices and arrange on a serving dish, over-lapping in a rosette fashion. Serve with the sauces in small dishes at the centre of the platter.

recipes.Title: Yam Ma-La-Kaw (Green Papaya Salad)
recipes.Ingredients:
1 Large unripe papaya
6 Red chillies
125 ml Small dried shrimp, soaked in boiling water
6 Cloves garlic
Juice of 1 lime
Nam pla
Sugar
recipes.Preparation: Peel, seed and grate the papaya. Grind the rest of the ingredients together until a smooth paste, Add the papaya and serve with a garnish of salad items.

recipes.Title: Strawberry Bruleé
recipes.Ingredients:
350 g Strawberries
4 tbsp White wine
3 tbsp Toasted almond flakes
450 g Greek style natural yoghurt
6 tbsp Soft light brown sugar
recipes.Preparation:
Reserve 6 strawberries and slice the remainder. Soak the sliced strawberries in the wine for at least 30 minutes.
Divide the strawberries between 6 ramekin dishes and sprinkle with the almonds.
Top each dish with yoghurt, sprinkle with the sugar and place under a hot grill for 1 - 2 minutes until the sugar has caramelised.
Serve decorated with the reserved strawberries and a sprig of mint.

recipes.Title: Horchata de Chufas
recipes.Ingredients:
Tiger nuts
1 litre Hot water
Sugar
Zest of ½ lemon
1 stick cinnamon
recipes.Preparation: Soak the nuts in water overnight. Tip them into a sieve and rinse free of earth. Place in a food processor with half the hot water and whizz to make a milky fluid. Decant and add the rest of the water, then whizz again. Decant again and press all the fluid from the remaining paste. Sweeten the fluid to taste and add the lemon zest and a small stick of cinnamon. Cover and chill thoroughly.

recipes.Title: Salad iz svyokly (Beetroot Salad)
recipes.Ingredients:
500 g Beetroot, cooked and peeled
3 Cloves garlic, crushed
120 g Walnuts, finely chopped, leave a few whole for decoration
Sour cream or mayonnaise
Salt
recipes.Preparation: Grate the beetroot into a salad bowl. Add the garlic and the chopped walnut. Mix together well and add enough cream or mayonnaise to bind the mix together. Season with salt. Decorate the top of the salad with a few walnut halves.

recipes.Title: Salad iz Kapusty (Cabbage Salad)
recipes.Ingredients:
1 kg Cabbage, roughly chopped
2 Large tart apples
2 Eggs, hard boiled
2 Spring onions, chopped
Fresh dill, chopped
Olive oil
Lemon juice
Salt
Black pepper
Sugar
recipes.Preparation: Put the cabbage in boiling salted water for 3 minutes. Drain and chop finely. Grate the apples coarsely and add to the shredded cabbage. Mix in the eggs, spring onions and herbs. Pour over enough oil to coat and add a squeeze of lemon juice. Season with salt, pepper and sugar to taste.

recipes.Title: Pumpkin & Coconut Milk Soup
recipes.Ingredients:
1 Medium Butternut squash or pumpkin, cut into small cubes
½ tsp Ground ginger
¼ tsp Cayenne pepper
½ tsp Cinnamon
1 tsp Ground coriander
¼ tsp Ground nutmeg
¼ tsp Ground cloves
1 Large leek, sliced
2 Tins coconut milk
450 ml Vegetable stock
recipes.Preparation:
Fry the squash in a little butter and oil and add the spice mix. Add the sliced leek. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable stock.
Simmer gently until the vegetables are tender. Season and then liquidise.

recipes.Title: FlammenKüche
recipes.Ingredients:
For the Base:
250 g Plain flour
7.5 g Fresh yeast or
3.5g dried yeast)
½ tbsp Sugar
1 tsp Salt
50 g Soft butter
150 ml Milk

For the Topping:
150 ml Double cream
150 ml Curd cheese or fromage blanc
Salt
Pepper
2 tbsp Oil
200 g Smoked bacon, cubed
2 Medium onions, sliced thinly
recipes.Preparation:
Mix together the flour and salt. Work in the butter. Warm the milk, add the sugar and then the yeast and stand until it froths. Add to the flour and knead well to a smooth, firm dough. Allow to rise in the bowl until doubled in bulk.
Knock down the dough, flatten it and roll it out thinly on 2 -3 large baking sheets.
Pre-heat the oven to maximum heat.
Mix together the cream, curd cheese, salt, pepper and oil and spread it on the top of each base. Scatter the bacon and onions on top and bake immediately in a very hot oven for about 15 minutes or until dappled with gold.. They should be sizzling hot but still bendy.
Cut in slices , roll or fold them up and eat with the fingers.

recipes.Title: Linsengericht
recipes.Ingredients:
500 g Lentils
1 Onion
1 Bay leaf
1 Clove
1 tbsp Lard
1 tbsp Plain flour
1 tsp Tomato purée
1 tsp Grated horse radish
½ tsp Mustard
1 tbsp White wine vinegar
Salt
Pepper

Meat:
1 Smoked fillet of pork
4 Smoked chaps of pork
1 Carrot, sliced
½ Celeriac, sliced
4 Bratwurst
1 tbsp Lard
Sprig of parsley
recipes.Preparation:
Wash the lentils  and put them in salted water. Halve the onion and stick one half with the clove and a bay leaf and simmer for  about 1 hour.
In the meantime, cut the second half of the onion into small dice and fry in the pan with the lard and flour to form a brown roux. Allow this to get cold.
Take the onion out of the lentils, add the tomato purée and boil briefly, then stir in the brown roux. Add the horseradish, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Put the fillet and the chaps of pork in lightly salted, boiling water and allow to simmer very gently for about 1½ hours until tender. After about 45 minutes add the carrot and celeriac.
Fry the sausages in the lard. Put the lentils in a serving dish, slice the fillet and the chaps and arrange on top of the lentils with the sausages. Garnish with the carrot, celeriac and parsley.

recipes.Title: Pork Tenderloin Medallions in a Cream Sauce****
recipes.Ingredients:
2 Small pork tenderloins
Dash of lemon juice
1 tsp Cumin seeds
1 tbsp Ground coriander
1 tbsp Nando's chilli sauce
2 Large cloves garlic, thinly sliced
3 tbsp Double cream
Salt
Sesame oil
recipes.Preparation: Trim and slice the tenderloins into medallions about 10 mm thick.  Splash over a dash of lemon juice and massage into the pork. Allow to stand for 10 minutes. Heat the oil in a frying pan until very hot. Add the medallions and scatter over the salt, cumin seeds, coriander and salt. Fry the medallions until just beginning to colour on one side then turn and add the garlic slices and the chilli sauce. Cook for another few minutes until tender, lower the heat and add the double cream, Stir well into the meat juices to make the sauce.

recipes.Title: Steak & Kidney Pudding
recipes.Ingredients:
700g shin of beef 
170g pork / lamb / ox kidney 
1 chopped onion 
beef stock 

Pastry
170g suet 
340g flour (self raising) 
pinch of salt
recipes.Preparation:
Cube steak (bite size) and roll in flour.  Put in casserole dish with kidney (also rolled in flour) and onion and cover with stock.  Bring up to simmer for 2 hrs approx - do not let it dry out - top up with stock if necessary.  Leave to one side.
Make suet pastry by blending suet and flour and gradually adding water to bind to a good non-sticky dough ball.  Split this into 2 halves, roll out a round to line your pudding basin (ceramic / pyrex), over-lapping edges of basin.  Spoon in meat and kidney with slotted spoon and then pour over liquid.  Dampen the crust edges and then roll out a (thicker) lid to seal the pudding.  Layer about 3 sheets of foil over top of basin.  (Ma P's special tip: make a strip of foil to place under basin in casserole dish to lift out when finally cooked).  You will need a casserole dish / saucepan big enough to fit your pudding basin and add boiling water approx. 2/3 up side of basin - then simmer for further 2-3 hrs.

recipes.Title: Banana Cake
recipes.Ingredients:
120 g Butter
¾ cup Sugar
1 Egg
3 Ripe bananas, mashed
1½ cups Self-raising flour
125 ml Milk (maximum)
Vanilla extract
½ tsp Bicarbonate of soda
½ tsp Baking powder
recipes.Preparation:
Cream the butter and sugar. Add the egg and bananas and blend well. Add the flour, bicarbonate of soda and baking powder. Add as much milk as necessary to form a moist cake dough.
Place the dough in a buttered 2 lb loaf tin and bake at gas 6 (200°C) for 30 - 35 mins.

recipes.Title: Selsig Morgannwg - Glamorgan Sausages
recipes.Ingredients:
6 Spring onions, finely sliced
550 g Fresh white breadcrumbs
350 g Caerphilly cheese, crumbled or grated
Large handful of parsley, finely chopped
2 sticks Celery, finely chopped
3 Medium eggs, lightly beaten
1½ tsp English mustard
4 tbsp Vegetable oil
recipes.Preparation:
In a large bowl, mix together the spring onions, 400 g of the breadcrumbs, the cheese, parsley and celery. Beat together the eggs and mustard and add two thirds to the bowl. Mix well to combine.
Divide the mixture into 12 and shape each portion into a chunky sausage. Put the remaining beaten egg mixture and breadcrumbs onto two separate plates. Dip each sausage into the egg mixture and then into the breadcrumbs. Arrange on a plate and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the sausages in batches for 10 minutes until golden brown, turning occasionally.
recipes.Keywords: spring onion, caerphilly cheese, celery, eggs

recipes.Title: Proper Fish Pie
recipes.Ingredients:
700 g Potatoes, chopped into bite-size chunks
65 g Butter
550 g Mixed fish and shellfish (salmon, pollock, mussels and raw prawns)
450 ml Whole milk, plus a little for the mash
2 bay leaves
1 Onion, finely chopped
75 g Baby spinach
75 g Frozen peas, thawed
65 g Plain flour
450 ml Fish stock
2 eggs, hard-boiled and quartered
recipes.Preparation:
Put the potatoes into a pan of salted water , boil and simmer for 20 minutes until tender. Mash with 15 g butter and a splash of milk; set aside.
Put the fish into a pan, add the milk, bay leaves and onion and slowly bring to the simmer and poach for 5 minutes . Lift out the fish, break into large flakes and set aside. Strain the milk into a large measuring jug. Discard the bay leaves, then save and set aside the onions. Make the liquid up to 500 ml with water if necessary.
Melt 15 g butter in a pan and add the poached onion. Fry for 5 minutes then stir in the spinach and peas. Cook for a further 2-3 minutes until the spinach has wilted. Season and spoon into a bowl.
In the same pan, melt the remaining butter and stir in the flour. Cook over a low heat for 1 minute. Remove from the heat and slowly add the strained milk and fish stock, stirring all the time. Return to the heat and bring gently to a simmer, stirring constantly, until the sauce has thickened. Season as required.
Pre-heat the oven to gas 4(180°C). Gently mix together the poached fish, prawns, mussels and vegetables. Spoon into an oven-proof dish and dot with the eggs. Pour the over the sauce. Cover with the mashed potato and bake for 20 - 25 minutes until the topping is crisp and the pie is piping hot.

recipes.Title: Boxty Pancakes
recipes.Ingredients:
450 g Floury potatoes, like Maris Piper
75 g Plain flour
1 tsp Baking powder
150 ml Buttermilk
4 medium eggs
2 tbsp oil
4 Large rashers unsmoked bacon
15 g Butter
200 g Black pudding, chopped
150 g Cherry tomatoes, halved
2 tbsp Red wine vinegar
50 ml Vegetable stock
2 tbsp chives, chopped
2 tbsp oregano, chopped
1½ tsp salt
recipes.Preparation:
Chop HALF the potatoes and put into a pan of cold water. Bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes.. Mash and then set aside.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a large bowl. Grate the remaining potatoes, then wrap in a clean tea towel and squeeze out all the moisture. Add to the dry ingredients with the mash. Season with pepper and stir well. Mix together the buttermilk and the eggs, then stir into the potato mixture.
Pre-heat the oven to gas 4(160°C). Heat the oil in an oven-proof, 23-26 cm,  non-stick frying pan and pour in the potato mixture. Flatten the top and turn the heat to low. Cook gently for 10 minutes until golden underneath. Cover the pan with a plate and flip the pancake onto the plate, then slide the pancake back into the pan and cook the other side for 5 minutes. Transfer the pan to the oven and cook for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, fry the bacon, slice thickly and keep warm. In the same pan, melt the butter and add the black pudding. Fry for 5 minutes then stir in the cherry tomatoes, vinegar and stock and cook for 1 minute. Remove from the heat and add most of the herbs. Season and set aside.
When the pancake is ready, put onto a board and slice into six. Put each slice onto a plate and spoon over the black pudding and bacon mixture. Garnish with the remaining herbs.

recipes.Title: Baked, Stuffed Aubergines
recipes.Ingredients:
2 Large aubergines
5 tbsp Olive oil
2 Onions, finely sliced
2 tsp Cumin seeds
1 tsp Ground cinnamon
4 cloves Garlic, finely chopped
300 g Cherry tomatoes, halved
1 tbsp Tomato purée
100 g Mozzarella, diced
Finely chopped parsley to garnish
recipes.Preparation:
Pre-heat the oven to gas 6 (200°C). Halve the aubergines lengthways, score the flesh and scoop it out, leaving a 1 cm edge.
Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan and sauté the onions and aubergine flesh for 5 - 6 minutes. Add the cumin seeds, cinnamon, garlic, cherry tomatoes and tomato purée and stir-fry for a couple of minutes. Season well.
Spoon the mix into the aubergine shells. Scatter the mozzarella over and place in an oven-proof dish. Carefully pour around 250 ml hot water. Cover the dish with foil and bake for 40 - 45 minutes until tender. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

recipes.Title: Plum and Almond Galette
recipes.Ingredients:
6-8 Plums, pitted and sliced
125 g Caster sugar
150 g Ground almonds
450 g Sweet shortcrust pastry
Icing sugar, for dusting
Whipped cream to serve
recipes.Preparation:
In a medium-sized bowl, gently toss the plum slices with the citrus peel, lemon zest, flour, caster sugar and ground almonds.
Pre-heat the oven to gas5 (190°C). Lightly flour a clean surface and divide the pastry into 6. Roll out each portion to form a piece about 18 cm square and 5mm thick. Put the pastry squares onto 2 large non-stick baking sheets lined with baking parchment. Place the plum mixture in the centre of each square, leaving a border of 5 cm on all sides. Fold the edges of the pastry up and over so that the filling is still visible.
Place the galettes in the oven and bake for 35 - 40 minutes until the pastry is lightly browned and the filling is bubbling. Cool on a rack for one hour, dust with icing sugar and serve with whipped cream.

recipes.Title: Chicken and Ham Croque Monsieur
recipes.Ingredients:
4 Slices good white bread, buttered
100 g Gruyere, grated
200 g Cooked chicken breast, shredded
4 Large slices cooked ham
4 tbsp Butter, melted
4 tbsp parmesan, grated
recipes.Preparation:
Sprinkle half the gruyere cheese over 2 of the slices of bread, then cover the cheese with the shredded chicken and ham. Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top, season well with salt and pepper, then top with the remaining slices of bread. Press down firmly.
Brush half the melted butter on top and sprinkle half the parmesan over. Place the sandwiches under a pre-heated grill for about 2-3 minutes. When golden brown, turn them over, brush with the remaining butter, sprinkle with the remaining parmesan and grill for a further 2-3 minutes. Remove the sandwiches, cut in half diagonally and serve.

recipes.Title: Carrot and Coriander Soup
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp Olive oil
1 Onion, chopped
5 Carrots, diced
½ tsp Ground cumin
2 tbsp Fresh coriander leaves, chopped
1 litre Vegetable stock
4 tsp Crème fraiche
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oil in a saucepan and sauté the onion until transparent. Add the carrots, cumin and 1 tbsp of the coriander leaves and sauté over a high heat for 2 minutes, stirring continuously. Add the vegetable stock and cook for 15 minutes until tender. Leave to cool for a few minutes.
Purée the mixture for at least 1 minute. re-heat if necessary and season to taste.
Serve with a spoonful of crème fraiche, freshly milled black pepper and some coriander leaves.

recipes.Title: Mexican Casserole
recipes.Ingredients:
500 g Steak Mince
2 x 400 g Cans of chopped Italian tomatoes
1 Red pepper, chopped
1 400 g Can Kidney beans
2 Medium onions, chopped
4 Large cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp Olive oil
175 ml Greek style yoghurt
4 Fresh red chillies, finely chopped
1 tbsp Honey
200 g Macaroni
Basil
Marjoram
Salt
Black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Sauté the onions and beef briefly and then add the red pepper and minced garlic; sauté for 3 minutes.
Add all the other ingredients except the kidney beans, bring to the boil and cover and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the kidney beans and simmer for a few more minutes.

recipes.Title: Stuffed Cabbage Leaves
recipes.Ingredients:
Butter
Savoy cabbage, large
Onion, medium, finely chopped
8 Garlic cloves
2 tsp Caraway seeds
2 Bay leaves
2 tsp Smoked paprika
50 g Raisins
Zest of ½ lemon
40 g Long grain rice, cooked and cooled
200 g Minced beef, lean
200 g Minced pork
8 smoked Polish Kabanos sausages
500 g Tomato passata
150 ml White wine
2 tsp Pepper
1 tbsp salt
Sour cream, to serve
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oven to gas 5 (170°C). Lightly butter a shallow, oven-proof dish; a lasagne dish is ideal.
Remove 12 large leaves from the cabbage, wash and cut out the tough stalk from the base, leaving the leaves intact. Blanch the leaves for 2 minutes in boiling water to soften and then plunge into ice-cold water and leave for 5 minutes. Drain well.
Melt a large knob of butter in a frying pan and gently cook the onion and garlic with the caraway seeds and bay leaves until very soft and lightly coloured. Stir in the paprika and cook for 2 minutes more. Tip the mixture into a large bowl, remove the bay leaves and add the raisins, lemon zest, rice and minced meats. Season with the salt and pepper and mix really well. Divide the stuffing into 12 portions and place in the centre of each cabbage leaf. Fold in the sides and roll to make neat parcels. Place in the dish with the edges tucked under. Nestle the sausages between the cabbage rows. Mix the wine with the passata and a pinch more salt and pour over the cabbage and sausages. Cover with foil and bale for 45 minutes.
Remove the foil, splash over the soured cream and serve with boiled potatoes.

recipes.Title: Porcini and Spinach Risotto
recipes.Ingredients:
25 g Dried porcini
50 g Butter
1 Onion, small, finely chopped
1 clove Garlic, crushed
200 g Chestnut mushrooms, sliced
150 g risotto rice
1 glass White wine
750 ml vegetable stock, kept simmering
100 g Spinach, chopped
Parmesan
recipes.Preparation:
Soak the porcini in a cup of boiling water for 10 minutes. Strain the liquid through a sieve to remove any grit and keep the liquor for the risotto. Roughly chop the porcini.
Heat the butter in a wide shallow pan and cook the onion and garlic until softened. Add the chestnut mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes then add the porcini and rice and stir until coated.
Tip in the wine and bubble until it's all absorbed. Gradually add the porcini liquor and then the stock, stirring until the rice is al dente. (All the stock may not be required.) Stir in the spinach until just wilted. Serve sprinkled with parmesan.

recipes.Title: Lamb Dhansak
recipes.Ingredients:
100 g Red lentils
500 g Butternut squash, cubed
2 Onions, roughly chopped
400 g Tin chopped tomatoes
1 tsp Turmeric
1½ tsp Cumin seeds
1½ tsp Coriander seeds
4 Cardamom seeds, squashed
400 g Lamb, lean and diced
20 mm cube Fresh ginger, grated
4 cloves Garlic, crushed
6 Green chillies, sliced
1 tsp Garam masala paste
Oil
Small bunch fresh coriander leaf
recipes.Preparation:
Put the lentils, butternut squash, onion and tomatoes in a pan with the turmeric, salt and add water to cover. Simmer gently for about 20 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Put the cumin, coriander and cardamom in a small pan and toast until fragrant then cool and grind.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the lamb in batches and brown all over. Scoop out and add the ground spices. Cook for 2 minutes then add the ginger, garlic and chillies. Cook for a few more minutes and then add the lamb, lentils and squash and about 200 ml water. Cover and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, removing the lid for the last 30 minutes. The lamb will now be tender and the sauce will have thickened. Stir in the garam masala and fresh coriander and serve with basmati rice or chapatis.

recipes.Title: Chocolate & Cardamom Torte
recipes.Ingredients:
300g dark chocolate roughly chopped
150g unsalted butter
6 eggs, separated
40g golden caster sugar
1¼ tsp ground cardamom

Chocolate sauce:
200g chopped milk chocolate
1 tsp ground cardamom
recipes.Preparation: Heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4.  Line a 18cm springform cake tin with greaseproof paper.  Melt the dark chocolate together with the butter in a heatproof bowl over a pan of simmering water or in the microwave.  Beat the egg yolks, half the sugar and the cardamom  until pale, very thick and creamy.  Add the melted chocolate and mix well.  Whisk the egg whites and remaining sugar until stiff.  Now carefully fold the egg whites into the chocolate mixture making sure you stir it very gently.  When mixed, spoon it all into the prepared tin and bake for 20-25 minutes.  Set aside to cool.  The finished torte should have a baked-mousse-like consistency.  For the chocolate sauce, bring 100ml water to the boil, add the milk chocolate and cardamom and whisk until thick and glossy.  Serve with the torte.

recipes.Title: Chorizo and Black Bean Soup with Avocado Salsa
recipes.Ingredients:
SALSA:
½ Avocado, cubed
Juice of one lime
Bunch of coriander, roughly chopped
SOUP:
250 g Black turtle beans, soaked overnight
1 litre Chicken stock
75 g Chorizo, finely sliced
1 Onion, finely chopped
142 ml tub Sour cream
recipes.Preparation:
Mix the avocado cubes with the lime juice and chopped coriander.
Cook the turtle beans and onion in the chicken stock in a covered pan for 45 minutes. Stir in half the chorizo. Divide the soup between 4 bowls and add a spoonful of sour cream to each.
Top the soup with the salsa and the remaining chorizo.

recipes.Title: Baked Custard with Blackcurrants
recipes.Ingredients:
400ml double cream
200ml milk
A dash of vanilla essence, or ½ vanilla pod
6 egg yolks
70g caster sugar
200g blackcurrants, topped and tailed
2 desertspoon sugar
Crème de cassis or cassis
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to 140 C.
Warm milk and cream together with vanilla. When almost at boiling point, take off heat and allow to infuse for half an hour.
Whisk egg yolks together until pale and creamy. Pour cream mixture over eggs and sugar and mix well. Strain into a 9 inch shallow gratin or other ovenproof dish. Place in a bain marie and bake until just set – about 50 minutes. Remove from bain marie. 
While the custard is cooking, place half the blackcurrants with half the sugar and booze/fruit vinegar in a bowl. Mix well and allow to sit. Put the rest of the fruit in a pan with sugar and a desertspoon of water. Dissolve sugar and remove from heat. When cool, mix with the other blackcurrants . Drizzle over baked custard before serving.

recipes.Title: Blackcurrant Fool
recipes.Ingredients:
1kg blackcurrants
brown sugar to taste 
300ml double cream
icing sugar to taste
1 egg white, beaten until stiff
recipes.Preparation:
Pick over and rinse the blackcurrants. Stew lightly with lots of brown sugar – enough so that the fruit doesn’t make your mouth pucker at all. Cool. Mush though a mouli or blender with restraint – just a few pulses. Last time I did this I made it so runny I had to pour the fruit over a handy packet of trifle sponges: but if you add no water (stew slowly to avoid catching) you may not need these. It’s more aesthetically pleasing without.
Whip the double cream, stir in a few tablespoons of icing sugar and fold in the beaten egg white. Pour the blackcurrants into a pretty white china, or better still, a glass bowl, or individual glasses, adding sponges if necessary. Spoon the cream mixture on top

recipes.Title: Butternut Squash with Pork Chipolatas
recipes.Ingredients:
1 Butternut squash, peeled and cut into 20-25mm cubes
1 Large onion, quartered and coarsely sliced
1 Red pepper, sliced
1 Birds eye chilli, very finely chopped
1 tbsp Cumin powder
1 tbsp Coriander powder
Olive oil
Salt
Black pepper
12 Good quality pork chipolata sausages (Tesco traditional pork chipolatas were found to be good)
recipes.Preparation:
Put 2-3 tbsp olive oil into a large roasting pan, add the spices, salt and pepper and place in a pre-heated oven at gas 5 (190°C) for about 5 minutes. Remove the pan from the oven, thoroughly mix the spice/oil blend and add the vegetables. Toss to completely cover the vegetables in the spiced oil. Place in the oven and set the timer for 40 minutes.
Squeeze each sausage at the centre and twist to form mini-sausages and cut into two. Put all the sausages into a frying pan and fry until well coloured.
Add the sausages to the vegetables and thoroughly mix together. Return to the oven until the 40 minutes has elapsed.

recipes.Title: Blue Cheese Dressing
recipes.Ingredients:
190 ml Sour cream
330 ml Mayonnaise
115 g Blue cheese, crumbled
½ tsp dry mustard
1 tsp Worcester sauce
2 cloves garlic, crushed
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper
recipes.Preparation: Place all ingredients in a large bowl and whisk together. Cover, place in refrigerator for 24 hours before serving.

recipes.Title: BLT Salad with Basil Mayonnaise Dressing
recipes.Ingredients:
225 g Back bacon cut into small strips
125 ml Mayonnaise
2 tbsp Red wine vinegar
60 ml Basil, chopped
4 Slices of bread (baguette if possible), cut into ½ inch cubes
1 tsp Salt
1 tsp Black pepper
1 tbsp Sesame oil
½ Lettuce, torn into pieces
350 g Cherry tomatoes, cut into quarters
recipes.Preparation:
Cook the bacon until evenly brown. Reserve 2 tbsp of the dripping. Whisk together the dripping, mayonnaise, vinegar and basil and let this dressing stand at room temperature.

In a large skillet, toss the bread pieces, salt and pepper over a medium heat, drizzle with oil and continue to cook until golden brown.

Toss the lettuce, tomatoes, bacon and croutons in a large bowl. Add the dressing and toss well before serving.

recipes.Title: Red Pepper Hummus with Smoked Paprika
recipes.Ingredients:
2 cloves Garlic
425 g can of Chick peas
160 g Sweet red peppers (from a jar is best or fresh grilled)
1 tsp Honey
Tabasco to taste
½ tsp Smoked paprika (to taste)
Black pepper
recipes.Preparation: Whizz the garlic, chick peas, red pepper and honey in a food processor until a smooth purée. Add the tabasco and black pepper to taste. Grind some black pepper over the hummus to serve.

recipes.Title: Spinach and Pea Pithiviers
recipes.Ingredients:
375 g Puff pastry made with butter
250 g Baby spinach leaves
200 g Petit pois
4 tbsp Mint, chopped
200 g Cream cheese with garlic
4 tbsp Cream to glaze
Salt
Black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Cook the spinach in a dry saucepan for a few minutes until wilted; drain and cool. Season with salt and black pepper.

Mash the peas and mint together in a food processor.

Lay the pastry on a board and roll out a bit thinner. Cut out four 10 cm and four 17 cm circles. Place the spinach on each of the 10 cm circles leaving a 1 cm edge. Place the garlic cream cheese on top of the spinach and then heap the pea mix on top. Cover each with the 17 cm circles and crimp the edges. Prick the centre of each pie and decorate by cutting spiral swirls into the tops.

Bake the pithiviers at gas 6 (200°C) for about 25 minutes or until puffed up and golden brown..
recipes.Keywords: puff pastry, spinach, peas, cream cheese

recipes.Title: Brazilian Chicken with Coconut
recipes.Ingredients:
2 g ground cumin 
2 g ground cayenne pepper 
2 g ground turmeric 
2 g ground coriander 
4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves 
salt and pepper to taste 
30 ml olive oil 
1 onion, chopped 
6 g minced fresh ginger 
2 jalapeno peppers, seeded and chopped 
2 cloves garlic, minced 
3 tomatoes, seeded and chopped 
1 x 400ml can light coconut milk 
1 bunch chopped fresh parsley
recipes.Preparation:
Mix the cumin, cayenne pepper, turmeric, and coriander in a bowl. Place the chicken in the bowl, season with salt and pepper, and rub on all sides with the spice mixture. 
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Place the chicken in the skillet. Cook 10 to 15 minutes on each side, until no longer pink and juices run clear. Remove from heat and set aside. 
Heat the remaining olive oil in the skillet. Cook and stir the onion, ginger, jalapeno peppers, and garlic 5 minutes, or until tender. Mix in the tomatoes and continue cooking 5 to 8 minutes. Stir in the coconut milk. Serve over the chicken. Garnish with the parsley.

recipes.Title: Chicken and Coconut in Banana Leaves
recipes.Ingredients:
5 ml low-sodium soy sauce 
5 ml barbeque sauce 
2 g minced fresh ginger 
180 ml coconut milk 
2 chicken drumsticks 
2 chicken thighs 
2 yellow plantains, peeled and cut into 3/4 inch slices 
1 sweet potato, peeled and cut into thick sticks 
1 fresh, unsplit banana leaf
recipes.Preparation:
Whisk together soy sauce, barbeque sauce, ginger, and coconut. Pour over chicken drumsticks, thighs, plantain, and sweet potato in a resealable plastic bag. Seal, and marinate 30 minutes. 
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). 
Gently warm the whole banana leaf over a fire or gas burner until the leaf is pliable, but not burnt, 3 to 4 minutes. Cut the leaf into four large squares, measuring at least 12x12 inches. Carefully cut four long, thin strips from the rib of the leaf, these will be used as 'string' to tie the packets later. 
Place a piece of meat onto each banana leaf square, and evenly divide the vegetables on top. Pour in any remaining marinade, and fold the leaves around the chicken like a present. Securely tie with the rib strips, and place the packets onto a baking sheet. 
Bake in preheated oven until the chicken is tender and no longer pink in the centre, about 1 hour. Check the packets occasionally to make sure they do not burn.

recipes.Title: Imam Bayildi
recipes.Ingredients:
2 large Aubergines
Olive oil
2 large Onions, finely chopped
230 g Tomatoes, chopped
3 large cloves Garlic
1 tsp Cinnamon
1 tsp caster sugar
1 tbsp Parsley, chopped
1 tbsp Pine kernels, chopped
Salt
Black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Place the whole aubergines in a large pan of boiling water, cover and cook for 10 minutes. Drain the pan and plunge the aubergines into cold water; leave for 5 minutes. Cut them in half lengthwise and scoop out most of the flesh leaving a 1.5 cm shell. Arrange the shells in a roasting tin and sprinkle with salt and black pepper. Pour 4 teaspoons of olive oil into each shell, place in a pre-heated oven at 180°C for 30 minutes.

While the aubergines are cooking, gently fry the onions and garlic for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes, cinnamon, sugar and parsley; season to taste with salt and pepper. Continue to simmer this mixture for about 20 minutes, until reduced by about 50%. Chop the aubergine flesh and add to the mixture with the chopped pine kernels. Cook for a further 10 minutes.

Remove the aubergine shells from the oven, stuff them with the mixture and serve hot or cold.

recipes.Title: Orzo ai Frutti di Mare
recipes.Ingredients:
180g Orzo
1 bag mussels
10 king prawns, shelled
150 ml Prosecco
Saffron, 10 strands
6 cherry tomatoes, chopped
3 cloves garlic, minced
1 large shallot, finely chopped
1 tsp dried Basil
few flakes of chilli
Fish stock
Olive oil
Butter
recipes.Preparation:
Was and remove the beards from the mussels. Reject any that do not close after tapping. Wash and de shell the prawns.

In a large saucepan, fry the shallot in half olive oil - half butter until soft. Add the minced garlic and fry for a minute. Add the chopped tomatoes, prosecco, fish stock, chilli and saffron and bring to the boil. Add the basil and mussels, return the pan to the boil and add the mussels. Place the lid on and simmer for a few minutesa until the mussels have opened.

Remove the mussels from the pan and shell, placing the mussels into a bowl.

Reduce the mussel juices by 50% or more and then add the mussels from the bowl.

Add the orzo to boiling, salted water with a knob of butter and cook until al dente (about 7 minutes).

Briskly fry the prawns in butter and olive oil until pink and add to the mussels in sauce.

Turn the orzo out onto a plate and place the seafood on top.

recipes.Title: Salmon with Fennel and Potatoes
recipes.Ingredients:
300 g waxy new potatoes
1 small bulb fennel
Salt
Black pepper
1 bunch fresh flat-leaf parsley, leaves picked and finely chopped
2 cloves garlic, peeled and finely chopped or grated
15 g butter, cut into small pieces
olive oil
2 x 120 g salmon fillets, scaled and pin-boned
a few sprigs fresh mint, finely chopped
pinch of dill
1 small handful Parmesan cheese, grated
zest of 1 lemon
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat your oven to 220°C/gas mark 7. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Halve the potatoes lengthways and trim the fennel bulb, reserving the leafy fronds for garnishing later. Cut the fennel bulb into eight wedges, add these to the salted water with the halved potatoes and parboil for around 6 minutes.

Drain the vegetables in a colander and leave to steam-dry for a minute. Transfer to a large roasting tray and season well with salt and pepper. Drizzle well with olive oil, toss everything together in the roasting tray, then shake it out so it is in one even layer. Cook in the oven for about 30 minutes, or until golden.

While the vegetables are roasting in the oven, start preparing the salmon fillets. Skin the fillets and pinch them so they plump up and use the length of a knife to score them. You want to score about 1cm down into them. Soften the butter and blend in minced garlic, dill, chopped mint and parsley. Push this mix into all the cuts in the fish.

Once the potatoes are nice and golden, take them out of the oven and sprinkle the grated Parmesan over them. Give everything a bit of a jiggle, then lay the salmon on top. Sprinkle the lemon zest over the top, drizzle with olive oil then cook for 15 minutes.

Just before the salmon comes out of the oven, chop the reserved fennel fronds. Sprinkle them over the finished dish, then serve it with some wedges of lemon.

recipes.Title: Salmon with a Parmesan and Lemon Zest Crust
recipes.Ingredients:
Charlotte or Jersey Royal potatoes
Green Beans
Two fillets of salmon, pin bones removed
Butter
2 cloves garlic, mashed
Dill
Parmesan cheese, grated
Zest of half a lemon
Salt
Black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Clean and pat dry rhe salmon fillets, Soften the butter and fold in the mashed garlic and a ½tsp of dried dill. Finely grate the parmesan and the zest of ½ a lemon. Score the salmon and paste the butter mix into the cuts. Sprinkle the fillets with parmesan and lemon zest and then season with salt and black pepper. Preheat oven to 200°C (gas mark 6).

Boil the potatoes and then when there are 15 minutes to go put the salmon in the oven in a baking tray. At 10 minutes to go boil the beans in salted water.

Serve the salmon with buttered potatoes, beans and with a nice Prosecco.

recipes.Title: Mango Caramel and Cream Napoleons
recipes.Ingredients:
FOR THE MANGO CARAMEL
    3 ounces (6 tablespoons) unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
    1/2 cup granulated sugar
    1 cup light-brown sugar
    1 teaspoon coarse salt
    1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
    1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
    1/4 cup fresh lime juice (from 2 limes)
    2 large mangoes, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch dice

FOR THE MANGO FILLING
    2 large mangoes, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch dice
    1/2 teaspoon finely grated lime zest
    1/4 cup fresh lime juice (from 2 limes)
    8 fresh mint leaves, julienned, plus sprigs for garnish

FOR THE MINT CREAM
    1 cup heavy cream
    1/2 cup packed fresh mint leaves, roughly chopped
    1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract

FOR THE SPICED PHYLLO
    2 ounces (4 tablespoons) unsalted butter
    1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
    1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
    2 tablespoons confectioners' sugar, plus more for dusting
    6 sheets phyllo dough, thawed if frozen
recipes.Preparation:
Make the spiced phyllo: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Melt butter with cinnamon and ginger in a small saucepan. Cut 2 pieces of parchment to fit a rimmed baking sheet. Brush 1 piece of parchment with spiced butter, and sprinkle with 1 tablespoon confectioners' sugar. Place 1 phyllo sheet on top, and gently brush with spiced butter. Top with another phyllo sheet. Repeat, buttering and layering remaining sheets. Sprinkle remaining tablespoon confectioners' sugar on top. Using a paring knife, trim edges of phyllo to fit parchment, then cut into about 24 2-by-3 1/2-inch rectangles (don't cut through parchment).
Transfer parchment and phyllo to an upside-down rimmed baking sheet. Brush remaining sheet of parchment with spiced butter, and place on phyllo, buttered side down. Place another baking sheet, right side up, on top of phyllo. Bake until golden brown, 12 to 14 minutes. Transfer phyllo to a wire rack, and let cool. Phyllo will keep, covered, for up to 3 days.

Make the mint cream: Bring cream and mint to a boil in a small saucepan. Remove from heat, cover, and let stand for 1 hour. Prepare an ice-water bath. Strain cream into a bowl, discard mint, and stir in vanilla. Cover, and place bowl in ice-water bath. Let cool, stirring occasionally, about 20 minutes.

Make the mango filling: Combine all the ingredients in a bowl.

Make the mango caramel: Prepare another ice-water bath. Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add sugars, salt, ginger, and cinnamon. Cook, whisking constantly, until sugars begin to dissolve. Add lime juice, and cook, stirring often, until sugars dissolve and sauce thickens slightly. Stir in mangoes, bring to a simmer, and cook until mangoes are tender, about 15 minutes. Transfer to a bowl. Place bowl in ice-water bath, and let cool, stirring occasionally.

Place 2 tablespoons mango caramel in a medium bowl. Add mint cream, and whisk until soft peaks form.

To assemble: Place 1 phyllo rectangle on a plate, and spoon mango caramel over top. Top with mango filling. Using an offset spatula, spread 1 tablespoon whipped cream on top. Top with a second piece of phyllo, then caramel, filling, and cream. Dust a third piece of phyllo with confectioners sugar, then place on top. Repeat with remaining phyllo, caramel, filling, and cream. Garnish with mint sprigs, and serve.

recipes.Title: Celeriac tartare with smoked trout
recipes.Ingredients:
1 small celeriac
2 x 125g packs smoked trout, flaked
100g bag rocket
extra-virgin olive oil, to drizzle

For the tartare dressing:

6 tbsp mayonnaise
1 small handful capers, rinsed and chopped
2 tbsp lemon juice
2 tbsp cornichons, finely chopped
1 small handful parsley leaves, finely chopped
recipes.Preparation:
Combine all the ingredients for the tartare dressing with some salt and set aside.

Peel the celeriac and, either finely slice it, then cut into matchsticks, or simply grate it coarsely. Mix the celeriac into the dressing until combined. Place piles of smoked trout, celeriac and rocket onto serving plates and drizzle everything with olive oil.

recipes.Title: Scallops with lemongrass and chilli
recipes.Ingredients:
70 ml dark soy sauce
    1½ tbsp lemon juice
    ½ tsp chilli oil
    1 tsp lemongrass, finely diced, white part only
    1 garlic clove, crushed
    1 tbsp brown sugar
    2 kaffir lime leaves, stems removed, finely sliced
    2 tbsp vegetable oil
    18 scallops, roe removed
    1 long red chilli, seeded and julienned
    coriander, to garnish
recipes.Preparation:
1. In a mixing bowl, combine the soy sauce, lemon juice, chilli oil, lemongrass, garlic, sugar and half the lime leaves. Whisk well to dissolve the sugar, then set the dressing aside.

2. Heat a flat chargrill pan or frying pan to very high. Add the vegetable oil. Add the scallops to the pan and allow to cook for 30 seconds before turning. Take care not to cook the scallops all the way through, as they will continue to cook once taken off the heat. The scallops should be slightly caramelized around the edges.

3. Remove the seared scallops to a serving platter, or to individual clean scallop shells, if you have some. Spoon the dressing over, garnish with the remaining lime leaves, chilli and coriander and serve.

recipes.Title: Chicken or Steak Fajita
recipes.Ingredients:
Main dish:
6 breasts of chicken or 
4 x 250 g steaks cut into large pieces and deeply scored on one side (prawns as an alternative)
2 large onions, coarsely sliced
2 red peppers, coarsely sliced
For the marinade:
4 tbsp oil
3 tbsp lime juice
1½ tbsp ground cumin
1½ tbsp oregano
6 large cloves of garlic, crushed
4 red chillies, finely chopped
salt and black pepper
Guacamole:
4 ripe avocados, coarsely chopped
2 shallots, finely chopped
2 large tomatoes, finely chopped
2 red chillies, finely chopped 
Lemon juice to taste
Salt and black pepper
Salsa:
6 large tomatoes
2 green chillies, finely chopped
1 medium onion, finely chopped
1 tbsp lime or lemon juice
salt and black pepper

Cheddar cheese, grated
Sour cream
Lettuce, thinly sliced
12 flour tortillas heated in the microwave for one minute, cover with a clean tea towel or napkins to serve
recipes.Preparation:
Marinade - combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly. Put in the meat and rub the marinade well into the scored flesh. Leave for at least two hours at room tremperature.
Prepare the guacamole and salsa ahead of time.
Guacamole - combine all ingredients in a bowl and mash with a fork. Leave some small chunks of avocado to give texture. Cover
Salsa - combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly. Cover
Cheese - grate and cover
Lettuce - thinly slice and cover.
15 minutes before serving, take four long dishes and arrange the salsa, guacamole, cheese, lettuce and sour cream in bands across the dish.
Place four metal skillets under the grill and heat some oil in three heavy, cast iron pans.
Cook the onions and red peppers in two of the pans over high heat to slightly caramelise.
Cook the meat over a high heat enough to brown on both sides. Remove from the heat and slice the meat.
Place some of the onions and red peppers onto each skillet; they will sizzle if the skillet is hot enough.
Top with some of the meat.
Serve with the guacamole and salsa and the hot tortillas.

recipes.Title: Pork and Chorizo Casserole
recipes.Ingredients:
2 good Chorizo sausages
2 thick pork loin steaks
2 carrots, sliced into short sticks
1 can peeled plum tomatoes
1 stick celery, finely sliced
10 shallots peeled, whole
2 tins of beans (mixed beans, butter beans, kidney beans, borlotti beans or black-eyed peas - your choice
1 can of vegetable soup
6 cloves garlic, crushed
2 red chillies, finely chopped
1 tbsp paprika powder
Salt and black pepper
Oil
recipes.Preparation:
Put the oil into a heavy, oven-proof casserole. Fry the shallots until beginning to brown. Add the garlic and meat and briskly cook for 5 minutes. Add the carrots and celery and cook for a further few minutes. Add the sliced chorizo, soup, beans and canned tomatoes. Heat all together for a few minutes and then flavour with the chilli, paprika ans salt and pepper.

Place in an oven at gas mark 5, 180°C cook for one hour.

Remove and serve with a good, full-flavoured rioja wine and some crusty baguette.

recipes.Title: Butternut Squash Soup
recipes.Ingredients:
1 butternut squash, diced
1 red onion, chopped
1 large shallot, chopped
2 tsp ginger, chopped
2 stalks lemongrass, bruised (you could use 2 x tsp of pre-minced lemongrass in a jar)
4 kaffir lime leaves, finely chopped
6 cloves garlic, minced
1 red chilli, chopped
2 tbsp red curry paste
1 chicken stock pod
1 tbsp fish sauce
1 tbsp sriracha sweet chilli sauce
2 x 50g sachets of cocnut cream or 1/2 can of coconut milk
Juice of 1 lime, chopped raw cashews
recipes.Preparation:
Sauté onions, chilli and squash in a large saucepan on high for 5 minutes.
Add red curry paste and garlic and sauté a further 5 minutes.
Add enough water to cover the ingredients, and throw in the lemongrass, ginger, kaffir lime and stock pod.
Simmer until the squash is cooked.
With a stick blender, purée the soup to make it smooth.
Start tweaking the flavours, add the fish sauce and sweet chilli sauce, add half a cup of chopped, fresh coriander, the coconut milk and any of the optional extras.
Taste and then adjust the flavour to your liking. If it’s too strong, add some more milk, more sweet chilli if it’s too salty, etc.

recipes.Title: Linguine Carbonara
recipes.Ingredients:
4 rashers smoked back bacon, sliced into small strips
3 large cloves garlic, minced
300g fresh linguine or 200g dried pasta
2 large eggs
25 g fresh, grated parmesan cheese
salt 
black pepper
40 g fresh grated parmesan cheese for serving
recipes.Preparation:
Fry the bacon strips in a pan over low heat until crisp, add garlic and fry until golden.

Boil the water with a knob of butter and a pinch of salt, add the linguine and simmer for 3 minutes.

Beat the eggs and add salt and black pepper and then the parmesan. Beat together.

When cooked, drain the linguine and add the fried bacon. Toss over a low heat until well mixed. Turn off the heat and add the beaten eggs. Mix thoroughly and serve with the grated parmesan.

recipes.Title: Rum Baba
recipes.Ingredients:
For the starter:
    100ml milk, at blood temperature
    7g yeast
    1 tsp sugar
    100g plain flour
For the dough:
    100ml milk
    80g sugar
    300g plain flour
    1 egg, lightly beaten
    90g butter, softened
    50g dried apricots, chopped
    zest of 1 orange
For the rum syrup:
    100ml water
    100g sugar
    4 tbsp rum
For the icing:
    250g icing sugar
    juice of ½ lemon
recipes.Preparation:
First make the poolish. Mix the milk with the yeast and sugar in a large bowl, add the flour and leave it overnight somewhere cool.

The next day, mix the poolish with the milk, sugar and flour. You will end up with a sticky dough.

Add the egg and butter with your hands, then add the apricots and orange zest.
Leave the dough to rise, covered, for 1½-2 hours until doubled in size.

Work the dough a little over a well-floured surface and divide it into eight pieces.
Shape them into balls and put them into eight empty 400g tins or equivalent cake tins. Leave to prove for another hour.

Preheat the oven to 180C/gas mark 4. Bake the cakes for  35-40 minutes.

For the rum syrup, heat the water and sugar gently until the sugar dissolves, then boil for five minutes to turn it into a syrup.
Add the alcohol, cook it off for a minute or so then remove from the heat and let it cool slightly.

When the babas are ready, ease them out of their tins. Pierce their tops with a skewer and pour over the rum syrup.
For the icing, mix the icing sugar with the lemon juice and drizzle over the babas.

Serve with custard and, if you like, stewed rhubarb.

recipes.Title: Chicken Marbella
recipes.Ingredients:
120ml olive oil
120ml red wine vinegar
220g pitted prunes
85g pitted Spanish green olives
60g capers, with a bit of juice
6 bay leaves
1 head of garlic, minced
2 tbsp dried oregano
salt and ground black pepper
4.5kg quartered chickens pieces
220g packed brown sugar
240ml dry white wine
2 tbsp flat-leaf parsley or fresh cilantro, finely chopped
recipes.Preparation:
In a large bowl, combine the olive oil, vinegar, prunes, olives, capers and a splash of the juice, the bay leaves, garlic, oregano and a hefty pinch each of salt and pepper. Add the chicken and stir to coat. Cover the bowl and refrigerate overnight.

When ready to cook, heat the oven to 180°C (Gas mark4).

Arrange the chicken in a single layer in 1 or 2 large, shallow baking pans. Spoon the marinade evenly over the chicken. Sprinkle the chicken pieces with the brown sugar and pour the white wine around them. Bake, basting frequently with the pan juices for 50 minutes to 1 hour.

With a slotted spoon, transfer the chicken, prunes, olives and capers to a serving platter. Moisten with a few spoons of the pan juices and sprinkle generously with the parsley or cilantro. Serve the remaining pan juices on the side.

recipes.Title: Garlic Parmesan Roasted Potatoes
recipes.Ingredients:
1 large sweet potato
1 large yellow potato
1 medium red onion
2 tablespoons olive oil
2 tablespoons unsalted butter
5 cloves garlic, minced
1 teaspoon dried thyme
1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
1/2 teaspoon dried basil
1/3 cup freshly grated Parmesan
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
2 tablespoons chopped parsley leaves
recipes.Preparation:
1. Preheat your oven to 425°F (210°C). Rinse and cut potatoes in 1/4-inch slices. Proceed same way with onion. Line up potatoes and onion alternately in a greased baking pan.

2. In a bowl, combine melted butter, olive oil, herbs, salt, pepper, parmesan and minced garlic. Brush the mixture generously over the potato and onion rows. Transfer to the oven and bake for 1 hour, until fork tender and a bit crispy on the edges. Serve hot, with a sprinkle of fresh parsley and additional parmesan on top.

recipes.Title: Cauliflower and Pancetta Macaroni Cheese
recipes.Ingredients:
1 large cauliflower, cut into florets
150g macaroni
150g pancetta, diced
3 tbsp butter
4 tbsp plain flour
600ml whole milk
1 bay leaf
50g parmesan, grated
100g mature cheddar, grated
A pinch of fresh nutmeg, grated
1 tbsp dijon mustard
1 large pinch cayenne pepper
75ml double cream
salt and black pepper to taste
recipes.Preparation:
Cook the cauliflower in salted water for 6-8 minutes until tender - set aside.
Use the same water to cook the macaroni until al dente, drain and set aside.
Fry the pancetta until crispy; remove and add to the cauliflower and pasta.
Melt the butter, add the flour and then slowly add the milk with heating until a smooth white bechamel has been made. Add the bay leaf and simmer for about 10 minutes until thick and smooth.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (gas mark 6). Mix the cheeses and add all but a handful to the bechamel to make a cheese sauce. Add the nutmeg, mustard, pepper and cream then taste and season as required. Pour all into a 1.5 - 2 litre gratin dish and scatter the remaining chees over the top. Bake for 20 - 25 minutes until golden brown.

recipes.Title: Pork, Garlic and Sriracha Stir-Fry
recipes.Ingredients:
450g ground pork
1 tbsp oil
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 onion, sliced
1 aubergine, cut into half moons
1 red capsicum, cut into strips
225g green beans, cut into 10cm pieces
60ml soy sauce
2 tbsp packed brown sugar
4 tsp sriracha (chili sauce)
8 tbsp chopped cilantro
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oil in a wok and add the onion and garlic. Saute until softened (about 4 minutes) and add the meat. Fry until browning and then add the capsicum and aubergine, Fry for 2 - 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a small bowl combine soy sauce, brown sugar and Sriracha; add to the wok with the green beans. Sauté until green beans are bright green.

Top with cilantro and serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Coconut Curry Ramen
recipes.Ingredients:
2 tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 small yellow onion, chopped
Salt
Freshly ground black pepper
1 x 400ml can chick peas, rinsed and drained
1 medium red capsicum, cut into 1/2in pieces
240ml sugar snap peas, cut into 1/2in pieces
100g ramen noodles
1 litre vegetable stock
1 x 400ml can full-fat coconut milk, shaken well
2 tbsp. red curry paste
8 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro
recipes.Preparation:
In a large pot over medium-low heat, combine olive oil, garlic, and onion; season with 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the chick peas, capsicum, sugar snap peas, and noodles; cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the stock, coconut milk, and curry paste and stir until combined. Bring to boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve immediately.
recipes.Keywords: coconut, onion, chickpeas, sugar snap peas, noodles, spicy

recipes.Title: Salmon Burritos
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 teaspoon lime juice
2 cloves garlic, peeled and minced
1½ teaspoons ground dried chiles
1½ teaspoons salt
2 small salmon fillets
1 sweet potato, peeled, quartered lengthwise, then sliced 1/4 inch thick
4 tbsp guacamole
1 red onion, peeled, halved lengthwise, and cut into 1/4-inch-thick wedges
1 fresh poblano chile, stemmed, seeded, and chopped
4 wheat flour tortillas (10 in. wide), warmed
Chopped cilantro, shredded lettuce, sour cream, and lime wedges
recipes.Preparation:
Make the guacamole from a small avocado.

Preheat oven to 220°C Gas 7. Line a baking pan with aluminum foil.

Whisk together the olive oil, lime juice, garlic, ground dried chillies, and salt.

Rinse salmon and pat dry. Brush flesh side of salmon with 2 tablespoons of the lime-chile marinade. Set aside.

Toss the sweet potato, onion, and chile in a bowl with the remaining marinade. Arrange vegetables in a single layer on the baking pans.

Roast vegetables for 10 minutes, then add salmon, skin side down, to one pan and return to oven. Continue roasting until potatoes are tender when pierced and salmon is opaque but still moist-looking in center of thickest part, 7 to 10 minutes.

Remove skin from salmon and slice fillet into six equal portions.

Spoon vegetable mixture equally onto warm tortillas. Top each with a piece of salmon and a little cilantro, cabbage, guacamole, and sour cream. Fold tortilla over the filling. Serve with more sour cream and the lime wedges.

recipes.Title: Sticky plum pork
recipes.Ingredients:
2 tbsp sunflower oil
500g pork fillet, cut into 12 slices
180g  plum  sauce
180g hoisin sauce
4 star anise
Red chilli, seeded and finely chopped
40g ginger, peeled and finely chopped
1 tbsp sesame oil
6 spring onions, diagonally sliced
1 x 250g pack pak choi, leaves separated
2 tbsp light soy sauce
Rice, fried with egg
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the pork, in batches, on both sides, until golden.
Return all of the pork to the pan with the stir-fry sauce, star anise, chilli and two thirds of the ginger. Simmer for 4-5 minutes, until the pork is cooked through and the sauce is piping hot.
Meanwhile, heat the sesame oil in a wok and stir-fry the spring onions, pak choi and the remaining ginger for 2 minutes. Add the soy sauce and cook for 30 seconds.
Serve with egg fried rice.

recipes.Title: Asparagus wrapped in pastry with balsamic dipping sauce
recipes.Ingredients:
Short crust pastry with cheese 
Flour for work surface
150g grated Parmesan
16 asparagus spears 
1 tbsp  salt 
180ml balsamic vinegar
1 tbsp. sugar  
1 bay leaf
¼ tsp dried thyme
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to gas mark 6 (200°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper and set aside.

Meanwhile, roll out on a lightly floured surface and cut cheesy pastry to create 16 rectangles of  60 x 150  mm. Sprinkle each strip with 1/2 tablespoon Parmesan, turn over and center an asparagus spear atop the strip. Wrap strips to enclose asparagus; dampen edges of pastry with water and seal to close. Place pastry-wrapped asparagus seam side down on prepared baking pans, spacing appetizers about 2 inches apart.

Lightly brush tops of pastry-wrapped asparagus with water and sprinkle each with a pinch of salt. Bake until golden brown, 15 to 18 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a small pan over medium-high heat, bring vinegar, sugar, bay leaf, and thyme to a gentle boil and cook until liquid is reduced to 1/2 cup, 12 to 15 minutes. Strain, reserving sauce and discarding herbs. 

Serve asparagus warm with balsamic dipping sauce.

recipes.Title: Asparagus and bacon tart
recipes.Ingredients:
1 sheet puff pastry
2 eggs, divided
1 tbsp whipping cream
flour, for sprinkling
4 slices bacon, chopped into lardons
24 asparagus spears, washed and trimmed
150g ricotta
150g parmesan, grated
300g freshly grated gruyère, emmental or fontina cheese
2 tbsp Chopped chives
Freshly ground black pepper
Salt
Extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to gas mark 6 (200°C). Line a baking sheet  with baking paper. Mix together 1 egg and whipping cream to make egg wash. Set aside.

Roll out pastry on lightly floured surface to make a slightly larger rectangle. Using a sharp paring knife, gently score a 20mm border, carefully cutting halfway through pastry. Using a fork, gently prick center area all over. This will prevent the middle from rising out of control. Brush border lightly with egg wash and bake 10 minutes. Transfer to cooling rack and let cool slightly. Reserve egg wash.

Meanwhile, heat a large pan over medium heat. Add bacon and cook until crispy. Remove bacon and drain, and reserve about 2 tablespoons of the bacon fat. Add the asparagus to pan and cook until crisp-tender, about 3 minutes. (The asparagus will cook more in the oven).

In a medium mixing bowl, combine ricotta, parmesan, gruyère, chives, remaining egg, remaining egg wash, and black pepper. Spread cheese mixture evenly across center of puff pastry, leaving 20mm border. Evenly arrange asparagus across center of pastry. Lightly drizzle asparagus with olive oil and bake until pastry is golden brown and asparagus is fork tender, 25 minutes.

Sprinkle with coarsely ground salt and serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Asparagus and chive tart
recipes.Ingredients:
1 sheet frozen puff pastry, thawed in refrigerator overnight
Plain flour, for rolling out pastry
1 egg, beaten with 1 tbsp.  whipping cream
300g freshly grated Parmesan
300g freshly grated gruyère, emmental or fontina
2 tbsp. freshly chopped chives
2 large eggs
1 tbsp. whipping cream
½ tsp. Freshly ground black pepper
Extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling
24 asparagus spears, washed and trimmed
Salt
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to gas mark 6 (200°C) and line a baking sheet with baking paper. Roll out pastry on lightly floured surface to make a 250 x 400mm rectangle. Using a sharp paring knife, gently score a 20mm border, carefully cutting halfway through pastry. Using a fork, gently prick center area all over, every 25mm, then brush border lightly with egg wash and bake 10 minutes. Transfer to cooling rack and let cool slightly.

Meanwhile, in a medium mixing bowl combine Parmesan, fontina, chives, eggs, whipping cream and pepper. Spread cheese mixture evenly across center of puff pastry, leaving a 20mm border. Evenly arrange asparagus across center of pastry, alternating direction and avoiding the border.

Lightly drizzle asparagus with olive oil and bake until pastry is golden brown and asparagus is fork tender, 25 minutes.

Sprinkle with coarsly ground salt and serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Chicken Paprikash
recipes.Ingredients:
1 large chicken, jointed (or use 2 large chicken legs and 2 breasts, halved)
salt
2 tbsp olive oil
knob butter
2 onions, chopped
4-6 cloves garlic, chopped
2 tbsp sweet paprika powder
1 tbsp hot paprika powder
1 tbsp smoked paprika
1 tbsp flour
285ml chicken stock
3 tbsp chopped fresh flatleaf parsley
4 red peppers, seeds removed and cut into 1cm/0.5in strips
4 large ripe tomatoes, roughly chopped
250ml soured cream
Black pepper to season

Dumplings:
250g flour
1 tsp salt
black pepper
1 tbsp baking powder
1 egg, beaten
2 tbsp melted butter
235ml full-fat milk
recipes.Preparation:
Rub the chicken pieces with salt. Heat the oil and butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan and brown the chicken all over for a few minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set to one side.
To the same pan, add the onions and garlic and sweat for about 5 minutes. Add the paprika, then the flour, and stir until combined - take care not to burn it.
Add the stock and stir. Return the chicken pieces to the pan, adding a bit more stock if the mixtures seems too dry. Add half of the parsley and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes and simmer gently for about 30 mins. Add the red pepper strips bring to the boil again and continue to simmer for another 30 mins.
Meanwhile, mix together the flour, salt, black pepper and baking powder in a bowl.
In another bowl, mix the egg with melted butter; add to the dry ingredients with enough milk to make a semi-stiff batter (do not over-mix,). Drop teaspoonfuls into simmering chicken stock. Cook covered for about 18-20 minutes with no opening for the first 10 minutes.
When the paprikash is finished, stir in the sour cream and the remaining parsley. Check the seasoning, add the dumplings, remove the pan from the heat and serve.

recipes.Title: Risotto frutti di mare
recipes.Ingredients:
8 prawns, shell off
Bag  of mussels
4 Scallops

For the stock
25ml olive oil
1 garlic clove, chopped
¼ red chilli, chopped
1 tomato, chopped
1 Shallot
¼ tsp saffron
900ml fish stock
cooking liquor from the mussels

For the risotto
50g unsalted butter
2 shallots, chopped
1 garlic clove, chopped
350g risotto rice e.g. Arborio
120ml dry white wine
1 tbsp olive oil
recipes.Preparation:
Peel the prawns, reserving the shells for the stock. Set the prawns aside until needed. Wash the mussels, scrape them clean and pull out the beards. Open by placing in a pan with a splash of water, covering tightly then setting over a high heat until they have opened. Strain through a colander to remove any grit. Save the liquor for the stock. Remove the meats from all but 8 of the shells, discard the empty shells. Leaving a few whole mussels in the risotto makes it look very appetizing. Set the mussels aside until needed.
To make the stock, heat the oil in a large pan and add the garlic, onion and chilli. Fry for 5 minutes without colouring. Add the reserved prawn shells and cook for another couple of minutes then add the tomato, saffron, fish stock and mussel liquor. Bring to the boil and simmer for 30 minutes then push through a conical sieve with the back of a ladle to extract as much flavour as possible.
To make the risotto, melt the butter in a heavy-based pan (this will lessen the chance of the risotto burning on the bottom as it cooks) then add the shallots and garlic and sweat until softened. Add the rice and stir for a couple of minutes until well-coated with butter. Pour in the wine. Bring to the boil then remove from the heat and let the rice absorb all the liquid. You can make the risotto to this stage some time before completing the dish. The final cooking time, about 20 minutes, is reduced to about 10 by doing this.
Return the pan to a medium heat and add the shellfish stock to the rice in three stages, allowing the liquid to be absorbed each time before adding the next amount. Stir continuously until the stock is almost completely absorbed.
While the risotto is cooking, brush the rest of the seafood with olive oil and grill for 3-4 minutes. When the rice is just tender but still firm to the bite (al dente),  carefully mix the seafood including the mussels into the risotto.

recipes.Title: Seafood, lobster thermidor
recipes.Ingredients:
3 tbsp butter
2 shallots, finely sliced
small bunch of tarragon + 5 extra sprigs
300ml fresh fish stock1 tbsp plain flour
150ml whole milk
3 tbsp
double cream
2 egg yolks
½ nutmeg, grated
2 tbsp English mustard
2 lobsters
4 tbsp brandy
50g gruyere cheese, grated
recipes.Preparation:
1. Heat 1 tbsp butter in a saucepan. Once foaming,add shllots and the bunch of tarragon; fry over a medium heat for 3-4 minutes until starting to soften. Pour in the stock and boil for 10-12 minutes, until reduced to 2-3 tbsp.
2. Meanwhile, make the white sauce. Heat 1 tbsp butter in a pan over a medium heat and, once foaming, stir in the flour. Cook for 1-2 minutes until slightly golden. Remove from the heat and gradually add the milk, stirring after each addition until smooth. Return to a low/medium heat, stirring, for 5-7 minutes until a thick sauce.
3. Strain the reduced fish stock into the sauce, add the cream and season. Cook for 3-4 minutes more, stirring until thickened again. Transfer to a bowl, cool for a few minutes, them stir in the egg yolks, nutmeg and mustard. Cover the surface with clingfilm and set aside.
4. Prepare the lobsters and chop the claw and tail meat. Heat the final 1 tbsp butter in a frying pan set over a high heat. Once foaming, stir in the lobster meat, any juices and the roe. Fry for a few minutes then splash in the brandy and boil or flambé until the alcohol has evaporated. Set aside to cool for a few minutes.Pick and chop the leaves from the six tarragon sprigs, then stir into the white sauce with the lobster.
5. Divide the mixture between the lobster shells and place on a baking tray (cover with cling film and chill if making ahead, up to 24 hours in advance). To serve, preheat the grill to high and scatter the cheese over the prepared lobsters. Grill for about 4-5 minutes, until piping hot and golden.

recipes.Title: Pork fillet stuffed with caramelised shallots
recipes.Ingredients:
Olive oil
3 large or 6 small shallots, trimmed and peeled
2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
Golden caster sugar
Balsamic vinegar
8 leaves basil, chopped
800g Pork fillet, trimmed
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C, gas 6). Put a little olive oil in a small oven-proof pan and add the shallots, roll them around and roast them with the lid on until they are tender enough to squash flat (about 60 minutes). Sprinkle on a little sugar and some balsamic vinegar, then add the chopped sage and season well.

Cut down the centre of the pork fillets to make a deep pocket, being careful not to cut all the way through. Scatter the sliced garlic and basil onto the fillet and season with black pepper. Push the shallots into the pocket all the way along and then rub the outside of the pork with olive oil and season well. Tie the pork along its length to keep it together. Heat a little oil in a frying pan and brown the pork all over. Transfer to a roasting tin and cook for 25 minutes, or until a skewer poked into the centre comes out feeling hot. Leave to rest for 10 minutes.

Slice the pork and serve with new potatoes and a green vegetable.

recipes.Title: Chocolate mousse
recipes.Ingredients:
150g dark chocolate, 72% cocoa, broken into small pieces
25g butter
5 eggs, separated
3 tbsp caster sugar
recipes.Preparation:
1. Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl set over a pan of simmering water, stirring occasionally (or melt in a microwave oven). Set aside to cool slightly,
2. Place the egg yolks and 1 tbsp sugar in a clean bowl, set over a pan of simmering water. Using an electric beater, whisk for 3-4 minutes until pale and thickened. Remove from the heat and stir the chocolate through the yolks.
3. In a separate, clean bowl, with clean beater, whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks with a pinch of salt. Beat in the remaining 2 tbsp sugar until stiff and glossy. Fold1/3 through the chocolate and yolk mixture to loosen, then carefully fold in the remaining egg white 1/3 at a time, trying to retain as much air as possible. Spoon into 4 glasses or ramekins (about 175ml capacity) and chill for at least 4 hours until set.

recipes.Title: Blackberry souffle
recipes.Ingredients:
Butter, for greasing
3 tbsp golden caster sugar + extra to dust
150g blackberries
Few drops of vanilla extract
Few drops of lemon juice
½ tbsp cornflour
2 egg whites
icing sugar to dust
recipes.Preparation:
1. Preheat the oven to 180°C (gas 4) and put a baking shetet on the top shelf of the oven. Grease two large ramekins (200ml volume) and dust with sugar.
2. Put the berries and 1 tbsp sugar in a small pan and simmer for 5-6 minutes until the fruit has broken up (help it by crushing with a wooden spoon). Whizz this in a blender then sieve into a mixing bowl discarding the pips. Cool slightly then stir in the vanilla extract and lemon juice. Put 1 tbsp purée into each ramekin. Mix the cornflour with ½ tbsp water then stir into the remaining purée. Set aside.
3. Put the egg whites into a bowl and whisk first at slow speed, then medium speed. When the whites reach soft peaks, scatter over the remaining 2 tbsp sugar. Whisk until dense and silky.
4. Fold 1/3rd of the egg white into the purée then gently fold in the remainder until combined; take care not to over-mix. Divide the mixture between the ramekins, filling to the top. Smoothe the surface with a knife and clean the edges with your thumb wrapped in a piece of kitchen paper, making a slight indentation around the edge. Cook on a baking sheet for 10 minutes until well risen. Dust with icing sugar and serve at once, with creme fraiche if liked.

recipes.Title: Chocolate fondant
recipes.Ingredients:
50g butter + extra for greasing
1 tbsp cocoa powder, sieved for dusting
50g dark chocolate (70% cocoa solids), chopped into small chunks
1 egg + 1 yolk
25g caster sugar
1 heaped tbsp plain flour
recipes.Preparation:
1. Preheat the oven to 200°C (gas 6). Grease 2 x 150ml dariole moulds, add the cocoa powder to one, then transfer to the other, turning as you go until the moulds are evenly coated. Discard the exces cocoa powder.
2. Melt the chocolate and butter together with a pinch of salt in a bowl set over a pan of simmering water (or in a microwave oven in short bursts). Stir to combine and set aside to briefly cool.
3. Whisk together the egg, egg yolk and sugar until tripled in volume; it should hold a trail for 2-3 seconds. Sift over the flour and gently fold in. Loosen the melted chocolate with a little of the egg mixture, then, in two batches, carefully fold in the remainder. Divide the mixture between the moulds, cleaning the edges with kitchen paper as necessary.
4. Bake for 10 minutes until risen and a crust has formed on top; they should still have a slight wobble. Turn out onto heated plates and serve at once, dusted with cocoa powder.

recipes.Title: Chicken liver parfait
recipes.Ingredients:
200g chicken livers, trimmed and cut into 2cm pieces
60g butter cut into 15g pieces
1 shallot, finely chopped
2 sage leaves, shredded
½tsp pink peppercorns, crushed
1 pinch ground allspice
50ml sherry
2tbsp double cream
½tsp lemon juice
½tsp caster sugar

Clarified butter
75g butter
1tsp pink peppercorns, crushed
recipes.Preparation:
1. Pat the chicken livers dry and season. Put 15g butter in a frying pan over a medium heat then sear the livers for 3 minutes on one side and 1 minute on the other. Toss occasionally for another 3 minutes until cooked through.Set aside on a plate.
2. Put 15g butter into a pan over a medium heat. Add the shallot and sage, season and fry gently for 5 minutes, until starting to caramelise. Add the peppercorns and allspice and sauté for 1 minute. Pour in the sherry and simmer until reduced by half, then stir in the cream, lemon juice and sugar. Return the liver and any juices to the pan, stirring everything togetyher, then remove from the heat and set aside to cool for 15 minutes.
3. whizz in a blender with 30g butter until smooth. Add more salt, pepper, lemon juice and sugar to taste. Pass through a fine sieve, spoon into ramekins and smooth the tops.
4. For the clarified butter , warm the butter gently in a pan. Once melted, the milk solids should sink to the bottom. Skim off any scum. Pour a spoonful of the clear butter over each of the parfaits, sprinkle with crushed peppercorns, then top each with another spoonfiul of butter. Cool to room temperature and then chill. Store in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.Title: Leek fondue linguine
recipes.Ingredients:
4 large leeks, shredded
50g butter
60ml white wine
6tbsp creme fraiche
400g linguine
parmesan shavings for the topping
½ lemon
recipes.Preparation:
Melt the butter in a pan and add the leeks; cook very gently for about 5 minutes adding the wine. Add the creme fraiche and cook for another 15 minutes or until the leeks are meltingly soft. Season well.
Cook the pasta and toss it with the leek fondue. divide it between four bowls and add a handful of parmesan shavings and a squeeze of lemon juice.

recipes.Title: Tart tatin
recipes.Ingredients:
5-7 eating apples (mix of sweet and sharp)
175g golden granulated sugar
50g butter, cut into cubes
325g all butter puff pastry, ready rolled sheet
recipes.Preparation:
1. Heat the oven to 190° (gas 5). Cut the apples in half, peel and core and set aside.
2. Put the sugar and 100ml of water in a 20cm oven-proof frying pan and stir with a wooden spoon. Put the pan over a medium heat and cook, without stirring, until the syrup caramelises to a deep golden brown. Remove from the heat. Add a pinch of salt and the butter and carefully tilt the pan back and forth to mix it in.
3. Arrange the apples, rounded side down, in the pan, nestling them as close together as you can, cutting some into quarters or smaller chunks to fill in the gaps. Lay the pastry sheet over the top of the pan and use a knife to cut a circle that is just a bit bigger than the pan. Fold the edges of the pastry inside the pan 9use the handle of a table knife, not your fingers) around the apples. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown.
4. When the tart comes out of the oven, leave for a minute, then cover the pan with a plate (and your hands with an oven cloth as some hot caramel will leak out) and carefully flip the tart out onto a plate. You might need to scrape some caramel out of the pan over the apples. Be careful with the pan handle too as it will still. be hot from the oven.

Serve with vamilla ice cream.

recipes.Title: Chocolate and amaretto mousse
recipes.Ingredients:
170g 70% cocoa dark chocolate
4 eggs, separated
150ml amaretto
1 orange, zested +2 tbsp juice
200g mascarpone
20g flaked almonds, toasted
recipes.Preparation:
1. Melt the chocolate in a heat-proof bowl over a pan of simmering water. Cool it a little. Whisk the egg whites in a bowl until they reach soft peaks. Pour the amaretto into the cooled melted cholate, add the egg yolks and whisk.
2. Add a large tbsp of egg white to the chocolate mix and stir thoroughly. Slowly add the remaining egg white in two batches, folding carefully into the mix with a large metal spoon (to make sure that you don't lose any of the air bubbles).
3. Divide the mixture between 4 martini glasses or tumblers and chill for at least 6 hours.
4. Beat the orange zest and juice into the mascarpone and spoon over the chilled mousse. Sprinkle the tasted almonds over to serve.

recipes.Title: Pea and parmesan soufflé
recipes.Ingredients:
1tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 small leek, trimmed and thinly sliced
salt and pepper
180g peas
310ml milk
50g butter + extra for brushing
50g plain flour
140g parmesan, grated + extra to serve
4 eggs, separated
recipes.Preparation:
1. Preheat the oven to 180°C (gas 4). Heat the oil in a medium pan over medium heat. Add the leek, season and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes, or until softened. Add the peas and milk, bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and, using a hand-held blender, beat until smooth, then set aside.
2. Melt the butter in a medium pan over a medium heat. Add the flouir and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes. Reduce the heat and gradually add the pea mixture, whisking to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes or until extremely thick. Transfer to a large bowl and set aside.
3. Brush 4 x 250ml ramekins with the extra melted butter and sprinkle with 20g of parmesan. Add the egg yolks and the remaining parmesan to the pea mixture and mix well. Place the egg whites in a large bowl and using a hand mixer, whisk until soft peaks form.In three batches, carefully fold the egg whites into the pea mixture.
4. Divide the soufflé mixture between the ramekins. Run your finger around the inner edge of each ramekin ½cm deep. Place the ramekinns on a baking tray and bake for 25 minutes, or until puffed and golden. Sprinkle with the extra parmesan and serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Triple chocolate cookies
recipes.Ingredients:
100g dark chocolate, chopped
200g butter, at room temperature
100g caster sugar
2 eggs
275g plain flour
1tsp baking powder
35g cocoa powder
100g white chocolate, chopped
140g milk chocolate, chopped
recipes.Preparation:
1. Preheat the oven to 200°C (gas 6) and line two baking sheets with non-stick baing paper. Melt the dark chocolate in a bowl over a pan of simmering water (or in a microwave). Set aside to cool slightly.
2. Beat the butter and sugar in a bowl with a whisk until pale and creamy. Gradually beat in the eggs, one at a time, then whisk in the cooled melted plain chocolate.
3. Mix the flour, baking powder and cocoa with a pinch of salt, then sift over the cookie mix.Fold in gently along with the white chocolate and 80g of the milk chocolate.
4. Use two spoons to divide the mixture equally into 18 golf ball sized pieces and place on the baking sheets 4cm apart.
5. Bake for 15 minutes or until firm but still soft in the centre. Remove from the oven and leave to cool for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool a little more.
6. Meanwhile, melt the remaining milk chocolate and drizzle over the cookies with a teaspoon. Leave to set, then serve either warm or cold.

recipes.Title: Merthyr Pie
recipes.Ingredients:
1kg Beef shin, off the bone or
1.5kg on the bone
2 medium carrots, halved
1 medium onion, quartered
2 celery sticks, halved
1 small garlic bulb, halved
3 fresh bay leaves
1 fresh thyme sprig

For the bread and cheese layers:
150g beef dripping
8 thick slices of good bread, preferably sourdough
3-4tbsp dijon or English mustard
150g cheddar cheese, grated
recipes.Preparation:
1. Heat the oven to 140°C (gas 1). Put the beef shin in a lidded oven-proof casserole with the vegetables and herbs.
