Cut in half crosswise and serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Avocado with crab
recipes.Ingredients:
350 g crab meat
95 g Greek yogurt
½ red onion, crushed
2 tbsp. Chopped chives
3 tbsp. lemon juice
½ tsp. cayenne pepper
Salt
50 g grated cheddar
50g parmesan
2 avocados, halved and pitted
4 large prawns
recipes.Preparation:
In a medium bowl, stir together lump crab meat, yogurt, red onion, chives, lemon juice, and cayenne and season with salt.
Scoop out avocados to create bowls. Dice scooped out avocado and fold into crab mixture.
Preheat grill. Fill avocado bowls with crab mixture and top with the cheeses. Briefely fry the 4 prawns in butter until just pink. Grill the avocados until cheese is just melted, about 1 minute. Decorate each avocado with a prawn and some more lengths of chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Avocado egg boats
recipes.Ingredients:
2 ripe avocados, halved and pitted
4 large eggs
Salt
Freshly ground black pepper
3 slices bacon
Freshly chopped chives, for garnish
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to 180°C (160ºC fan). Scoop about 1 tablespoon worth of avocado out of each half; discard or reserve for another use.
Place hollowed avocados in a baking dish, then crack eggs into a bowl, one at a time. Using a spoon, transfer one yolk to each avocado half, then spoon in as much egg white as you can fit without spilling over.
Season with salt and pepper and bake until whites are just set and yolks are still runny, 10 to 15 minutes. (Cover with foil if avocados are beginning to brown.)
Meanwhile, in a large pan over medium heat, cook bacon until crisp, 8 minutes, then transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and chop.
Top avocados with bacon and chives before serving.

recipes.Title: Crab ravioli
recipes.Ingredients:
150g pasta dough
For the filling
100 g fresh white crabmeat
finely grated zest 1 lemon
1 tbsp. chopped fresh parsley
2 tbsp. crème fraiche
For the sauce
100 g butter
4  basil leaves, roughly chopped
Juice of ½ lemon
recipes.Preparation:
To make the filling, combine all the ingredients in a bowl. Cover and chill.

Take half the pasta dough and knead a few times to develop elasticity. Dust with a little flour and shape into a rough rectangle. Roll out pasta by hand or feed it through thickest setting of a pasta machine a few times, folding and turning dough after each feed to smooth edges. Continue feeding through machine, narrowing setting after each rolling – make sure to support pasta as it gets  thinner to prevent ripping. Stop when dough is thin enough to see your hand through it. Lay pasta sheet on baking parchment and cover with clingfilm while you repeat process with  remaining dough.

To shape ravioli, divide filling into six mounds, spacing evenly along length of first pasta  sheet. Brush around outsides of filling with water, then carefully lay second sheet over the  filling. Press around filling to seal (try to remove any air bubbles). Use a 9cm (31/2in) heart cutter to stamp out ravioli around the filling mounds. Press the ravioli edges with tines of a fork for a frilly effect. Place in a roasting tin lined with baking parchment.

To serve, bring a large pan of water to the boil. Carefully add ravioli to boiling water and  simmer for 2-3min until pasta is tender. Meanwhile, heat butter and basil in a medium  frying pan until butter is just starting to turn golden brown. Remove from heat, stir in lemon  juice (it will splutter). Drain pasta and serve immediately drizzled with butter sauce.

recipes.Title: Thai green prawn noodles
recipes.Ingredients:
2 tsp. vegetable oil
2 echalion shallots, thinly sliced into rings
4 tbsp Thai green curry paste
500 ml vegetable stock
160 ml tin coconut cream
300 g mixed stir-fry vegetables
150 g mixed/exotic mushrooms, torn if large
300 g ready-to-wok/fresh flat or udon noodles
Juice 1 lime, plus wedges to serve
For the prawn dumplings
300 g raw, peeled, king prawns
1 tbsp. cornflour
1 tbsp. sweet chilli sauce
1 spring onion, finely chopped
2 fresh kaffir lime leaves (1 double leaf), central stalk removed
2 tbsp. vegetable oil, plus extra to grease
recipes.Preparation:
First make the prawn dumplings. Put the prawns, cornflour, sweet chilli sauce and ½tsp fine salt into a food processor and pulse to a rough paste. Add the spring onion and lime leaves and pulse briefly to combine. Chill for 30min to firm up.
Lightly grease your hands and a plate. Use a tablespoon measure to scoop out portions of the prawn mixture and gently roll it all into balls. Place on the plate and chill until needed.
For the curry, heat the oil in a large wok or pan (that has a lid) over low heat. Add shallots and cook for 3-4min, until softened. Add the curry paste, fry for 30sec until aromatic, then stir in the stock and coconut cream. Add the vegetables, turn up the heat and bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and remove from heat.
For the prawn dumplings, heat the oil in a frying pan over low-medium heat. Add the dumplings and fry for 3-4min, turning gently, until just pink and opaque. Add the mushrooms and fry for 3min, until tender.
Stir noodles into the vegetable curry pan, gently separating them. Add the dumplings and mushrooms, return curry pan to medium heat and bubble for 5min until piping hot. Season with lime juice and salt, if needed, and serve in bowls with lime wedges for squeezing over.

recipes.Title: Sicilian pasta
recipes.Ingredients:
1 medium onion
4 cloves garlic
2 tablespoons olive oil from the anchovy tin
½ teaspoon soft light brown sugar
12 anchovies (canned in olive oil)
7g butter
tiniest pinch of ground cloves
Pata cooking water
200 grams linguine or spaghetti
1 bunch freshly chopped flatleaf parsley
recipes.Preparation:
Finely chop the onions and garlic.
Heat the oil in a heavy-based pan and cook the very finely chopped onion and garlic over a low heat until you have a soft, golden mush - about 20 minutes. Add the brown sugar, stir it in and let the onion mixture cook for another minute or so.
Remove the anchovies from the tin, and chop them very finely. Add them to the onion mush, stirring until they begin to melt, then stir in the butter and the pinch of ground cloves, followed by a tablespoonful of pasta cooking water and when all is combined, gradually stir in more cooking water. When this has come together as a puree, take the pan off the heat.

Tip the drained pasta into the anchovy and onion sauce.  Add some oil from the anchovy tin if you need it too. 
Sprinkle over most of the parsley, just roughly chopped, thoroughly turning the pasta in the pan to coat each strand in the anchovy sauce. Remove to a warm bowl, sprinkle over the remaining parsley and take to the table.

recipes.Title: Black pepper beef
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp whole black peppercorns
300 g beef fillet, sliced
1 small onion, cut into strips
1 green pepper, cut into strips
2 tbsp oyster sauce
2 tbsp oil
2 tbsp light soy sauce
1 tsp sugar
0.5 tsp salt
recipes.Preparation:
Coarsely grind the peppercorns in a pestle and mortar – not too fine, but you also don’t want to be crunching down on any whole peppercorns either.
Place a wok over a medium-high heat and add 1 tablespoon of the oil. Once smoking, add the beef and fry for 90 seconds to seal each piece. Transfer to a plate and set to one side.
Add the remaining oil to the wok and fry the onion and pepper strips for 2 minutes.
Once the onion is translucent, add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, ground peppercorns and salt, along with 3 tablespoons of water.
Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 3 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the cooked beef and serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Pork chow mein
recipes.Ingredients:
200g wheat soba noodles, soaked in hot water
300g pork loin / pork fillet, cut into matchsticks
2 carrot, cut into matchsticks
1 yellow pepper, cut into matchsticks
1 green pepper, cut into matchsticks
2 spring onion, sliced
200g red cabbage, shredded
200g beansprouts
100g watercress
1 tbsp vegetable oil
Dash of Sesame Oil
Pinch of salt and pepper to taste

Marinade:
2 tsp Oyster Sauce

Sauce Mix:
100ml chicken stock
2 tbsp Oyster Sauce
1 tbsp Dark Soy Sauce
recipes.Preparation:
Marinade the pork for 30 minutes.

Turn wok onto high heat and add ½ tbsp vegetable oil. Add marinated pork and sear until cooked, then remove. Add another ½ tbsp vegetable oil into wok. Stir-fry vegetables, then add pork, followed by noodles and sauce mix. Stir for 1-2 minutes and serve on a plate.

Place watercress over noodles and flash fry beansprouts for 30 seconds with some salt, pepper and a dash of Sesame Oil. Pour beansprouts over the noodles. Garnish with spring onions.

recipes.Title: Crab Linguine
recipes.Ingredients:
300g dried linguine pasta
250g fresh white  crab meat, picked over for pieces of shell
2 fresh red chillies, deseeded and finely chopped
1 bunch of flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
zest and juice of 1 lemon (zest is optional)
150ml olive oil, for drizzling
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Parmesan, grated for serving
recipes.Preparation:
Bring a pan of salted water to the boil, add the pasta and cook according to the packet. Meanwhile, combine the crab meat in a large bowl with the chilli, parsley, juice and zest, if using. Stir together.
Drain the pasta (reserve some of the cooking water) and add to the crab sauce along with a couple of tablespoons of the pasta cooking water. Use tongs to thoroughly mix the pasta with the crab so that all the pasta gets a good coating of sauce.
Serve in warmed bowls and sprinkle over a generous amount of parmesan, a drizzle of olive oil and a grinding of black pepper. It goes deliciously with a cold glass of Gavi.

recipes.Title: Prawn fettucine
recipes.Ingredients:
175g fresh fettucine
2 tsp olive oil
3 garlic clove, finely sliced
pinch chilli flakes
50ml white wine
2 tbsp  crème fraîche
juice of ½ lemon (or to taste)
150g raw peeled prawns
4 basil leaves, finely chopped
salt 
freshly ground black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Cook the pasta for 2 minutes in salted water. Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan and gently fry the garlic and chilli flakes for 2 mins. Add the prawns and fry until pink. Tip in the wine and bubble over a high heat for 1 min, then lower the heat and stir in the crème fraîche and lemon juice. Season to taste with salt and plenty of black pepper. Simmer for 1 min to reduce a little, then add the basil.

Drain the pasta and tip into the sauce. Use tongs to mix everything together. Divide between 2 shallow bowls.

recipes.Title: Prawn risotto
recipes.Ingredients:
1 large shallot, diced
4 cloves garlic, crushed
350 g arborio rice
salt
1000 ml  chicken stock
360 ml dry white wine
Juice of 2 lemons
2 tbsp. freshly chopped parsley, plus more for garnish
1 tsp. crushed chilli flakes
450 g medium prawns, peeled and deveined
100 g freshly grated Parmesan
2 tbsp butter
recipes.Preparation:
In a large deep-sided pan or pot over medium heat, melt 1 tablespoon butter. Add onion and cook until soft, 5 to 6 minutes, then add 1 clove garlic and cook until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes more. Add rice and stir until combined, then season with salt.
In batches, begin adding stock, 120ml at a time, making sure stock is fully absorbed before adding the next batch. Once broth is done, add 240ml wine and simmer, stirring occasionally until fully absorbed.
Meanwhile, cook prawns: In a large pan over medium heat, melt remaining butter. Add remaining garlic, lemon juice, parsley, and chilli flakes and stir, 2 minutes, then add shrimp and season with salt. Cook prawns until pink, 3 to 4 minutes, then add remaining wine. Bring to a simmer, then add prawn mixture, 1 tbsp. butter and Parmesan to risotto and stir until combined and creamy.
Serve with parsley.

recipes.Title: Prawn and coconut curry
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp. coconut oil, divided
250 g raw King prawns, peeled and deveined
½ onion, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
2 tsp. ground cumin
1 tsp. salt
2 tsp. ground corriander
2 green chillies, finely chopped
25g coconut cream
70g tomato paste
1 x (200g) can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
½ tbsp. cornflour 
1 tbsp. warm water
1 tbsp. chopped fresh coriander 
250 g cooked rice, for serving
recipes.Preparation:
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt 1 tablespoon coconut oil. Add shrimp and cook until pink, 1 to 2 minutes per side, then remove shrimp from pan and set aside. Add remaining tablespoon coconut oil, onion, and chilli. Cook until onions are soft, 4 minutes, then add the garlic.
Stir in cumin, corriander, salt,, then add coconut milk, tomato paste, and chickpeas. Stir until combined and bring to a simmer. Mix cornflour and water together, then stir into skillet. Simmer until thickened, 5 to 6 minutes.
Stir in cooked shrimp and simmer, 2 minutes more. Sprinkle with coriander and serve with rice.
recipes.Keywords: seafood, prawns, chickpeas, coconut, curry, spicy

recipes.Title: Lancashire Hotpot
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp butter
1 tbsp vegetable oil
500g lamb - not too lean - neck is best, but shoulder works well too, cut into bite-size chunks
2 brown onions - peeled and sliced thinly
1 heaped tbsp plain flour - use gluten free plain flour if required
480ml hot chicken or vegetable stock
2 bay leaves
½ tsp salt
½ tsp ground black pepper
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
3 medium sized carrots - peeled and cut into chunks
680g potatoes - peeled and sliced to 2-3mm thick
1 tbsp melted butter for brushing
¼ tsp dried thyme
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Melt the butter and vegetable oil in a medium sized casserole and fry the lamb pan until lightly browned all over (about 3-4 minutes). Spoon the lamb into a bowl, then add the onions to the casserole and cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring regularly, until soft.
Add the lamb back in, then stir in the flour, cooking for a minute. Add in the stock, bay leaves, salt, pepper and Worcestershire sauce. Give everything a stir, bring to a gently bubble. Then place a lid on it and cook in the oven for 30 minutes.

After 30 minutes, stir in the carrots. Top with the sliced potatoes. Start from the outside, and layer the potatoes, moving towards the centre.
Brush the top of the potatoes with the melted butter and sprinkle on the dried thyme. Cover with a lid or foil and place back in the oven for 1 hour.
After an hour, turn the oven up to 200°C and remove the lid. Cook for a further 30 minutes until the potatoes are browned and crisp on top.
Take out of the oven, and leave to rest for 5 minutes or so (it will be very hot), then serve with some green veg.

recipes.Title: Pork Yakisoba
recipes.Ingredients:
450g soba noodles
1 tbsp vegetable oil
450g pork tenderloin or pork belly, cut against the grain in thin strips
1 carrot, cut into julienne strips
1 small onion, cut into julienne strips
1 tbsp freshly grated ginger
3 cloves garlic, minced
¼ head white cabbage, shredded
80ml yakisoba sauce
salt and ground black pepper to taste
2 tbsp pickled red ginger (beni shoga), or to taste
2 tbsp kizami nori (dried flaked aonori seaweed), or to taste
recipes.Preparation:
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook soba in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until noodles are tender yet firm to the bite, 5 to 8 minutes. Drain noodles and rinse with cold water. Set aside.

Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Add pork and stir-fry with a pinch of salt and pepper, about 5 minutes. Transfer meat to a plate, reserving oil in wok. Add carrots, onion, ginger, and garlic to the wok and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes.

Add cabbage to the wok and stir-fry briefly, about 1 minute. Add drained soba noodles. Pour in 1/2 the yakisoba sauce and stir-fry until noodles and vegetables are covered with sauce, about 3 minutes. Return pork to the wok. Add additional sauce as desired. Remove from heat.

Garnish yakisoba with kizami nori and a small pile of beni shoga just before serving.

recipes.Title: Lamb pie Tuscan style
recipes.Ingredients:
1.6kg boneless lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
plain flour, for dusting
olive oil, for frying
1 onion, finely sliced
1 garlic bulb, halved through the middle
350ml white wine
500ml chicken stock
10 thyme sprigs
3 bay leaves
1 x 460g jar roasted red peppers, drained and sliced or use fresh roasted peppers
100g green olives, pitted
handful flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
500g shortcrust pastry
1 egg, beaten
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to gas 1, 140°C, fan 120°C. Season the lamb and dust with flour. Heat a little oil in a large frying pan and brown the lamb in batches. Transfer to a casserole dish.
Add another 1 tbsp of oil to the pan. Gently fry the onion for 5 minutes, then add it to the casserole dish with the garlic and wine. Set it on the hob and bring to the boil. Simmer for 2 minutes, then add the stock and herbs; cover. Bake for 2 hours, or until the lamb is tender. Scoop out the meat and set aside in a large pie dish. Discard the thyme, bay leaves and garlic. Put the casserole over a high heat and simmer the juices, until glossy. Pour over the lamb; set aside to cool. Stir through the peppers, olives and parsley.
Preheat the oven to gas 6, 200°C, fan 180°C. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the pastry to the thickness of a pound coin. Brush the rim of the pie dish with beaten egg and cover with the pastry lid.
Trim the overhang, then crimp the edges to seal. Make a small steam hole in the centre. Roll out the pastry trimmings and cut out decorations in the shape of your choice (optional), such as leaves or letters. Brush the pie with beaten egg, then add your decoration (if using) and glaze again. Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until golden.

recipes.Title: Rainbow pie
recipes.Ingredients:
700g butternut squash chunks sprinkled with chilli flakes
2 onions, thinly sliced into half moons
6 garlic cloves, crushed
2 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for greasing
1 tbsp dried thyme
700g shortcrust pastry
flour, for dusting
500g spinach
2 x 250g tubs ricotta, sprinkled with nutmeg
25g cheddar cheese, grated
130g basil pesto
1 lemon, zested 
25g panko breadcrumbs
460g roasted peppers, thickly sliced
1 egg, beaten
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to gas 6, 200°C, fan 180°C. Spread out the squash in a large roasting tin with the onions and garlic, drizzle over the oil, season and scatter with the thyme. Toss to combine. Cut the red peppers in half and lay on grease-proof paper on a baking tray. Place both the above in the oven and roast for 25-30 mins until tender, tossing halfway through. Set aside to cool completely.
Meanwhile, roll out 500g pastry on a lightly floured surface to a 38cm circle. Lightly grease the base and sides of a 23cm round springform cake tin. Lift the pastry into the tin and gently press into the base and sides to evenly line, leaving a 1cm overhang. Prick the base all over with a fork. Chill for at least 30 mins, or up to 6 hrs ahead.
Put the spinach in a large saucepan, cover with boiling water and leave to wilt. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool; squeeze out as much water as possible. Put the spinach, ricotta, hard cheese, pesto and lemon zest in a bowl, season and mix well.
Preheat the oven to 190°C, fan 170°C. Remove the chilled pastry case from the fridge and scatter half the breadcrumbs over the base. Arrange the roasted squash and onions on top in a single, even layer. Top with the spinach mixture. Layer on the roasted peppers, overlapping to create an even layer. Scatter with the remaining breadcrumbs.
Roll out the remaining pastry on a lightly floured work surface to a 24cm circle, then lay it on top of the pie and press the edges together to seal. Trim away any excess, then crimp all the way around. Brush the top of the pie with beaten egg. Make 3 incisions in the centre to allow steam to escape. Place the tin on a baking tray and bake for 1 hr or until the pastry is cooked and golden.
Leave to cool for at least 30 mins before releasing from the tin. Transfer to a wire rack for 2 hrs if serving warm, or leave to cool completely. Once cool, keep in an airtight container in the fridge; it will be easier to slice once it has been chilled. Will keep, covered, for up to 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.Title: Bacon and asparagus risotto
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp olive oil
6 slices bacon, chopped (preferably thick cut)
1 small onion, diced
4 cloves garlic, crushed
160 g arborio rice
760 l chicken stock
180 ml dry white wine
1 bunch asparagus, stalks trimmed and cut into thirds
2 tsp dill
1 tsp oregano
2 tsp basil
25g parmesan cheese
Knob of butter
Salt
Freshly ground black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
In a pot over medium heat, cook bacon until crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and drain. Add onion to bacon fat and cook until soft, 5 minutes, then add garlic and cook until fragrant, 2 minutes more. Add rice and stir until combined, then add 240ml chicken stock.
Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until stock is completely absorbed. When it's absorbed, add wine. Stir until fully absorbed, then add remaining stock 240ml at a time until rice is tender and creamy, about 30 minutes. Season and add asparagus and let cook until tender, 6 minutes then stir in the dill, basil, oregano, parmesan, bacon and a knob of butter.

recipes.Title: Chicken karahi
recipes.Ingredients:
50 ml vegetable oil
650 g skinless, boneless chicken thighs, cut into irregular bite-sized pieces
4 medium ripe tomatoes, roughly chopped (around 110g each)
½ tsp. chilli flakes
½ tsp. turmeric
1 tsp. salt
1 medium head of garlic, roughly chopped
25mm piece of ginger, roughly chopped
4 green finger chillies, half kept whole
Handful fresh coriander
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oil in a large-based pan or wok. Add the chicken and let it settle for a few seconds before stirring.
Fry for 5 minutes on high heat, continuing to stir regularly until the fat from the chicken begins to render out. 
Toss in the ginger and garlic and fry for one minute before adding the turmeric, salt and chilli flakes. Immediately stir in the tomatoes and simmer everything together over medium heat until tender. This will take about 15 minutes depending on the size of your chicken pieces. If the moisture released from the tomatoes dries up before the chicken is cooked add a small splash of hot water to prevent the dish from catching on the base of your pan.
Turn the heat up to the highest setting and continuously stir fry the chicken until any remaining moisture dries up and the tomatoes have melded with the other ingredients, creating a chunky sauce that coats each bitesize piece. You'll know you've completed this stage when you swipe a wooden spoon from one side of the pan to the other and you can see the oil separates from the sauce. 
Turn off the heat and immediately stir in the chillies and coriander. If you prefer a saucier curry stir in a splash of hot water. Serve with naan, roti, or rice.

recipes.Title: Marry Me chicken
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
6 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs 
Salt
freshly ground black pepper
6 cloves garlic, crushed
1 tbsp. fresh thyme leaves
1 tsp. crushed chilli flakes
200 ml chicken stock
100 ml double cream
30 g chopped sun-dried tomatoes
30 g freshly grated Parmesan
freshly torn basil, for serving
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to 190°C (170ºC fan). In a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat, heat oil. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper and sear, skin-side down, until golden, 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer chicken to a plate and pour off half the fat from pan.
Return pan to medium heat and add garlic, thyme, and chilli flakes. Cook until fragrant, 1 minute, then stir in stock, double cream, sun-dried tomatoes, and Parmesan and season with more salt. Bring to a simmer, then return chicken to pan, skin-side up.
Transfer pan to oven and bake until chicken is cooked through (and juices run clear when chicken is pierced with a knife), 17 to 20 minutes.
Garnish with basil and serve.

recipes.Title: Ravioli with butternut squash and gorgonzola
recipes.Ingredients:
225g pasta dough (fresh, rolled into sheets)
340g butternut squash
1 tbsp olive oil
salt
pepper
½ tbsp butter
1 egg
125g gorgonzola cheese (crumbled)
25g cream cheese 
30g Parmesan cheese 

Sauce:
50g butter
100g gorgonzola cheese
150ml whipping cream
Chopped basil leaves
½ tsp nutmeg
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to 200°C degrees.
Peel the squash and cut into cubes and placing them on a baking sheet. Coat them with olive oil, salt & pepper. Roast the squash for 45 minutes until it is tender.
Allow to cool for 15 minutes or so.
Transfer squash to a food processor add the egg and cheeses. Puree until smooth.
Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Lightly flour your ravioli mold.
Lay one sheet of pasta on the mold, making sure the entire mold is covered. Take a tablespoon of filling and place into each well. Spritz the pasta sheet with a little water. Lay the second sheet on top and run a rolling pin over to seal. Turn the mold over and release the ravioli. Lay the ravioli on a floured baking pan and continue making ravioli until you've used all the pasta sheets. Make sure to cover the raviolis as you work.
Heat a large pot of water for the ravioli.
For the sauce, melt the butter in a sauce pan and add the cream. Add the gorgonzola, basil leaves and nutmeg. Cook on medium-low for 2-3 minutes, until there is a smooth, consistent sauce. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Cook the ravioli in the boiling water for 2 minutes, until it is floating. Remove from water and add directly to butter sauce.
Serve with freshly grated parmesan cheese

recipes.Title: John's granary bread
recipes.Ingredients:
2 heaped tsp brown sugar
600ml tepid water
15g yeast granules
50ml olive oil
585g granary flour
360g strong white flour
90g oats
2 tbsp sesame seeds
2 tbsp sunflower seeds
2 tsp salt
10ml cider vinegar
recipes.Preparation:
Measure out 580 ml tepid water in large measuring jug and stir in the brown sugar then add the yeast and stir vigorously until dispersed.
Tare the mixer bowl and add all the dry ingredients; mix at varying speeds until uniform. Add the 10ml of vinegar.
By this time the yeast will be frothing, so add the olive oil into the yeast mix and stir.
Set the mixer to lowest speed and add the yeast mix. Increase the speed to maximum until the mix has come together and all the powder has been taken up. Turn the speed to low again and set the timer for 10 minutes. If the mix comes to a ball around the dough hook, stop the mixer and clean the dough from the hook into the bowl and then lower the hook in again.
While the mixer is running, liberally grease the bread tin with butter.
After 10 minutes mixing, remove the dough from the bowl and spray the inside of the bowl with sunflower oil, then replace the dough. Spray a sheet of clingfilm with oil and cover the dough closely. Prove the dough for  about 40 minutes until it has doubled in size. If it doubles in less time, the temperature is too warm and the bread could have too loose a structure under the crust. In this case, cool the bowl for a minute or two. If the dough is taking too long to rise, warm the bowl a little.
After proving, turn out the dough, reserving the clingfilm and knock back the dough. Mould the dough into a sausage of the same dimensions as the bread tin and push the dough into the tin, moulding it into the corners. Add 1tsp salt to a small bowl of water and brush the surface of the dough with the salted water. Sprinkle the loaf with sunflower seeds and then pumpkin seeds. Brush again with the salted water and cover the loaf with the oiled clingfilm. Prove again for about 1 hour until the top of the loaf is well above the edges of the tin. Preheat the oven to 200°C normal (not fan). Bake for 40 minutes and then turn out onto a cooling rack.

recipes.Title: Gazpacho
recipes.Ingredients:
900g Ripe Juicy Tomatoes
2 Garlic Cloves
½ Onion (white type not sweet)
1 Green Sweet Pepper
1 Piece Cucumber (about 6 inches long)
½ tsp Ground Cumin
3 tbsp Sherry Vinegar
½ tbsp Salt
235ml Virgin Olive Oil
1 piece French Bread (3-4 inches long)
recipes.Preparation:
Rinse and chop all the vegetables. Peel the cucumber, no green left.
Place the piece of bread in a bowl with water in order to soak it. Once soaked, put all water away, squeeze the soaked bread with your bare hands as much as you can and set aside.
In a good blender or food processor put the tomatoes (previously cut in 4-5 pieces each), the garlic, onion, pepper, cucumber, squeezed bread. Add remaining ingredients and blend at the highest speed until the soup is very smooth. Pour it in a jar or bowl and let it chill in your fridge.

recipes.Title: Slow-cooked smoky pork ribs
recipes.Ingredients:
Sauce:
300g tomato ketchup
75ml cider vinegar
50g brown sugar
30g butter
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
1½ tbsp English mustard
1 tsp salt
200ml Guiness (from 440ml can)
2 tsp Bart smoky BBQ seasoning

900g pork ribs
recipes.Preparation:
Add all the sauce ingredients to a small pan and mediuim heat for 20-25 minutes until thick. Set aside.

Sprinkle the ribs with salt and then the seasoning and set aside for 20 minutes.

Heat the oven to 150°C fan, dab the ribs with Guiness and cook for 1 hour. Dab the ribs with more Guiness and cook for a further hour. Heat half of the sauce, glaze the ribs and cook for 10-15 minutes, repeat the glazing and cook for another 10-15 minutes.

Brush a large sheet of foil with the remaining Guiness and lay the ribs meat side down on the foil. Wrap up and allow to rest in a warm place 20 minutes.

Serve with the rest of the sauce and coleslaw.

recipes.Title: Blackberry galettes
recipes.Ingredients:
600g blackberries
fine zest of half a lemon
1 tsp lemon juice
pared zest of half a lemon to serve
50g caster sugar
1½ tbsp cornflour
2 tbsp demerara sugar
Vanilla ice cream to serve

Pastry:
300g plain flour
½ tsp salt
200g butter
50g caster sugar
1 egg, beaten
recipes.Preparation:
For the pastr, mix the flour and salt then rub in the butter. Add the sugar and half the egg then mix in 60-75ml ice cold water until a shaggy dough is formed. Flatten into a disc and chill for 20 minutes.

Cut the pastry into 4 pieces and then roll each out into a disc about 3 mm thick. Line a baking tray with a double layer of foil and then place the pastry discs on top.

Stir together the fruit, lemon zest, juice, sugar and cornflour; put ¼ on to each pastry disc leaving a 3-4cm border. Fold the edges of the pastry over the edges of the fruit. Brush the pastry edges with beaten egg and sprinkle with demerara sugar. Chill for 30 minutes.

Pre-heat the overn to 190°C fan. Place the tray of galettes in the oven and bake for 30 minutes until golden. Scatter the pared zest over the galettes and serve with a ball of vanilla ice cream.

recipes.Title: Paella marisco
recipes.Ingredients:
3 cloves garlic
½ onion
½ red bell pepper
1 cleaned tube of squid
80ml extra virgin olive oil
50g tomato puree
½ tsp smoked paprika
salt
black pepper
600ml fish stock
saffron
200g bomba rice
12 raw jumbo shrimp (peeled and deveined)
8 fresh mussels (debearded and cleaned)
8 clams
fresh parsley
lemon
recipes.Preparation:
First, cut up all ingredients, mince 3 cloves of garlic, dice 1/2 of an onion, dice 1/2 of a red bell pepper and cut 1 large cleaned tube of squid into small squares, also reserve 12 raw jumbo shrimp that have been peeled and deveined and 8 fresh cleaned mussels and clams.
Heat a paella pan or large frying pan with a medium-high heat and add the olive oil, once the oil is hot, season it with salt, add the onions and mix with the oil, after 1 minute add the red bell pepper, mix and cook for 3 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato puree, season everything with a generous 1/2 teaspoon of smoked paprika, a generous pinch of salt and freshly cracked black pepper, continue to cook for 2 minutes, then add the squid into the pan, add the fish stock and the saffron, gently mix everything together
Once the broth comes to a boil, add the rice to the pan and then gently distribute the rice throughout the pan with a wooden spoon, do not mix the rice, after 10 minutes of cooking, reduce to a low-medium heat (do not mix the rice after this point, you can give the pan a quick shake once in a while).
After simmering for 10 minutes and there is very little broth left, turn the fire back to a medium-high heat for 1 minute, this technique is to make the socarrat (burnt rice on the bottom of the pan), then turn off the heat, cover the paella pan completely and let it rest between 5-7 minutes. 
During this time, cook the shrimp, clams and the mussels and then add to the paella.
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley and a couple of lemon wedges.

recipes.Title: Korean BBQ beef ribs
recipes.Ingredients:
450g short beef ribs, trimmed and cut thinly into ½cm thick slices
2 pears (use a semi-hard sweet variety like conference or barlette), peeled and grated
3 cloves garlic, grated
3½ tbsp dark brown sugar
4 tbsp tablespoons soy sauce
2.5 tbsp roasted sesame oil
2 tsp grated ginger
8 grinds of black pepper (adjust to taste)
1 pinch sea salt

For the ssam jang sauce:
1 spring onion, finely chopped
1 clove garlic, grated
4½ tbsp Korean fermented soy bean paste (dwengjang)
3 tbsp roasted sesame seeds
2 tbsp Korean chilli paste (gochujang)
2 tbsp mirin
1½ tsp roasted sesame oil
recipes.Preparation:
To make the ssam jang sauce, mix all of the ingredients together. Put in a small bowl and serve later with the ribs.
Place the beef into a large re-sealable plastic bag. Add all of the other ingredients and massage into the meat well. Chill and let marinate for at least 2 hours or up to overnight.
Heat up a grill or griddle pan until very hot. Shake off any excess marinade from the meat and grill the beef strips until desired doneness, for rare about 30 seconds each side.
Serve immediately with white sticky rice, green leaf lettuce, sesame leaves (optional) ssam jang sauce (recipe follows). Place a small scoop of rice, a smear of ssam jang sauce and a piece of beef into a lettuce leaf. Wrap and enjoy.

recipes.Title: Pork satay
recipes.Ingredients:
1 kg pork fillet
2 large red peppers
4 spring onions

For the satay sauce:
200 ml coconut milk
2 tbsp crunchy peanut butter
1 x 5 cm piece of root ginger
2 cloves of garlic
1 red chilli
1 bunch of coriander
1 tsp allergy-friendly stock powder
2 tsp soft light brown sugar
1 good pinch of sea salt
2 tbsp warm water
1 tsp toasted sesame oil
recipes.Preparation:
First make the satay sauce. Gently heat the coconut milk in a small saucepan. Add the peanut butter and stir continuously over a low heat until it has dissolved and you are left with a thick sauce. Take off the heat and set aside.
Peel the ginger and finely grate both this and the garlic. Finely chop the chilli, retaining the seeds, and coriander and add to a bowl with the ginger and garlic. Add the stock powder, sugar, salt, warm water and sesame oil and then mix together. Pour over the peanut and coconut milk and stir together before dividing the sauce between two separate bowls.
Trim any excess fat from the pork fillet and cut into 2.5cm/1in chunks. Add the pork to one bowl of the satay sauce, mix thoroughly, cover and leave to marinate for 30 minutes to 3 hours (don't refrigerate as this tends to make the coconut milk solidify). Set aside the remaining sauce, also covered, for later.
While the pork is marinating, deseed the pepper and cut into 2.5cm/1in pieces. Finely chop the spring onion into rounds and set aside. When you are ready to cook, preheat the grill to medium-high.
Thread the marinated pork onto the skewers, alternating every now and then with the chunks of red pepper. Place under the grill and cook for 10-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until the pork is cooked and tender.
Remove from the grill, place on a serving platter, sprinkle over the spring onions and serve with a bowl of white basmati rice and the remaining satay sauce to dip the pork into.

recipes.Title: Ravioli with prawns and saffron bisque
recipes.Ingredients:
Filling:
12-14 tiger prawns, shelled
1 spring onion, sliced
10g basil, chopped
10g coriander, chopped
5g chives, sliced
1 lemon, zested and juiced
150g ricotta
Salt

Saffron bisque:
Reserved prawn heads and shells
1 onion, diced
3 stalks celery, diced
3 carrots, diced
2 lemongrass, sliced
4 cloves garlic, sliced
1 thumb ginger, sliced
1 medium chili, sliced
10g thyme
200ml white wine
500ml chicken stock
500ml water
200ml cream
1g saffron
1 lemon, juiced

Prawn head oil:
100ml oil
6 prawn heads
2 cloves garlic
1 thumb ginger
10ml chili flakes
15ml smoked paprika
Salt
recipes.Preparation:
Place a frying pan on high heat with a touch of oil. Season the prawns generously before searing them in the hot pan on either side. Remove from the pan and slice each prawn into 4-5 pieces.
Add the prawns to a bowl along with the remaining ingredients and combine. Line a tray with baking paper. Spoon the filling into 60g portions and place evenly on the tray. Place the tray in the freezer for 20-30 minutes, before rolling each portion into an even ball.

Make the saffron bisque. Pre-heat oven to 180°C and place the reserved prawn heads and shells on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes. In a large saucepan, sweat the onion, celery, carrots, lemongrass, garlic, chilli and thyme in a little oil. Add the roasted prawn heads and shells, before deglazing with the white wine. Add the chicken stock and the water, and bring to the boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 45 minutes. Strain the stock and place back on a medium heat. Reduce by 1/2, then add the cream and the saffron. Reduce by 1/2 once more and season with lemon juice.

To make the prawn head oil, heat the oil in a small saucepan, before adding the remaining ingredients. Cook on a low heat until everything is well caramelised. Turn the heat off and allow to steep for 20 minutes. Strain the oil through a sieve lined with muslin cloth.

recipes.Title: Roast chicken with pancetta and orzo
recipes.Ingredients:
2 tbsp. olive oil
1.7 kg whole chicken
2 carrots, cut into 1.5cm pieces
1 leek, finely sliced
2 celery sticks, sliced
100 g pancetta lardons
1 lemon, cut into 6 wedges
1 tarragon sprig, plus extra leaves, chopped, to garnish
500 mL hot chicken stock
300 g orzo pasta
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to 180°C fan. Roast the chicken in very little oil for 40 minutes. Remove chicken to a board and pour the meat juices into a casserole.

Add carrots, leek, celery and pancetta to the casserole and cook for 5min, until beginning to brown. Stir in lemon wedges, tarragon sprig and plentyof seasoning. Pour in the orzo and fry for a minute or two. Return chicken to the casserole dish, breast up. Pour in enough stock to cover the orzo; bring to the boil.

Cover with the lid and cook in the oven for 20min. 

Carefully transfer the chicken to a serving dish, spoon the orzo around it and leave to rest for 10min. Scatter over chopped tarragon and serve.

recipes.Title: Chicken and red pepper
recipes.Ingredients:
700g chicken
1½ tbsp butter
1 onion
6 garlic cloves minced
2 roasted red pepper diced
85g cream cheese cubed
270ml chicken stock
40g shaved parmesan cheese
Paprika
Salt
Pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Slice the peppers in half and roast, cut side down, on a parchment lined baking tray at 200° fan for 30-35 minutes.
Season both sides of the chicken tenderloins with salt and pepper.
Heat up a skillet over medium heat with 1/2 of the tablespoon of butter.
Cook the chicken tenderloins in the skillet on each side for 3-4 minutes, or until the chicken is no longer pink on the inside.
Turn off the heat and remove the cooked chicken to a plate.
Add in the other 1/2 tablespoon of butter to the skillet and turn the heat back on. Sprinkle in the diced onion, roasted red peppers and the minced garlic cloves. Stir and cook for about 3 minutes.
Pour in the broth, then add in the cream cheese cubes. Break up the cream cheese with a wooden spoon until it is fully incorporated into the sauce
Sprinkle in the parmesan cheese, mix until melted.
Add the chicken back into the skillet, pouring some of the sauce over the tenderloins. Heat up for one more minute, then serve with roasted vegetables.

recipes.Title: Bang Bang Prawns
recipes.Ingredients:
For the prawns:
200g panko bread crumbs
2 tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
2 cloves garlic
Salt
Freshly ground black pepper
2 large eggs
125 g plain flour
450 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined
Freshly chopped coriander, for garnish
For bang bang sauce:
2 tbsp. mayonnaise
2 tbsp. sweet chilli sauce
1 tbsp. sriracha
Juice of 1 lime
1 tsp. honey
Salt
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to 200°C (180ºC fan) and line a large baking tray with parchment paper. In a shallow bowl, stir together bread crumbs, oil, and garlic powder and season with salt and pepper. In another shallow bowl, whisk eggs. Put flour in a third bowl. Using tongs, dip prawns first in flour, then egg, then panko mixture, and transfer to prepared baking tray. Continue until all prawns are coated.
Bake until the prawns are crispy and golden, 13 to 15 minutes.
Make the bang bang sauce:
In a medium bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, sweet chili sauce, sriracha, lime juice, and honey and season with salt.
Drizzle Bang Bang Sauce over the prawns and garnish with coriander before serving.

recipes.Title: Sicilian pesto with Penne
recipes.Ingredients:
325 g  penne pasta
50 g blanched almonds
250 g cherry tomatoes
2 garlic cloves, crushed
small bunch basil
40 g Pecorino, finely grated, plus extra to serve
4 tbsp. extra virgin olive oil
8 pancetta slices, roughly chopped
recipes.Preparation:
Cook pasta in a large pan of boiling salted water. 

Meanwhile, pulse the almonds in a food processor until roughly chopped.Add the tomatoes, garlic, basil (including stalks), Pecorino and plenty of seasoning and pulse until fairly smooth. With the motor running, slowly pour in the oil until amalgamated. Check seasoning.

Fry the pancetta in a large, non-stick frying pan over medium heat until golden. Reduce heat to low and stir through the pesto. Drain the pasta, reserving a little of the starchy cooking water, and add to the pancetta pan. Cook, stirring through a little cooking water to loosen if needed, until warmed through.

Divide between 4 bowls, sprinkle over extra Pecorino and serve.

recipes.Title: Autumn tomato chutney
recipes.Ingredients:
1 kg Mixed Red and Green Tomatoes
200 g Sweet Red Peppers
300 g White Onions
3 Cloves of Garlic
1 Chilli
1 Thumb Size Piece of Fresh Ginger
2 tsp Mustard Seeds
200 g Sultanas
500 g Cooking Apples
1 tsp Flaked Sea Salt
0.5 tsp Allspice
575 ml Malt Vinegar
450 g Dark Brown Soft Sugar
recipes.Preparation:
Place tomatoes and peppers into a food processor and blend. Place into a large pan.
Blend the onions, garlic, chilli and ginger and add to the pan.
Add the mustard seeds and Sultanas.
Blend the cooking apples and add.
Add the salt and allspice.
Pour over the malt vinegar and bring to the boil over a medium heat.
Continue to cook over a medium heat for 1 hour, stirring occasionally to prevent the chutney from sticking to the pan. The liquid will dissolve and the chutney will become thicker.
Add the sugar and mix through, continue to cook for another hour, still stirring.
Once the mixture is thickened, pour into sterilised jars.
Once the chutney is cooled you can eat it straight away but for best results leave the chutney in the jars to mature for a couple of months.
recipes.Keywords: tomato, red peppers, onion, apples, sultanas

recipes.Title: Lamb passanda
recipes.Ingredients:
700 g lamb neck or shoulder, cut into 2-3cm chunks
1 x 4cm piece ginger, peeled and finely grated
4 garlic cloves, crushed
1 green chilli, finely chopped (deseeded if you prefer)
2 tsp. turmeric
2 tbsp. garam masala
1 tsp. smoked paprika
2 tsp. ground cumin
2 tsp. ground coriander
½ tsp. chilli powder
150 g natural yoghurt
2 tbsp. vegetable oil
2 large onions, finely sliced
10 cardamom pods, lightly bashed
2 cinnamon sticks
1 medium tomato, chopped
200 g coconut cream
75 g ground almonds
1 x 200g pack of baby spinach
Small pack of coriander, roughly chopped
50 g flaked almonds, toasted
recipes.Preparation:
First, add the lamb pieces to a medium sized mixing bowl, along with the ginger, garlic, chilli, turmeric, garam masala, paprika, cumin, ground coriander, chilli powder and yoghurt. Mix well until the lamb is completely coated. Cover and leave to marinade in the fridge for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan or casserole pot over medium high heat. Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and golden brown, 8-10 minutes. Add the lamb with all the marinade, cardamom pods and cinnamon sticks and cook until lightly browned, 8-10 minutes.
Add the tomato, coconut cream, 400ml water, ground almonds and season with salt and pepper. Stir everything together, bring to a simmer then cover with a lid and gently simmer, stirring occasionally, for 2 1/2 - 3 hours, until the lamb is completely tender and falling apart, adding more water to loosen if needed.
Remove the cardamom pods and cinnamon sticks then stir the spinach through until wilted. Taste and season with more salt and pepper if you like. Stir through the coriander and serve with rice or naan and top with the toasted flaked almonds.

recipes.Title: Korv stroganoff
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp tomato purée
1 tbsp Dijon mustard
1 tsp paprika
70 ml single cream
1 pinch sea salt and black pepper
200 g fresh tagliatelle or pappardelle
2 tbsp capers or eldercapers
1 handful finely chopped fresh chives
1 tbsp butter
1 large onion, peeled and finely chopped
170 g smoked sausage or falukorv, very finely diced
recipes.Preparation:
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil for the tagliatelle or pappardelle.
Put the butter, onion and sausage into a large pan. Fry, stirring occasionally, until the sausage and onion are golden. Add the tomato purée, mustard, paprika and cream, continuing to stir so the flavours mingle, and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Taste for seasoning and adjust to taste.
Add the pasta to the pan of boiling water. Cook for 7 minutes (or according to packet instructions). Drain the pasta, reserving a small cup (around 80ml/2.7 fl oz) of pasta water.
Add the cup of pasta water to the sausage sauce. Stir in with the capers and take off the heat.
Toss the pasta in the sauce until well coated, and sprinkle over the chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Tortellini burrata
recipes.Ingredients:
For the tomatoes confit
150 g datterini or cherry tomatoes
1 glug of olive oil
1 pinch fine salt
½ tsp icing (confectioners’) sugar
2 thyme sprigs

For the pasta dough (makes 200g of dough)
64 g plain (all-purpose) flour
56 g durum wheat flour
3 egg yolks

For the tortellini and sauce
375 g burrata plus 25g to serve
300 g ricotta cheese
2½ tbsp olive oil
1 tsp fine salt, plus extra for the sauce
15 datterini or plum cherry tomatoes, halved
1 garlic clove, unpeeled
1 pinch Espelette pepper or paprika
200 g pasta dough
1 egg yolk, beaten (optional)
1 pinch each of salt and pepper

To serve/garnish
10 tomatoes confit
5 marjoram leaves
recipes.Preparation:
First make the tomatoes confit. Preheat the oven to 180°C. Wash and halve the tomatoes vertically. Place each half cut-side down in an ovenproof dish. Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with salt and the sugar and add the thyme. Roast in the preheated oven for 30 minutes.
First make the pasta dough. On a clean work surface, make a mound with the plain (all-purpose) and durum wheat flours and create a well in the centre. Put the egg yolks into the well and gradually mix the flour into the centre to combine with the egg yolks. Gradually add the flour from around the sides until all the flour is mixed and you have a smooth ball of dough.
Now make the filling. Finely chop the burrata, reserving a little for the garnish, and then mix the rest with the ricotta. Stir in 4 tablespoons of the olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a frying pan, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over a medium heat and fry the garlic for 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes and continue cooking for 10 minutes over a low heat until the tomatoes break up. Season with salt, pepper and Espelette pepper.
Add the burrata mixture to the pan and stir to combine. Set aside.
On a lightly floured work surface, roll out the pasta dough to 2mm thick using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Trim the edges to give it a square shape, then mark out a grid of 4-cm squares.
Using a small spoon or a piping bag, place a little filling in the middle of a square.
Moisten two adjoining sides with a little water or egg yolk, then fold two opposite points inwards and press them together to form a triangle (tortellino). Pinch the edges to prevent them opening during cooking. Repeat to make the remainder of the tortellini.
Cook the tortellini for 4 minutes in a large pan of salted boiling water. Drain using a slotted spoon.
To serve, add some tomato confit, the reserved burrata and some marjoram leaves to garnish.

recipes.Title: Pasta aglione
recipes.Ingredients:
1 kg cherry tomatoes, halved around the equator (not pole to pole)
7 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
5 garlic cloves (skin on)
0.2 tsp dried chilli flakes or finely sliced fresh red chilli
320 g dried pasta
1 handful basil leaves, roughly torn if large
25 g grated Parmesan
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to 170°C (340°F/Gas 3).
Put the tomatoes cut side up in a roasting tray and pour over the oil. Put the garlic cloves between the tomatoes and any tomato stems, if you have them, as they will flavour the oil.
Scatter with dried chilli (if using – add fresh chilli later on), season with salt and pepper, and roast for 15–20 minutes or until the tomatoes just start to collapse and brown.
After 10 minutes stir the fresh chilli (if using fresh instead of dried) into the oil (fresh chilli might burn if put on top of the tomatoes at the beginning).
Meanwhile, cook the pasta to coincide with the end of the cooking time for the tomatoes.
When the tomatoes are cooked, remove the tray from the oven and use the flat of a wooden spoon to squeeze the soft garlic out of their skins.
Mix this gently with the tomatoes and discard the garlic skins as well as the tomato stems. Pour the drained pasta into the hot tray.
Add the basil leaves and use a pair of tongs to combine, then serve straight away in warmed bowls, scattered with Parmesan.

recipes.Title: Coconut and oat biscuits
recipes.Ingredients:
80 g plain flour
100 g rolled oats
60 g desiccated coconut
80 g unsalted butter
2 tbsp golden syrup
60 g caster sugar
0.5 tsp bicarbonate of soda
1 tsp hot water
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to 170ºC/Gas Mark 3. In a large bowl, mix together the flour, oats and coconut.
Tip the butter, golden syrup and sugar into a medium-sized saucepan and, stirring constantly, melt over a low heat.
Add the dry ingredients. Mix together the bicarbonate of soda and hot water, and add to the mixture. Stir everything together until combined, then shape into walnut sized balls.
Pat each ball down slightly on to the lined baking trays, leaving a 5cm gap between each. Bake on the middle shelf of the preheated oven for 10 minutes until slightly spread and golden.
Leave to cool on the tray for 5 minutes before transferring the cookies to a wire rack to cool completely.

recipes.Title: Porchetta
recipes.Ingredients:
2.5kg pork belly, boneless
600g of pork loin
2 sprigs of rosemary, leaves picked
3 sprigs of fresh thyme, leaves picked
1 large bulb of smoked garlic
1 tbsp of fennel seeds
1 pinch of chilli flakes
1 lemon, zested
2 tbsp of white wine
1 tsp  salt
½ tsp black pepper
500ml of water
recipes.Preparation:
To begin, place the fennel seeds and chilli flakes in hot, dry pan and toast for 30 seconds, until fragrant
Peel the garlic cloves and place in a pestle and mortar. Add the herbs, toasted spices, salt, pepper and white wine and grind to a rough paste
Place the pork belly skin-side down and lay the loin across the width. Trim the loin down to size so it rolls up neatly
Lightly score the belly flesh in a 2cm diagonal pattern and massage the stuffing paste into the belly and loin. Place the loin back onto the belly
Roll up tightly, tie up with butcher's string and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight. This will dry out the skin, giving a crispier crackling
Preheat the oven to 160°C/gas mark 3
Place the pork on a wire rack set over an oven tray. Pour in the 500ml of water and cook in the oven for 3 1/2 to 4 hours. Check at intervals; if the water has evaporated, add a little more
Leave to rest for 30 minutes before carving. Slice and serve warm in buttered bread rolls

recipes.Title: Stuffed Peppers
recipes.Ingredients:
4 Green or red capsicum, sliced in half 
6-8 shallots, sliced and chopped
8 cherry tomatoes, chopped
4 rashers of bacon, chopped
1 tbsp honey
1 tbsp chipotle sauce
60g parmesan, grated
salt
black pepper
olive oil
recipes.Preparation:
Place the capsicum in an oven-proof dish, season and drizzle with olive oil. Roast in the oven at 190°C(180°C fan) for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, fry the bacon for 5 minutes. Blend the shallots, tomatoes, honey and chipotle and season well. Add to the bacon and fry over a medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.

After the capsicum have roasted for 10 minutes, remove from the oven and stuff with the shallot mix then return to the oven for another 20 minutes.

Remove from the oven, sprinkle with the parmesan and then finish in the oven for another 5-10 minutes so that the cheese has melted and is bubbling,
recipes.Keywords: red peppers, shallots, tomato, bacon, spicy

recipes.Title: Sichuan beef
recipes.Ingredients:
2 tbsp soy sauce
2 tsp rice vinegar or white wine vinegar
1 tsp cornflour
2 cm root ginger, peeled and sliced
500 g lean beef steak, visible fat removed, cut into bite-sized pieces
Sesame oil for frying
2 garlic cloves, crushed
2 red chillies, deseeded and thinly sliced, plus extra to garnish
0.25 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, crushed
1 pinch Chinese five-spice powder
1 red pepper, deseeded and cut into chunks
1 yellow pepper, deseeded and cut into chunks
1 spring onion, finely chopped, to garnish
recipes.Preparation:
Put the soy sauce, vinegar, ½ teaspoon of salt, cornflour and ginger in a bowl with 1 tablespoon of water and mix together.
Add the steak and stir to coat well. Cover and leave to marinate in a cool place for 30 minutes.
 Fry the garlic, chilli, Sichuan peppercorns and five-spice powder for 1 minute.
Add the marinated beef (reserving the marinade) and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Remove and keep warm.
Add the peppers to the wok and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then return the steak and reserved marinade to the wok. Stir-fry briskly over a medium heat for 1 minute.
Season with plenty of black pepper, scatter over the spring onion and extra chilli and serve hot with rice of your choice.

recipes.Title: Aubergine shakshuka
recipes.Ingredients:
¼ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper
2 large eggs
50 g feta cheese, roughly chopped
6 large tomatoes on the vine, chopped
2 tbsp tomato puree
1 large aubergine, sliced into rounds
¼ red onion
1 jalapeno
1 garlic clove, finely chopped
1 tsp cumin
½ tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp cinnamon
Handful of torn basil
2 tbsp olive oil, for frying
To serve:
1 sprig of parsley
1 sprig of mint
2 warm pitta bread
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to 220°C/gas mark 7. Plunge the aubergine into boiling water for 10 minutes, then into cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan. Season the aubergine slices and fry them in batches for 3-4 minutes on each side, until golden and tender, adding more oil as necessary. Transfer the slices to a plate as they are cooked.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a medium frying pan and sauté the onion and jalapeno gently over a low to medium heat for about 8 minutes, stirring every now and then, until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook for a further minute.
Tip the tomatoes into the pan along with any juice and stir into the onion. Cook for 8 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down and softened; they should be a pulp.
Pour in the tomato juice and cook, again over a low heat, for 5 minutes. The sauce will be quite thick by this stage.
Season with salt, black pepper and the cumin, if using.
Spread a layer of aubergine slices over a large, ovenproof dish, then spoon over half the tomato sauce. Repeat to make two layers.
Make a hole in the sauce with the back of a large spoon and crack an egg into it. Do the same all round the dish until you’ve positioned all the eggs. Scatter over the feta.
Bake in the oven for 5 minutes. Pick the leaves off the parsley and mint sprigs, and chop roughly. When the shakshuka is ready, scatter over the herbs and serve with the warm pitta bread.

recipes.Title: Chicken wings with tomato
recipes.Ingredients:
2 tbsp groundnut oil
1 onion, chopped
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 kg chicken wings
0.5 tsp sea salt
0.5 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 tsp ground cumin
400 g chopped tomatoes
1 tsp tomato purée
1 pinch caster sugar
1 spring onion, sliced diagonally, to garnish
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat a large saucepan over a medium-high heat, drizzle in the groundnut oil and add the chopped onion and paprika.
Stir frequently for around 5 minutes and fry until softened and reddish in colour.
Add the chicken wings, salt and pepper and sprinkle in the cumin.
Fry the wings in the spices for 3 minutes, turning over halfway until the skin is browned on both sides and covered in those aromatic spices.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, sugar and 250ml cold water, and give it a good stir so it’s all mixed well together.
Bring to a boil then reduce the heat to medium and cook, uncovered, for 45 minutes.
Once the chicken is cooked through, the sauce will have reduced to a rich tomato coating on the wings.
Serve garnished with spring onions over white basmati rice or simply get your hands dirty and enjoy as they are.

recipes.Title: Tomato and mozzarella bread
recipes.Ingredients:
250 g strong white bread flour, plus extra for dusting
5 g salt
5 g instant yeast
1 tsp sugar
200 ml tepid water
1 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for sprinkling
Fine semolina or flour for dusting (optional)
10 cherry tomatoes, halved
1 ball of buffalo mozzarella, about 125g
1 pinch dried oregano for sprinkling
recipes.Preparation:
Oil a 1½ litre square plastic container.
Put the flour into the bowl of a mixer fitted with a dough hook. Add the salt. Measure out 200ml tepid water and dissolve in the sugar. Add the yeast and wait until the mix froths. Add three-quarters of the water and begin mixing on a slow speed. As the dough begins to come together, slowly add the remaining water. Mix for a further 5-8 minutes on a medium speed. The dough should now be wet and stretch easily when pulled. Add the olive oil and mix for another 2 minutes.
Put the dough into the oiled tub, cover and leave until at least doubled in size - about 1 hour.
Line a baking tray with baking parchment or silicone paper.
Dust your work surface heavily with flour - add some semolina too, if you have some. Tip the dough out carefully onto the surface. Rather than knocking it back, handle it gently so you keep as much air in the dough as possible. Coat the top with flour too. Cut the dough in half lengthways.
Stretch each piece of dough a little and lay the two breads on the prepared  tray, placing them apart. Push 10 tomato halves into the surface of each bread. Tear the mozzarella into little pieces and push them in between the tomatoes. Sprinkle each bread with olive oil, then oregano. Leave to rest for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, heat your oven to 210 °C.
Bake the breads for 15-20 minutes. Serve while still warm.

recipes.Title: Sticky soya and ginger pork fillet,
recipes.Ingredients:
For the marinade
4cm fresh root ginger, peeled and grated
2 garlic cloves, crushed
4 tbsp soy sauce
2 tbsp sweet chilli sauce
3 tbsp runny honey
For the pork
1 large pork fillet (about 600g/1lb 6oz), fully trimmed
4 spring onions, finely shredded into long, thin strips
1 red chilli, seeds removed and thinly sliced
2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander
salt and freshly ground black pepper
freshly steamed rice or cooked noodles, to serve
recipes.Preparation:
To make the marinade, place all of the ingredients in a bowl and mix well.

Place the fillet in the marinade. Season with salt and pepper and turn until the fillet is fully coated with marinade. Leave to marinate for a few hours in the fridge.

Preheat the oven to 220C/200C Fan/Gas 7 and line a small roasting tin with baking paper.

Removed the fillet from the marinade (reserving the marinade to use later) and place in the roasting tin. Roast for 25–30 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through. Remove the fillet from the roasting tin and set aside on a board to rest. Cover with foil and leave for 5 minutes before carving.

Place the reserved marinade in a small saucepan and place over a medium heat. Bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally. Carve the pork into slices and arrange on a serving platter. Pour the hot marinade over the top and scatter with the spring onions, chilli and coriander. Serve with rice or noodles.

recipes.Title: Bacon and cheese swirls
recipes.Ingredients:
250 g Self-raising flour, plus a little extra for dusting
0.5 tsp Table salt
75 g Unsalted butter, diced and cold, plus another 25g
50 ml Semi-skimmed or whole milk
8 Large rashers, shoulder or back bacon, rind removed
1 Medium onion, peeled and finely chopped
100 g Cream cheese
100 g Cheddar cheese, grated
0.5 Bunch flat-leaf parsley, chopped
1 Clove garlic, peeled and crushed
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to 180°C/gas mark 4
Place the flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl, then rub in the cold, diced butter using your hands
Add the milk gradually, while mixing until just combined. Turn out the dough on to a floured surface and roll into a rectangle 1cm thick
Melt the remaining unsalted butter in a small saucepan over a moderate heat. Brush the dough with some of the melted butter, and then layer the bacon on top, leaving a 2cm edge on one of the long sides of the dough
Mix the onion, cheese, parsley and garlic together and spread evenly over the bacon
Brush the bare edge of the dough with water, and then roll into a spiral, sealing the edge brushed with water to the body of the roll. Wrap the roll in cling film and refrigerate for 20 minutes
Cut the roll into slices and place, spiral side up, on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Bake for 15 minutes or until golden

recipes.Title: Meat loaf
recipes.Ingredients:
250 g onions, halved and diced
6 clove garlic, minced
50 g unsalted butter
500 g minced beef
500 g minced pork
40 g beef suet, finely grated
115 g bread, soaked in milk and when soft, really squeezed out
2 medium eggs, lightly beaten
2 generous pinches of thyme, chopped
3 tsp salt
2 tsp black pepper
1 pinch clove
1 tsp piri piri
100 g breadcrumbs, or enough to coat the loaf
recipes.Preparation:
Sweat the onions and garlic in butter over a low heat until they become soft and translucent. Season to taste and leave to cool.
Meanwhile in a large bowl, mix the beef, pork, suet, bread, eggs, thyme, the salt and some pepper. Mix thoroughly for a couple of minutes to tenderise.
When the onion-garlic mixture is cool, add to the meat and mix well so everything is evenly distributed.
On a clean surface, flatten and bash the meat mixture. Repeat several times to tenderise, then form a very smooth, tight loaf. Leave to rest in the fridge on a lined baking tray for at least 30 minutes. You can also leave this overnight in the fridge.
Preheat the oven to 180°C fan/gas mark 6.
Once rested, take the meat loaf from the fridge. Pour the breadcrumbs into a tray and roll the meat loaf in the crumbs. Wrap the loaf tightly in fresh greaseproof paper, making sure you put the fold on the bottom of the tray to prevent the paper from opening during cooking.
Cook for 50 minutes and then remove greaseproof paper. Turn up heat to 200°C /gas mark 7 and cook for an extra 10 minutes so the meat loaf turns a lovely golden brown.
Rest for 10 minutes, slice and serve.

recipes.Title: Russian mushroom julienne
recipes.Ingredients:
450g white button mushrooms, thinly sliced
60g thinly sliced onions
2 cloves garlic, minced
3 tablespoons butter, divided
60ml dry white wine
235g sour cream
salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
115g shredded Mozzarella cheese
recipes.Preparation:
Clean and slice mushrooms.
Preheat oven to 190°C
In a large pan melt the 2 tablespoons of butter. Next, add sliced mushrooms, onions, and garlic. Sauté on medium heat until mushrooms give out liquid and have reduced to about half the size. Drain the mushrooms and set aside.
In the same skillet, melt the remaining 1 tablespoon butter then add white wine. Simmer on medium heat for 2 minutes. Add the sour cream and mix to blend. Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in the mushrooms.
Pour the sauce with mushrooms into an 8x8-inch baking pan, or divide equally among 4 ramekins. Sprinkle with cheese and bake for 10 minutes or until the cheese is melted. Serve with crusty bread.
recipes.Keywords: mushroom, onion white wine, sour cream cheese

recipes.Title: Chicken Yakisoba
recipes.Ingredients:
SAUCE:
1½ tbsp. Worcestershire sauce
1 tbsp. soy sauce
1 tbsp. ketchup
1 tbsp. oyster sauce
1 tsp. sugar 

2 chicken breasts, cut into 4cm strips
Salt
Freshly ground black pepper
3 tbsp. vegetable oil
Small onion, sliced 
1 carrot, cut into 1/2cm planks 
½ green cabbage, roughly chopped
3 spring onions, cut in thirds 
30 g bean sprouts
450 g yakisoba noodles (ramen-style wheat noodles)
recipes.Preparation:
In a small bowl, whisk Worcestershire, soy, ketchup, oyster sauce, and sugar until combined and set aside. Season chicken strips liberally with salt and black pepper. In a heavy bottomed pan over medium-high heat, preheat 2 tbsp of oil. Add chicken and cook, turning occasionally, for 7 minutes until browned and just cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add 1 tbsp of oil to the pan before adding onion and carrot. Sauté until the carrots and onions are just softened, 3 minutes. Add in the cabbage, spring onions, and bean sprouts. Stir fry for 4 to 5 minutes until the cabbage has wilted slightly and some of the vegetables have begun to brown. Season with salt and pepper.
While the chicken and veggies are cooking, prepare the yakisoba noodles according to the package instructions but save any added seasoning packets or sauces for a later use. Make sure your noodles are thoroughly drained after cooking. When ready, add drained noodles to the pan, mix until the veggies are evenly distributed. Add the cooked chicken and yakisoba sauce and toss everything to coat. Stir fry for an additional 2 to 3 minutes until everything is mixed and the noodles start to brown in places. Serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Buddha noodles with chicken
recipes.Ingredients:
350 g packet udon noodles
3 tbsp. smooth peanut butter
3 tbsp. soy sauce
2 tbsp. sesame oil
1 tbsp. honey
1 tbsp. lime juice
1 clove garlic, crushed
250 g Shredded cooked chicken
350 g red and green capsicum
2 avocados, thinly sliced
2 spring onions, thinly sliced
1 tsp. sesame seeds
recipes.Preparation:
In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook noodles according to package instructions. Drain noodles and rinse with cold water to cool.
Return noodles to saucepan. Add peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, honey, lime juice and garlic. Stir until sauce is creamy and noodles are fully coated. If the sauce is too loose, turn heat to low and cook until the sauce has thickened, about 1 minute.
Divide noodles between bowls. Top each serving with chicken, peppers, avocado and spring onions. Garnish with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.Title: Steamed pork bun
recipes.Ingredients:
Ginger water:
60ml boiling water
25mm ginger, minced

Dough:
75ml warm water
1 tsp sugar
1 tsp yeast
110g plain flour
40g cornflour
1 tbsp sesame oil
salt

Filling:
150g minced pork
2 cloves garlic
½ tbsp oyster sauce
½ tbsp light soya sauce
½ tsp dark soya sauce
½ tbsp sherry
1 tsp cornstarch
½ tsp salt
½tsp sugar
black pepper
½ tbsp toasted sesame oil
chives
small chilli, finely chopped
recipes.Preparation:
Ginger water:
Mince the ginger and add to the boiling water.

Dough:
Add the sugar to the warm water, then add the yeast - stand for 5 minutes until bubbling.
Add the flour to the mixing bowl and pour the yeast water in as the mixer operates. Mix until an elastic ball is formed, about 15-18 minutes. Cover the bowl with clingfilm and prove until doubled in size.

Filling:
Add the ginger water to the pork in a mixing bowl. Add the rest of the ingredients down to the pepper. Beat everything together until the pork is even and sticky. Add the oil, chives and chilli and mix for a minute. Cover and refrigerate.

Buns:
Punch down the dough, roll into a sausage and divide into six pieces. Press each ball until a disc. Roll out the disc until it is about 4.5 in. wide, but thinner at the edges. Place about 2 tbsp filling into the centre. Make a series of pleats and then work the pleat in to the centre until the bun is formed.

Steam:
Line the steamer with baking parchment (with holes) and place the buns with 1in. gaps. Steam for 15 minutes. Stand for 2 minutes before opening.

recipes.Title: Prawn Gyoza
recipes.Ingredients:
For the gyoza skins:
100g strong white flour, plus extra for rolling
½ tsp fine salt
67ml boiling water
1 tbsp vegetable oil, for frying
1 tbsp sesame oil

100g cooked, peeled North Atlantic prawns, chopped
½ tsp fine salt
½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
½ tbsp sesame oil
½ lemon, zest only, finely grated
1 tbsp oyster sauce
1 tbsp chopped spring onion
1cm piece fresh root ginger, peeled, grated
recipes.Preparation:
For the gyoza skins, sift the flour into a large bowl and mix in the salt. Stir in the boiling water using a knife or a pair of chopsticks until the mixture comes together as a dough. (You many not need to use all of the water.) Roll the dough into a ball, cover with cling film and set aside to rest for one hour.
Turn out the dough onto a lightly floured work surface and knead for five minutes until smooth and elastic. (You can use the dough hook attachment of a food processor for this.)
Roll out one of the balls onto a lightly floured work surface, stretching and turning the dough as you go, until the gyoza dough is as thin as possible. Using a 10cm/4in cookie cutter, cut discs from the gyoza dough and stack them on top of each other, dusting the top of each with a little flour before adding the next one. Repeat the rolling and cutting process until all of the dough has been used.

For the prawn filling, mix prawn filling ingredients together in a large mixing bowl until well combined (the ingredients will form a gloopy paste). Season well with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Chill in the fridge until needed.

To assemble the dumplings, hold a gyoza skin in the palm of your hand and add one teaspoon of the filling mixture. Wet the edges with a little water using your fingertip and seal the dumpling, pinching along the edges to create a pleated fan effect (the end result should resemble a mini Cornish pasty).

To cook the dumplings, heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan with a lid over a high heat. Arrange the gyoza in the pan, in batches if necessary, leaving space between each one, and fry for 2-3 minutes, or until the bottoms are golden-brown. Take care as they will burn quickly. Remove from the pan and transfer to the steamer. Steam the dumplings for a further two minutes.

recipes.Title: Salmon devilled eggs
recipes.Ingredients:
2 large free-range eggs
7g smoked salmon
1 sprig of fresh dill , plus extra for serving
1 pinch of cayenne pepper
MAYONNAISE
1 large free-range egg yolk
2 teaspoons Dijon mustard
1/2 lemon , (20ml juice)
100 ml olive oil
100 ml sunflower oil
recipes.Preparation:
In a saucepan, cover the eggs with cold water and bring to the boil over a high heat.
Simmer for 6 minutes, then drainand place the eggs in cold water to cool.
Peel and halve them lengthways, scoop the yolks into a bowl and roughly mash. Set aside.
Make your mayonnaise. In a bowl, whisk the egg yolk, mustard and lemon juice with an electric whisk until frothy.
Combine the oils in a jug, then drizzle them into the egg mixture, whisking constantly until combined. Season to taste with sea salt and black pepper.
Add 60g of mayo to the egg yolks (refrigerate the rest for up to a few days).
Finely chop and stir in the salmon and dill fronds, then add the cayenne pepper and mash to combine.
Spoon into the egg whites, top with extra dill and serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Love dumplings
recipes.Ingredients:
200 g raw peeled prawns
1 large shallot
2 cloves of garlic
4 spring onions
½ a bunch of fresh coriander
16 round dumpling wrappers

DIPPING SAUCE
½ fresh red chilli
½ lime
2 tablespoons caster sugar
2 tablespoons fish sauce
recipes.Preparation:
Start by making the dipping sauce. Finely chop the chilli, then combine with the lime juice (about 2 tablespoons), sugar, fish sauce and 8 tablespoons of water. Pour into a bowl for dunking.
Smash the prawns with the side of your knife, then finely chop them. Peel and very finely chop the shallot and garlic, then trim and finely slice the spring onions (keep the white and green parts separate). Pick and finely chop the coriander leaves.
Put the prawns, shallot, garlic, coriander and the whites of the spring onions in a bowl, generously season with black pepper and a pinch of salt, and give it a good mix.
Lay out your wrappers and spoon a teaspoon of filling into the middle of each. Brush the edges of one wrapper with water, fold it in half, then pleat and pinch the edges together to secure. Repeat with the others.

Place an oiled pan over a medium heat, add the dumplings and fry for 2 minutes. Then transfer to a steamer and steam for 10 minutes.

recipes.Title: BBQ chicken dim sum
recipes.Ingredients:
For the casing -
65g All-purpose flour + extra for dusting
80g Boiling water
Salt to taste

For the filling -
125g Chicken mince
1 tbsp oyster sauce
½ Carrot, small, finely minced
3 cloves Garlic, minced
1 shallot, finely chopped
smoky BBQ seasoning, to taste
Salt and pepper to taste

Dipping Sauce
2 tbsp Light soy sauce
2 Red chillies
¼ tbsp Sesame oil
½ tbsp Chopped spring onion
recipes.Preparation:
First make the dough. In a large bowl mix the flour and salt. Now add boiling water gradually and start mixing it using a wooden spoon.
When the dough becomes cool enough to handle, start kneading it with hand. Add some dry flour if it gets sticky and continue kneading until it becomes soft.
Cover it with a damp kitchen towel and keep it aside for 30 minutes.
Next prepare the filling. Add chicken mince, chopped carrots, chopped leeks, minced garlic and chopped green onion in a large bowl and mix them together with a light hand. Season with soy sauce, salt and black pepper to taste. Mix well.
Now it’s time to make the casing. Tip out the dough on a flat surface and knead it again. Take small ball of dough of about 1 inch diameter. Roll it into a thin round disc of about 2 inches diameter and about ¼ centimeter thick. Make sure the casing is thin, else it will not cook thoroughly and will not let the chicken cook evenly.
Now let’s stuff the chicken dim sum. Take about a tablespoon of the chicken filling and place the filling in the center of the disc. Now shape the dim sum by squeezing the sides of dough disc.
Once all the dim sums are shaped, steam them on medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes. Keep the steamer covered during steaming. (If you don’t have a steamer, boil water in a sauce pan and place a stainless steel sieve or colander over it. Cover the tiny holes of the sieve with some cabbage leaves and place the dim sums on top. Cover the dim sums with a dome-shaped lid and start steaming.)
While the chicken dim sums are steaming, make the dipping sauce by mixing the light soy sauce, spring onion greens, finely chopped red chilles and sesame oil. Whisk them thoroughly and reserve until serving.
After the chicken dim sums are thoroughly cooked (you can check by inserting a toothpick at the center of a dim sum and it should come out clean), take them out and garnish with greens of spring onions. Serve the hot chicken dim sum along with soy chilli dipping sauce.

recipes.Title: Chinese BBQ sauce
recipes.Ingredients:
3 minced fresh garlic cloves
1piece fresh ginger, minced
120 ml hoisin sauce
60 ml sherry wine
60 ml soy sauce (low-sodium works too-)
50 g sugar
½ teaspoon Chinese five spice powder
3 teaspoons red food coloring
recipes.Preparation:
Mix all ingredients in a bowl,( or a jar with a tight fitting lid), until the sugar is dissolved. Refrigerate until you are ready to use it.
For a dipping sauce, bring it to a full rolling boil, over med. heat, then reduce the heat to low, and simmer until it is thick, and slightly reduced.
For a marinade, marinate meat for 4-24 hours, turning once every two hours. You then grill or roast the meat until it is cooked through,(and slightly charred- this adds to the flavor!).

recipes.Title: Tomato pie
recipes.Ingredients:
230mm diam.pie shell
7 ripe tomatoes, sliced
1 yellow onion
178ml mayonnaise
28g shredded mozzarella cheese
28g grated Parmesan cheese
ground black pepper to taste
2 teaspoons fresh basil
2 teaspoons fresh oregano
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat oven to 175 degreesr°C.

Bake the pastry shell for 8 to 10 minutes or until browned.

Slice onion and place in the bottom of pastry shell. Slice tomatoes and arrange over onions. Add black pepper to taste.

In a medium bowl, combine mozzarella, parmesan and mayonnaise. Spread this mixture evenly over tomatoes.

Bake at 175 degrees°C for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown. Once cooked, garnish with fresh herbs.

recipes.Title: Sweet potato, feta and red onion frittata
recipes.Ingredients:
300 g sweet potato, peeled and cut into 1cm (½in) cubes
1 tbsp butter
1 tbsp olive oil
2 red onions, very thinly sliced
1 garlic clove
1 tsp thyme leaves, plus small sprigs to serve
1 tbsp balsamic vinegar
1 tbsp flat-leaf parsley, chopped, plus extra to serve
6 large eggs, beaten and liberally seasoned
125 g feta
recipes.Preparation:
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and cook the sweet potato for 8-10 minutes or until tender. Drain well.
While the potato is cooking, heat the butter and olive oil in a large, ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat and add the red onions. Fry the onions for 8 minutes until nicely caramelised and soft.
Add the garlic, thyme and balsamic vinegar and fry for a further 2 minutes until the garlic is fragrant and the vinegar has evaporated.
Stir the parsley through the onions, then scatter the sweet potatoes around the pan.
Pour over the beaten egg and swirl it around to fully cover the base of the pan. Break the feta into chunks and scatter over the egg.
Cook over a low heat for 5-6 minutes until the sides and the underside of the frittata are starting to look set.
Transfer to a hot grill for 3-4 minutes or until the top of the frittata is golden and it is set all the way through. Scatter over some thyme and parsley to serve.
recipes.Keywords: sweet potato, red onion, eggs, feta cheese

recipes.Title: Chinese roasted pork ribs
recipes.Ingredients:
For the marinade
1 x 5cm (2in) ginger, finely chopped
4 garlic cloves, finely chopped
60 ml hoisin sauce
1 x quarter of a teaspoon chilli powder
1 tbsp light soy sauce
1 tsp white sugar
1 x eighth of a teaspoon of ground white pepper
1 x quarter of a teaspoon salt
1 tsp oyster sauce
1 tbsp Shaoxing rice wine
1 tbsp sesame oil

For the ribs
1 kg pork ribs
1 tbsp oil
