Add the cloves, stick of cinnamon and the lemon strips. Gently bring the mixture to the boil over a medium heat, then reduce the heat a little and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened. Remove from the heat and leave to one side to cool. Stir in the rose water to taste, if using.
For the custard, start by heating the milk with 200ml of the double cream, the remaining 250g of caster sugar and the vanilla paste in a large saucepan over a medium heat. When it is hot, but not boiling, slowly pour in the semolina, whisking constantly, until it is all incorporated. Reduce the heat a little and keep whisking until you have a thickened, smooth custard.
Whisk in 75g of the butter, and leave to cool for 10-15 minutes. After this time, whisk in the remaining double cream and the eggs until smooth.
When everything is ready, assemble your galaktoboureko. Preheat the oven to 170°C fan and melt the remaining 125g of butter in a saucepan. Take the filo out of the fridge and drape with a slightly damp tea towel to stop it drying out while you work. Lightly butter a 25cm x 30cm deep roasting tray, then brush each sheet of filo with butter and line the tin. You’ll want to use ¾ of the sheets to line the base and sides of the tin, leaving any excess hanging over the edge. Once it is ready, fill with the semolina and smooth it out with a spatula. Fold over any overhanging pastry, then top with the final few sheets, making sure they are well buttered also.
Cut the pie into segments, using a serrated knife (you need to do this before baking), place the tray in the hot oven and bake for about 45 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Remove from the oven and immediately and evenly pour over the cooled syrup. Set aside to cool completely, and for the custard-filled pastry to soak up the syrup.

recipes.Title: Pork ribs, baked with rice
recipes.Ingredients:
8 pork belly ribs
2 tsp ground cumin (flat tsp)
½ tsp ground cinnamon
½ tsp paprika
½ tsp grated nutmeg
2 tsp fennel seeds, chopped or crushed using a pestle and mortar
2 tbsp mixed sesame and veg. oils

For the rice:
2 onions, finely chopped
4 large garlic cloves, crushed
250g long-grain rice
700ml chicken stock
a few sprigs of oregano or marjoram, chopped

For the beans:
150g broad beans (podded weight)
30g butter
1 tbsp chopped parsley
recipes.Preparation:
Put the ribs in a large lidded ovenproof pan or dish, season generously and sprinkle over the spices and oil; mix well to cover all the ribs. Stand for a 2 hours. Preheat the oven to 200°C fan. Plave the ribs in the oven uncovered for 10 minutes, until the ribs start to colour. Reduce the oven temperature to 170°C fan and cover the pan or dish. Cook for a further 35 minutes, turning every so often.
Remove from the oven and transfer the ribs to a plate. 
To make the rice, spoon out most of the fat from the pan you cooked the ribs in, leaving about 3 tbsp. Add the onions and garlic and fry over a low heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently so they don’t colour too much. Add the rice and chicken stock, and mix well. Season then bring to the boil and scatter over the oregano or marjoram.  
Turn down the heat and place the ribs on top of the rice. Cover with the lid and return to the oven for 40 minutes, or until the rice is tender.
Meanwhile, cook the broad beans in a pan of boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes, then drain. Add the butter and parsley and stir until melted, about 1 minute. Season to taste then spoon over the ribs to serve.

recipes.Title: Thai chicken soup 2
recipes.Ingredients:
1 small onion, cut into crescent-moon shaped slices
1 tbsp groundnut or rapeseed oil
2 shallots, finely chopped
2cm cube of fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped
1 medium-sized red chillies, deseeded and cut into strips
2 fat lemongrass stalks, tough outer leaves removed and core chopped
4 garlic cloves, finely chopped
750ml chicken stock
200g creamed coconut (in the block)
150g small waxy potatoes, cut in half
10ml fish sauce
1 tbsp soft light-brown sugar
juice of 1 lime
200g chicken breast fillet, cut into thin strips
4 kaffir lime leaves
8g Thai basil leaves
5g mint leaves
1 red bird’s-eye chilli, deseeded and thinly sliced
recipes.Preparation:
In a large pan, sauté the onion in the oil until just colouring. 
Put the shallots, ginger, red chilli, lemongrass and garlic into a food processor with 3 tbsp water and whizz to a paste.
Add to the onions and cook for a further 2 minutes.
Add the chicken stock and bring it up to the boil. 
Turn down to a simmer and add the creamed coconut. Stir to help melt the coconut in the stock.
Put the potatoes into the pan, along with the fish sauce, sugar and the juice of one of the limes. Let the soup simmer (but not boil) until the potatoes are tender – about 12 minutes.
Add the chicken, which will cook in just 2 minutes, and the lime leaves. 
Tear the basil and mint leaves and add to the soup, with the bird’seye chillies and the juice of the other lime.
Taste - it shouldn’t need salt or pepper but should be hot, sour, salty and sweet. Adjust this balance if you need to.

recipes.Title: Mackerel Szechuan style
recipes.Ingredients:
For the potato salad:
200g waxy potatoes
2 large shallots, thinly sliced
3 tbsp rice vinegar

For the fish:
2 medium whole mackerel
1 tbsp dried red chillies, sliced, or 1 tbsp chilli flakes
1½ tbsp Sichuan peppercorns
125ml corn oil
25ml sesame oil
a handful of leafy herbs, to garnish (I used Vietnamese coriander)
recipes.Preparation:
Finely shred the potatoes using a mandoline with a julienne blade, or slice them as thinly as possible, then cut into matchsticks. Soak in a bowl of cold water for 2-3 minutes then rinse to remove any excess starch.
Meanwhile, remove the heads and guts from the mackerel and wash thoroughly. Score the mackerel 4-5 times on one side.
Add the shredded potatoes to a pan of salted boiling water and simmer for 1 minute, or until the potatoes are just cooked. Drain and leave to cool. 
Heat the chillies, Sichuan peppercorns and both the oils in a large, deep frying pan set over a medium heat until the oil begins to bubble. Carefully lower in the scored mackerel and cook for 2-3 minutes, then carefully turn them over. Cook for a further 2-3 minutes, basting the mackerel with the chilli oil. Use a spatula to remove them from the oil on to a serving plate. 
Spoon 2 tbsp of the mackerel cooking oil into a second pan over a medium heat. Add the sliced onion and fry gently for 2-3 minutes until soft. Add the cooked potato and toss together. Stir through the rice vinegar and season. 
Place the mackerel on 2 plates and arrange the potato salad next to the fish. Spoon over some of the chilli and Sichuan-pepper oil and sprinkle with a little sea salt. Garnish with the herbs.

recipes.Title: Pollo assado
recipes.Ingredients:
1.3 kg chicken thighs or legs, trimmed of excess skin and fat (boneless and skinless, or bone-in and skin-on)
3 cloves garlic, minced
68ml orange juice (about 1 medium orange)
2 tbsp achiote paste (about 1.5 ounces)
2 tbsp olive oil
1 tbsp lime juice (about ½ lime)
1 tbsp white wine vinegar
1 tbsp ground coriander
1 tbsp salt
2 tsp smoked paprika
2 tsp dried oregano
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 tsp ground cumin
¼ teaspoon ground cloves
Vegetable oil, for greasing grill
recipes.Preparation:
Add all ingredients except the chicken in a small bowl. Whisk to combine.
Place the chicken in a large ziploc bag or baking dish and add the marinade. Close the bag, massage together to coat, and refrigerate for 2 to 6 hours. (Do not marinate longer than 8 hours, or the chicken will get mealy and begin to break down.)
Preheat the grill to high heat for direct cooking. Grease the preheated grill grates to prevent sticking by wiping them down with a folded paper towel that's been soaked in vegetable oil.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and shake off any excess liquid. Grill the chicken skin side down over direct heat for about 5-7 minutes, with the lid closed as much as possible, until the skin is crispy and golden. Flip and grill for an additional 5-7 minutes, until the meat is firm and the internal temperature registers 165°F.
Serve pollo asado with warm corn tortillas or flour tortillas and Mexican rice.

recipes.Title: Chicken enchiladas
recipes.Ingredients:
White Enchilada Sauce:
40 g butter (3 tablespoons)
40 g plain white flour / all-purpose flour (5 tablespoons)
150 ml sour cream 
300 ml chicken stock
3 jalapenos (diced)
½ tsp cumin
¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper
½ teaspoon salt

Chicken Filling:
400 g cooked and shredded chicken 
150 g frozen or canned sweetcorn 
4 spring onions (sliced)
100 g grated cheddar cheese 
½ teaspoon salt
¼ teaspoon pepper
8 flour tortillas (for wrapping)

For Topping
100 g shredded mozzarella 
cilantro/coriander (chopped)
recipes.Preparation:
Preparing the White Sauce for Enchiladas:
In a medium-sized saucepan, melt the unsalted butter over medium heat. Once the butter has melted, add the all-purpose flour and whisk continuously for about a minute to create a roux. Slowly and gradually pour in the chicken broth while whisking vigorously to prevent any lumps from forming. Continue cooking and whisking until the mixture thickens. Stir in the diced jalapeños, and season with cumin, salt, and pepper. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the sour cream. Keep stirring until the sour cream is incorporated and the sauce is smooth and creamy. Remove from the heat, and set it aside while preparing the chicken filling.
Preparing the Chicken Filling and Assembling the Dish:
In a medium-sized bowl, mix together cooked and shredded chicken with sliced green onions, sweetcorn, ¼ of the creamy white sauce, and grated cheese along with salt, and freshly ground black pepper. Preheat your oven to 180 °C . Prepare your baking dish by spreading a generous spoonful of white sauce on the bottom to prevent the tortillas from sticking. Take a tortilla and spoon a generous amount of the chicken filling onto the center of the tortilla. Roll it up tightly and place it seam-side down in a prepared baking dish. Repeat this process with the remaining tortillas and filling until the baking dish is filled with enchiladas.
Baking and Serving the Enchiladas:
Pour the prepared white sauce evenly over the enchiladas, making sure to cover them entirely. The creamy white sauce will add a velvety richness to the dish. Sprinkle the 100 grams of shredded mozzarella or any other melty cheese such as Monterey Jack or Gruyère cheese on top, creating a deliciously gooey layer that will melt to perfection in the oven.

Place the baking dish in the preheated oven and bake for approximately 30 minutes, or until the cheese is golden and bubbling.
Once the enchiladas are baked to perfection, remove them from the oven and let them cool for a few minutes.
Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro, adding a burst of freshness and color to the dish. The vibrant green cilantro will beautifully complement the creamy white sauce and the enticing flavors of the chicken filling.
recipes.Keywords: chicken, sour cream, sweet corn, cheese, tortillas

recipes.Title: Chicken, Tuscan style
recipes.Ingredients:
6 large skinless chicken thighs, bone in (see tip)
2 tbsp plain flour
2 tsp paprika
2 tbsp olive or sunflower oil
1 large onion, finely chopped
1 large red pepper, deseeded and finely chopped
2 garlic cloves, crushed
2 tsp tomato purée
30g sun-blushed tomatoes, chopped (sun dried)
150ml white wine
150ml chicken stock
150ml pouring double cream
150g baby spinach
55g Parmesan, grated
salt and freshly ground black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Place the chicken in a bowl. Add the flour and the paprika and season well with salt and pepper. Toss together to coat the chicken.

Heat the oil in large, deep frying pan over a high heat. Add the chicken and fry for 3-4 minutes on each side, until browned and crisp. Set aside.

Add the onion and pepper to the unwashed pan and fry for 4-5 minutes over a medium heat, until soft (you may need to add a little extra oil). Add the garlic and fry for 30 seconds.

Stir in the tomato purée, tomatoes, wine and stock. Bring to the boil then return the chicken to the pan along with any resting juices. Cover, reduce the heat, and simmer for about 30 minutes, until tender.

Add the cream and spinach and stir until wilted. Remove from the heat, sprinkle in the Parmesan and serve piping hot.

recipes.Title: Lamb dopiaza
recipes.Ingredients:
4 tbsp Vegetable oil (use 5 tbsp if your lamb is quite lean)
3 Green cardamom pods
1 Cinnamon stick (2.5cm)
4 Cloves
8 Black peppercorns
2 Smallish onions (1.5 chopped and 0.5 sliced)
2 Large tomatoes, quartered
10 g Fresh root ginger, peeled weight
5 Large garlic cloves
½ tsp Turmeric
1 tsp Ground cumin
1½ tsp Ground coriander
1 tsp Garam masala
½ tsp Chilli powder
1 Pinch salt, to taste
4 tbsp Greek yogurt
500 g Leg of lamb, cubed
1 Good squeeze lemon juice, to taste
1 Good handful of chopped fresh coriander leaves
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oil in a non-stick saucepan. Add the whole spices and, once they have sizzled a bit, add the chopped onions and cook until browned; the darker the onion, the deeper the flavour.
Meanwhile, make a fine paste of the tomatoes, ginger and garlic using a hand blender. Stir in the powdered spices, salt and yogurt until smooth.
Add the lamb to the pan and seal the outsides. Add the tomato-yogurt paste and bring to the boil while stirring very often. Then reduce the heat, cover and cook for 45-50 minutes, or until the lamb is tender. Add the sliced onions 30 minutes into the cooking process and give the pot a stir every 10-15 minutes, making sure it does not dry out. Ideally, the dish should cook in its own sauce but, if necessary, add a splash of water.
By the time the lamb is tender, the sauce should have reduced to a creamy consistency with a tangle of sweet, sliced onions. If it is too dry, add a splash of water. Taste and add more salt, chilli powder or lemon juice, as you prefer, until it is perfect for you. Stir in the chopped coriander and serve with Paratha, Chapati or Naan bread.

recipes.Title: Roast lamb with pecorino
recipes.Ingredients:
120 g pecorino cheese, finely grated
6 garlic cloves, finely grated
1 pinch each of sea salt flakes and freshly ground black pepper
3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus more if needed
1 handful leaves from a small bunch of basil, plus more to serve (optional)
1.8 kg leg of lamb
2 medium red onions, cut into wedges
600 g small waxy potatoes, scrubbed, then halved or quartered, depending on size
350 g red and yellow tomatoes, halved or quartered
250 ml white wine
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to 240°C.
Put the cheese, garlic and some salt into a mortar and pound to a rough purée, gradually adding the olive oil. Tear the basil leaves, add them to the mortar and pound them too.
Place the leg of lamb in a roasting tin. Make deep incisions all over it and push the paste from the mortar down into them. You can also loosen the meat around the bone to make a pocket and push the paste into that, too. Season all over and put into the oven.
Roast for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 200°C
Add the onions, potatoes and tomatoes to the roasting tin, toss them in the fat in the pan, adding a little more oil if it’s needed to moisten them, then season and roast for a final 45 minutes, adding the wine after 20 minutes. The lamb will be pink. If you prefer it more well done, cook it for a little longer.
Remove the lamb to a plate, cover with foil, insulate well (you could use old towels or tea towels) and leave to rest for 15 minutes. If the potatoes are tender, cover them and keep warm in a low oven while the lamb rests. If they’re still a bit firm, increase the oven temperature to 220°C, return the vegetables to the oven, uncovered, and cook until they’re ready.
Serve the lamb with the potatoes, tomatoes and onions, scattered with a few basil leaves, if you like.

recipes.Title: Falafels
recipes.Ingredients:
200g dried chickpeas,
2 cloves of garlic,
1 small onion, chopped,
2 tablespoons chopped fresh coriander, parsley, or mint,
1 tablespoon ground cumin,
1 teaspoon ground coriander,
1 teaspoon dried mint (can be mint tea),
½ teaspoon salt,
½ teaspoon pepper,
½ teaspoon bicarbonate of soda,
2 tablespoons chickpea flour or wheat flour,
oil for deep frying.
recipes.Preparation:
Soak the chickpeas: Avoid using canned chickpeas - they are too soft and the falafels may fall apart. Cover the dried chickpeas with cold water and let them sit for at least 12 hours, preferably overnight. Then drain them thoroughly and dry on a paper towel.
Prepare the mixture: Combine the soaked chickpeas, garlic, onion, chopped herbs, and spices in a food processor. Add bicarbonate of soda and flour. Blend on high speed for 2-4 minutes until the mixture becomes uniform and slightly sticky. If it is too dry, you can add a bit of water.
Chill the mixture: Cover the bowl with cling film and place it in the refrigerator for at least an hour. This allows the mixture to set, making the falafels easier to form and better at holding their shape during frying.
Shape the falafels: If you have a special falafel mould, use it to shape the perfect patties. If not, wet your hands with water and form balls about the size of a walnut. This prevents the mixture from sticking to your hands.
Frying: Pour a generous amount of oil into a pot or deep pan - the layer should be about 2.5-5cm deep. Heat the oil to about 180°C (you can check by dropping a small piece of the mixture in - if it starts frying immediately, the oil is ready). Fry the falafels in batches for 2-3 minutes on each side until they become golden and crispy. Do not add too many at once, as they will lower the oil temperature and fry unevenly.

recipes.Title: Mexican pancakes
recipes.Ingredients:
Ingredients for pancakes:                      

250 grams of all-purpose flour,
2 eggs,
500 millilitres of milk,
350 millilitres of sparkling water,
1 pinch of salt,
1 tablespoon of oil.

Ingredients for stuffing:  
1 onion,
1 red bell pepper,
2 cloves of garlic,
200 grams of minced beef,
1 teaspoon of hot paprika powder,
1 teaspoon of ground cumin,
1 teaspoon of sweet paprika,
1 teaspoon of salt,
1 teaspoon of pepper,
1 tablespoon of oil,
250 grams of grated cheese.
recipes.Preparation:
Start by preparing the pancake batter. Place all the ingredients in a bowl and mix thoroughly to avoid lumps.
Let the batter rest for 20 minutes, then cook the pancakes in a heated pan.
Prepare the stuffing: heat oil in a pan, add chopped onion, chopped bell pepper, and minced garlic. Sauté until the ingredients are translucent.
Add the meat and cook until it turns brown.
Add the spices and mix thoroughly.
Place a portion of stuffing on the cooked pancake, sprinkle with grated cheese, and wrap.
Cook the finished pancakes in the pan so that the cheese melts, or bake them in the oven with tomato sauce and cheese.

recipes.Title: Lamb shank curry
recipes.Ingredients:
2 lamb shanks
plain flour, for dusting
2 tbsp vegetable or corn oil
1 tsp coarsely ground black pepper
black seeds from 6 or so green cardamom pods (or substitute ¼ tsp ground cardamom)
1 black cardamom pod (optional)
small piece of cinnamon or cassia stick
1 tsp fenugreek seeds
1 tsp black or yellow mustard seeds
1 tsp cumin seeds
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp fennel seeds
1 tsp ground turmeric (or 1 tbsp freshly grated)
1 tbsp ghee
1 medium onion, finely chopped
2 medium green chillies, finely chopped, seeds and all
6 garlic cloves, crushed
20g ginger, scraped and finely grated
pinch of saffron
1 tbsp dried fenugreek leaves or kasoori methi
1 tbsp curry leaves
1 tbsp tomato purée
600ml lamb or beef stock
1 dsp tamarind paste
3 tbsp peanut butter
2 tbsp chopped coriander leaves
recipes.Preparation:
Season the lamb shanks and lightly dust with plain flour. Heat  vegetable or corn oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and fry the shanks for a few minutes, turning them regularly until nicely coloured.
Meanwhile, put the spices, up to and including ground turmeric, in a large lidded ovenproof casserole dish or wide sauté pan. Cook over a medium heat for 2-3 minutes, turning regularly with a spoon until they are lightly browned.
Add the ghee, a finely chopped medium onion, the chopped green chilli,  crushed garlic cloves, ginger, pinch saffron,  fenugreek leaves and curry leaves, and cook with a lid on for 4-5 minutes until the onions have softened, stirring every so often.
Add tomato purée, the lamb or beef stock and tamarind paste, bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the lamb and top up with a little more stock if needed so the shanks just submerge. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid and simmer gently for 1-1½ hours or until the shanks are almost tender, turning them once or twice and topping up with a little water if necessary.
Remove the lid and simmer for a further 30 minutes to reduce the sauce until the lamb is tender but still holding its shape. Take a ladle of the sauce and blend in a liquidiser until smooth. Return to the pan with 3 tbsp peanut butter and stir through over a low heat.  If the sauce isn’t thick enough remove the lamb and simmer until it thickens.
Transfer to a serving dish and scatter with 2-3 tbsp chopped coriander leaves. Serve with basmati rice.

recipes.Title: Chicken, Paprikas csirke
recipes.Ingredients:
450 g chicken breast,
4 tablespoons of oil or butter,
1 large onion,
60 ml Hungarian sweet paprika (about 4 tablespoons),
2 tablespoons of flour,
350 ml of chicken broth,
250 ml of cream,
1 teaspoon of lemon juice,
Salt and pepper to taste.
recipes.Preparation:
Cut the chicken into pieces and sauté in 2 tablespoons of heated fat until it is white on the outside. Then transfer it to a plate lined with paper towels.
In the same pan, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of fat and add the onion sliced into thin half-moons. Sauté on low heat until it becomes translucent.
Next, add the paprika and flour, and sauté briefly, stirring constantly to avoid burning the spices.
Pour in the broth and mix thoroughly to eliminate any lumps. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
When the broth starts to boil, add the chicken, reduce the heat, and simmer covered for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
After this time, remove the chicken from the sauce and transfer it into a separate dish. Add the cream and lemon juice to the sauce, mix, and season to taste.
Place the chicken back into the sauce and heat for a few minutes.

recipes.Title: Lamb byriani (Hyderebadi)
recipes.Ingredients:
For the Marinade:
1 tablespoon garlic and ginger paste
1 teaspoon chilli powder or flaked chilli
1 teaspoon ground turmeric
2 teaspoon garam masala
200 g natural yogurt
½ teaspoon salt
500 g diced lamb
For the Curry Sauce:
20 g ghee
3 large onions (sliced)
3 green cardamoms (slightly crushed)
1 small cinnamon stick
2 bay leaves
1 teaspoon chilli powder or flaked chilli (adjust to your taste)
1 teaspoon garam masala
½ teaspoon turmeric
½ teaspoon mace (optional)
½ bunch coriander (chopped)
1 chilli (chopped)
250 ml chicken stock or lamb stock
salt to taste
For the Rice:
300 g basmati rice
50 ml fresh lemon or lime juice
1 teaspoon salt
2 green cardamoms (slightly crushed)
750 ml cold water (3 cups)
50 ml milk
pinch of saffron (optional)
recipes.Preparation:
Marinating the Lamb:
Mix garlic and ginger paste, chilli powder or flaked chilli, ground turmeric, salt, garam masala and natural yoghurt in a large bowl.
Mix until combined and add the diced lamb. Make sure all the lamb pieces are covered with marinade.
Cover the bowl with cling film or a lid and let it marinate in the fridge preferably overnight or for a minimum of 5 hours.
Cooking the Lamb Curry:
Put a heavy-based pan or a Dutch oven on medium heat and melt the ghee.
Add sliced onions and sauté them until caramelised and get really dark brown but not burnt. This would take around 20 to 30 minutes. Spare half of the caramelised onions on a plate and set them aside to use later for garnishing the biryani.
Add cardamoms, cinnamon sticks, bay leaves, flaked chilli, garam masala, mace (optional) and turmeric to the pan, and sauté for 40 seconds. Stir continuously to make sure they don’t get burnt. Add the mutton along with the marinade, the chicken stock or the lamb stock, coriander, and the chilli. Mix well and turn the heat to high to bring the mixture to a boil.
When it boils, lower the heat, close the lid and let it simmer for one hour or until the mutton is tender, stirring occasionally. Stir occasionally to avoid it sticking to the bottom of the pan.
Cooking the Rice:
While the mutton is cooking, prepare the rice. Wash the rice in a sieve under running cold water until the water from the rice is no longer cloudy. Soak the rice in room temperature water for 20 minutes. Drain the water and place the rice along with the lime or lemon juice, salt, cardamoms and water in a large saucepan. Bring it to a boil over medium heat and cook for 2 minutes. Strain the rice and discard the cooking liquid.
Layering the Mutton Biryani:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Warm the milk, add the saffron (if using) to infuse for about 10 minutes and set it aside to garnish the biryani. When the meat is tender enough, check the seasoning and add some salt if needed. Remove from the heat and spread the precooked rice on the top of the curry with the back of a spoon, making sure the rice totally covers the curry.
Garnish the top of the rice with the reserved caramelized onions and sprinkle on the milk infused with saffron. Tightly cover the pan or the Dutch oven with tin foil then place the lid over the foil. Cook in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. Remove the pan from the oven and let it rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.Title: Australian meat pie
recipes.Ingredients:
For the dough:
300 g flour
100 g butter
60 ml milk (warm)
60 ml water (warm)
0.5 teaspoon salt

For the filling:
500 g beef , minced or cut into fine pieces
50 g bacon , finely chopped
25 g butter
1 large onion , finely chopped
100 ml red wine
150 ml beef broth
2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce
1 tablespoon ketchup
1 tablespoon cornstarch
1 tablespoon water
0.5 bunch parsley , finely chopped
2 pinches of grated nutmeg
Salt
Freshly ground pepper
To brush the dough:
1 egg yolk
1 tablespoon milk
Ketchup
recipes.Preparation:
Dough:
Bring water and milk to boil. Add the butter and melt. Mix the flour and salt separately and add the liquids. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface and form a smooth, soft dough. Cover the dough and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Filling:
Sear the meat in butter and set aside. Sauté the bacon and then the onion. Add the meat and sauté for 5 minutes over medium / high heat, stirring constantly. Deglaze with red wine and stir well. Add broth, Worcestershire sauce, ketchup and nutmeg. Cover and braise for 1 hour. Dissolve the cornstarch in the tablespoon of water, and add to the meat. Add parsley. Add salt and pepper.
Simmer for another 2 minutes. Turn off the heat. Remove excess sauce and set aside. Cool meat completely.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Roll dough to about 3mm thick on a lightly floured surface. Cut four 15cm diameter circles with a cookie cutter. Place circle of dough inside buttered molds. Fill with meat and a little sauce. Reserve remaining sauce. Fold the edges over the filling. Gather the remaining dough and roll it again. Cut four 12cm diameter circles with a cookie cutter. Make a small x with a knife at the center of each circle. Place on the filling, and press edges so that the two layers of dough adhere. Beat the egg yolk and milk. Brush the pies and the edges with the mixture. Bake in the middle of the oven for 40 minutes.
Serve the Australian meat pies hot with ketchup on top. Serve the reserved sauce separately.

recipes.Title: Chicken stew, Thai style
recipes.Ingredients:
Chicken Casserole:
600 gram chicken breast
2 tablespoon butter for frying
300 ml coconut milk
150 ml water
1 cube chicken broth
2 tsp. red curry paste more for a stronger version
1 tsp. brown sugar
1 tbsp fish sauce
½ tbsp lime juice
1 red bell pepper cut into cubes
Pickled Cucumber:
1 Cucumber
1 Squash
4 tablespoon white wine vinegar
½ tsp salt
Pepper, freshly ground
1½ tbsp sugar
100 ml water
1 tbsp fresh rosemary, chopped
recipes.Preparation:
Cut the chicken into smaller pieces and brown them in butter in a pot until slightly golden.
Add all other ingredients and let it simmer for about 10 minutes.
Cucumber Salad:
Slice the cucumber thinly and make strips of the squash with a potato peeler.
Put both in a bowl together with the other ingredients. Mix together and let sit while the sauce finishes simmering.
Optionally thicken the sauce in the chicken stew a bit, season to taste, and serve with rice and cucumber salad.

recipes.Title: Paella mixta
recipes.Ingredients:
200g of rice (preferably for risotto, e.g., arborio),
200g of chicken breast (skinless),
110g of prawns (about 4 pieces),
100g of green peas (about 2/3 cup),
1 onion,
2 cloves of garlic,
700ml of vegetable broth,
1 red bell pepper.
3 tablespoons of olive oil,
1 lemon,
100g of frozen seafood mix.

Spices:
saffron,
salt,
pepper,
sweet paprika,
smoked paprika,
hot paprika,
turmeric.
recipes.Preparation:
Rinse the chicken breast, pat dry, and cut into cubes. Rinse the bell pepper, pat dry, and chop into small pieces. Clean the prawns, and thaw the seafood.
Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a pan, sear the prawns on each side, and set aside. Then add the chicken and brown on each side, before transferring to a bowl.
Heat another tablespoon of olive oil in the pan, add the onion and fry until translucent. Add the garlic, bell pepper, and green peas, mix and fry for about 5 minutes.
Add the rice, saffron, paprikas, and turmeric, mix and sauté for about 3 minutes.
Add the chicken, pour in the broth, and cook on medium heat for about 10 minutes. Then add the seafood and prawns, cover with aluminium foil, and simmer for about 5 minutes.
The paella should rest for a few minutes before serving. Serve with lemon wedges, directly from the pan.

recipes.Title: Chicken marinade 2
recipes.Ingredients:
40 ml extra virgin olive oil
19 ml apple cider vinegar (or try malt vinegar)
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
10ml habanero hot sauce or similar
6 cloves garlic, crushed
1 tsp dried basil
1 tsp cayenne pepper or chili powder
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp onion powder
1 tsp salt
1 tsp black pepper
450g chicken
recipes.Preparation:
Whisk all of the ingredients together until well combined.
Marinate your chicken in a baggie or large bowl, sealed, at least 2 hours in the refrigerator, or overnight for even more flavor.

recipes.Title: BBQ sauce
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp olive oil
2 jalapeno peppers diced
1 small red onion diced
½ medium red pepper
3 cloves garlic chopped
120 ml ketchup
110g dark brown sugar
30 ml apple cider vinegar
30 ml whiskey
2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
1 tbsp Dijon mustard
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper
¼ tsp cayenne pepper
½ tsp ground oregano
1 tsp cumin
1 tsp crushed chilli flakes
recipes.Preparation:
Place the olive oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Once it is hot, add the red onion, jalapeno peppers, and red bell pepper and sauté the herbs for 3-5 minutes until they begin to soften.
Add the garlic and cook for a minute until it becomes aromatic. Next, add the ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, whiskey, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard, paprika, salt, pepper, cayenne pepper, oregano, cumin, and chilli flakes.
Bring the BBQ sauce to a boil, then decrease the heat to medium-low and gently simmer it for10-15 minutes.
Place the sauce into a blender and puree it until the sauce is smooth and has a thick consistency.

recipes.Title: Pasta allo scoglio
recipes.Ingredients:
176g of spaghetti
500g of clams with shells
500g of mussels with shells
150g of squid
150 g of shrimps
100g of ripe cherry tomatoes
1 fresh hot chilli pepper
2 cloves of garlic
3 tbsp of extra virgin olive oil 
75 ml of dry white wine
a bunch of fresh parsley
salt to taste
black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Rinse clams under running water and then let them soak in plenty of cold water with a handful of coarse salt. Place the clams in a pan and cook over high heat covered with a lid. Wait for them to open, this will take about 3 minutes. Now strain the clam sauce with a fine strainer but DO NOT throw away their water, keep it aside. Finally shell the clams, keeping some clams with their shells that you will use for the final decoration of the dish. Repeat with the mussels. Wash the squid under running water, then cut them into rings. Set aside. Wash and chop the cherry tomatoes then chop the parsley. Set aside.
In a large saucepan, sauté the peeled garlic cloves in the extra virgin olive oil. Add the red hot chili pepper and the squid. Cook for about 2 minutes over medium heat. Then raise the heat and add the white wine. Stir and allow the alcohol to evaporate. Finally add the mussels and clams and lower the heat. Add a ladle of clams water and then the chopped tomatoes. Mix and cook over high heat for about 10 minutes. Finally, add the shrimp and chopped parsley. Cook over medium heat for about 3 minutes (shrimp have very short cooking times). Now cook the pasta. Bring plenty of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta according to the cooking times described on their packaging. Using a slotted spoon, drain the spaghetti 3 minutes before the end of cooking time.
 Place them directly in the pan with the seafood sauce. Stir and finish cooking the spaghetti in the pan for another 3 minutes over high heat. This way they will better absorb the flavor of the seafood sauce.
Stir well and transfer the pasta allo scoglio to a serving dish. Garnish with the shells kept aside and serve.

recipes.Title: Pizza dough
recipes.Ingredients:
624g '00' flour or strong white flour
2 tsp salt 
7g instant yeast 
4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra as needed
440ml cold water
recipes.Preparation:
Combine the flour, salt and yeast in the bowl of a food mixer or a large mixing bowl. Add the oil and water and mix with the dough hook at low speed for 8 minutes to form a sticky, elastic dough. Alternatively, combine the wet and dry ingredients with a wooden spoon, then knead on a kitchen surface with oiled hands for about 10 minutes.
Oil a work surface and your hands.
Tip the dough out and divide into 6 with an oiled knife.
Shape each piece into a ball, tucking the edges under to make a smooth top. One dough ball will make one pizza.
Pop each dough ball into an oiled freezer bag and secure the top. If you prefer, you can space the dough balls out in an oiled roasting tin and cover with oiled cling film.
Chill for 1-3 days to prove and develop the flavour. At this stage the dough can be frozen for up to 6 months and defrosted in the fridge overnight when needed.
Once proved, remove the number of dough balls required from the fridge and leave, still bagged or covered, to come to room temperature for 1-2 hours. Shape and cook, as directed in the following recipes.

recipes.Title: Bucatini alla zozzona
recipes.Ingredients:
65g guanciale (Italian dry cured pork cheek), trimmed and diced (use pancetta if you can’t find guanciale)
2 Italian-style sausages
200g can of cherry tomatoes
200g dried bucatini pasta
2 egg yolks
20g pecorino romano cheese, finely grated, plus extra to serve (optional)
1 tsp crushed black peppercorns
recipes.Preparation:
Put the guanciale in a cold, deep saucepan. Get it over a low heat for a few minutes, then increase the heat to medium. As the pan heats up, the guanciale will gently render off its fat and become golden and crisp; this will take some time, around 15 mins. Crumble in the sausage and fry it in the guanciale fat for 5 mins; it doesn't need to brown too much.
Stir in the cherry tomatoes and bring up to a simmer, then leave to cook for 30 mins. The cherry tomatoes will burst and release their sweet juice into the sauce, which is great with the salty meat.
For the pasta, bring a large pan of water to the boil. Salt it a little less generously than you normally would – there's salt in some of the other ingredients. Drop in your bucatini and stir it really well to prevent sticking.
The pasta will need around 10-12 mins to cook to al dente.
Meanwhile, mix the egg yolks, pecorino and black pepper together in a separate bowl to form a yellow paste. When the pasta is a couple of minutes away from being al dente, take a small ladle of hot pasta water and whisk it into the egg yolks – this is called tempering the eggs, and it warms them up so that when they go into the hot pasta, they don’t seize.
When your pasta is al dente, set aside your largest mug full of pasta water, then drain the rest. Put the pasta back in its pan and pour in the tomato sauce, mixing it over low heat. Remove from heat, then pour in the egg mixture and a good splash of the pasta water and stir everything together very well. You will instantly see the sauce become creamy and glossy. Add a little bit more pasta water if it is a bit thick, then serve. Sprinkle over extra pecorino, if you like.

recipes.Title: Coleslaw
recipes.Ingredients:
1 Large White Cabbage  (or 1 small white cabbage)
4 Medium Carrots  (peeled)
1 Brown Onion  (peeled)
1 small bunch chives, chopped
480ml Mayonnaise
100ml Sour Cream
2 tbsp White Wine Vinegar
2 tsp Salt
4 tsp Sugar  
2 tsp dijon mustard
Black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Julienne the white cabbage and the 2 carrots using a mandoline, so you have fine, even, strips. Place in a large bowl.
1/2 large white cabbage,2 medium carrots

Carefully grate (shred) the quarter of an onion using a grater and add the onion to the bowl.
1/4 brown onion
Add the cup (240g) of mayonnaise, 3 tbsp sour cream, 1 tbsp white wine vinegar, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tsp sugar, 1/8 tsp mustard powder and the pinch of white pepper.
240 g (1 cup) mayonnaise,3 tbsp sour cream,1 tbsp white wine vinegar,1/2 tsp salt,2 tsp sugar,1/8 tsp mustard powder,pinch white pepper
Stir everything together until thoroughly combined.
recipes.Keywords: cabbage, carrots, onion, chives, mayonnaise, sour cream, vinegar

recipes.Title: Melanzane alla parmigiana
recipes.Ingredients:
2 garlic cloves crushed
3 tbsp olive oil
400g can chopped tomatoes
1 tbsp tomato purée
2 aubergines cut into long, 5mm thick slices
45g parmesan , freshly grated
10g basil leaves, torn
1 egg beaten
recipes.Preparation:
Heat oven to 200°C fan. In a shallow pan, mix together the garlic and 4 tbsp of the olive oil. Cook over a high heat for 3 mins, tip in the tomatoes, then simmer for 8 mins, stirring every now and then. Stir in the tomato purée.

Meanwhile, heat a pan until very hot. Brush a few of the aubergines with a little oil, then add to the pan. Cook over a high heat until well browned and cooked through, about 5-7 mins. Turn them halfway through cooking. Lift onto kitchen paper and do the next batch.

When all the aubergines are cooked, lay a few of them in the bottom of an ovenproof dish, then spoon over some sauce. Sprinkle with Parmesan and basil leaves. Add seasoning, then repeat this process with the remaining ingredients. Finally, pour the egg over the top, sprinkle over a little more Parmesan, then bake for 20 mins or until the topping is golden.

recipes.Title: Baba ganoush
recipes.Ingredients:
2 medium aubergines
4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 garlic clove, crushed or finely grated
1 tsp cumin seeds, toasted
2 tbsp tahini
1 large lemon, juiced
handful of parsley leaves, roughly chopped, to serve (optional)
flatbreads or pittas and vegetable crudités, to serve
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Cut the aubergines in half lengthways and score a diamond pattern into the flesh using a small, sharp knife, then brush over some of the oil and season with salt.Pierce the skin in a few places with a sharp knife before grilling. Roast the aubergines, cut-side down, on a baking tray for 20-25 mins until charred and collapsed. Leave to cool.

Scoop out the cooled aubergine flesh into the bowl of a food processor, then add the garlic, cumin seeds, tahini and lemon juice. Season well, then blitz to combine. With the motor running, drizzle in all but 1 tsp of the remaining oil until thick and smooth. Season to taste. Spoon into a dish, drizzle with the reserved oil, scatter with the parsley, if using, and serve with flatbreads, pittas or vegetable crudités for dunking.

recipes.Title: Roast aubergine and coconut curry
recipes.Ingredients:
400g aubergines (about 2), sliced into rounds, then cut into quarters
2 tbsp coconut or olive oil
1 onion, chopped
2 cm piece of ginger grated to a pulp
3 garlic cloves grated to a pulp
2 red chillies halved, deseeded and chopped
1 tsp ground turmeric
2 tsp ground coriander
4 black cardamom pods crushed a little (but not so much that the pods open)
3 large plum tomatoes, roughly chopped
2 sachets of coconut cream
juice ½ lime
small bunch coriander leaves
rice or naan breads, to serve
recipes.Preparation:
Heat oven to 170°C fan. Spread out the aubergine in a roasting tin (you may need to use two) and drizzle with 2 tbsp of the oil. Turn the pieces over with your hands and season. Roast for 15-20 mins, tossing them halfway through cooking, or until they are dark golden and soft.

Heat the rest of the oil in a flameproof casserole dish and cook the onions over a medium heat until they are soft and pale gold. Add the ginger, garlic and chilli, and cook for another 3 mins, then add the turmeric, coriander and cardamom pods (leave the pods whole). Stir for 1 min, then add the tomatoes and seasoning. Cook over a medium-low heat until the tomatoes begin to soften, stirring, then add the coconut cream, 35ml water and the aubergine.

Bring to just under the boil, (if it boils, the coconut cream will split), then turn down to a gentle simmer. Simmer for 30 mins, stirring every so often. Add the lime juice to taste, and check for seasoning. Add a pinch of sugar if it needs it. Stir in the coriander and serve with rice or naan breads.

recipes.Title: Chinese hot and sour aubergine
recipes.Ingredients:
2 medium aubergine, cut into long batons
100g green beans trimmed and halved
2 tbsp vegetable oil
1 large onion cut into thick half-moons
1 red chilli halved, deseeded and thinly sliced
For the sauce:
2 tbsp light soy sauce
2 tbsp dark soy sauce
1 tbsp tomato purée
2 tbsp Chinese black vinegar or balsamic vinegar
1 tbsp golden caster sugar
1 tsp cornflour dissolved in 2 tbsp water
Boiled rice to serve
recipes.Preparation:
Put the aubergine in a bowl of lightly salted water and stand for 30 mins to soften. Drain and pat dry. Blanch the green beans in boiling water for 1 min then drain, rinse in cold water and drain again.

To make the sauce, combine all the ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. When hot, cook the aubergine pieces until nicely browned on all sides, don’t turn them too early, let them get a nice colour first. When they start to brown, add the onion and chilli, and keep stir-frying for 4 mins or until soft.

Add the sauce and green beans, cover with a lid, lower the heat and simmer for 2 mins or until the aubergine is soft. Serve with rice.

recipes.Title: Prawn curry with peanuts and coconut
recipes.Ingredients:
2 shallots, peeled and quartered
2 garlic cloves, peeled
3 cm piece fresh root ginger, peeled
1 small red chilli, deseeded
Small handful fresh coriander, plus extra leaves to garnish
2 tsp vegetable oil
2 tsp.ground coriander
2 tsp ground cumin
½ tsp ground cardamom, from about 6 fat green pods
3 tbsp smooth peanut butter
3 tbsp tomato purée
200 g chopped tomatoes
2 sachets coconut cream
125 ml hot fish or vegetable stock
250 g raw peeled jumbo prawns
recipes.Preparation:
Put onion, garlic, ginger, chilli and fresh coriander (including stalks) in the small bowl of a food processor and pulse to a chunky paste. Heat oil in a medium pan over medium heat, add the paste and cook, stirring, for 5min.
Add the spices, peanut butter and tomato purée to the pan and cook for 2min, until fragrant. Add the tomatoes, coconut milk, stock and some seasoning. Increase heat to high and bubble for 7min until slightly reduced.
Add prawns and simmer for 2min until the prawns have turned pink and opaque. Sprinkle with extra coriander and serve with rice, if you like.

recipes.Title: Västerbottensostpaj
recipes.Ingredients:
Shell:
120g plain flour
60g granary flour
125g butter
1 egg

Filling:
4 eggs
250ml whipping cream
100ml milk
300g Västerbotten cheese
1tsp salt
2 tsp black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Blend the flour and butter. Add the egg and blend quickly to form a dough. Press the dough into a 25-30 cm pie dish making sure to cover the sides. Cool in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Set the oven to 200°C. Prick the base of the shell with a fork and bake for 10 - 15 minutes.
Drop the oven temperature to 175°C. Whip together the eggs, cream and milk. Grate the cheese. Blend in the cheese, salt and black pepper.
Put the filling in the shell and place in the middle of the oven. Bake for 50 minutes or until the filling is set and has a golden colour.

recipes.Title: Monica's seafood chowder
recipes.Ingredients:
400g fresh seafood
300g hot smoked salmon
1 yellow onion, finely chopped
1 carrot, diced
Olive oil
2 tbsp plain flour
500ml fish stock
2-3 potatoes, peeled and diced
300ml milk
100ml whipping cream
pinch cayenne pepper
fresh ground black pepper
parsley, finely chopped
2 cloves garlic, minced
recipes.Preparation: Peel or prepare all the seafood. Break the salmon into pieces. Gently fry the finely chopped onion and carrot in olive oil without browning it. Add garlic, sprinkle over the flour and let it sizzle for a minute. Add the stock and potato, cover with a lid and let it simmer for 12 - 15 minutes or until the potatoes are cooked. Add the milk and cream, season with the cayenne, salt and pepper and let it boil for a few minutes. Add the seafood. Let it all get really hot, sprinkle with parsley and serve with the bread.

recipes.Title: Swedish cinnamon buns (kanelbullar)
recipes.Ingredients:
Dough:
240ml milk
56g butter
405g plain flour
50g granulated sugar
7g instant-rise yeast
2 teaspoons ground cardamom (seeds only)
3/4 teaspoon fine salt
Filling Ingredients:
113g butter
100 g light brown sugar
2 tablespoons ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon ground cardamom seeds
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
Topping Ingredients:
1 egg (whisked together with 1 tablespoon water)
pearled sugar
recipes.Preparation:
Combine the milk and 56g butter in a small saucepan.  Heat over medium-low heat, stirring frequently to melt the butter, until the mixture reaches 43°C. If the mixture gets too hot, just wait a few minutes for it to cool.
In a large mixing bowl, briefly whisk together the flour, sugar, yeast, ground cardamom and salt until combined.  Add the warm milk mixture and stir until the dough begins to form. Knead for 7-10 minutes at slow speed or until the dough is smooth and soft.
Form the dough into a ball, place it in a greased bowl and cover with a damp towel or plastic wrap.  Let the dough rise in a warm space for 1 hour, or until it has doubled in size.
Meanwhile, stir together the filling ingredients in a separate mixing bowl until evenly combined.
Once the dough is ready to go, turn it out onto a large floured work surface.  Use a rolling pin to roll the dough into a 55 x 38cm rectangle.  Carefully and evenly spread the filling mixture across the entire surface of the dough.  Then fold the left third of the dough in towards the center, and fold the right third of the dough over that towards the center.  Gently run the rolling pin over the dough to press out any big bubbles.  Then roll the dough out a bit more so that it forms a  38 x 20cm rectangle.
Slice the dough into even 3 x 20-cm long strips with the back of a knife or any blunt edge to partially seal the strips. Take one strip and twist it several times, gently stretching it as you do so until it nearly doubles in length. Grab one end of the twisted strip and loosely wrap the dough around two fingers twice, like a bandage.  Then loop the rest of the dough perpendicularly around the dough so that it forms a knot, and tuck the loose end in at the bottom.  Transfer the dough to a large parchment-covered baking sheet, and repeat with the remaining dough strips.
Loosely cover the dough buns with a clean kitchen towel and let them rise for 1½ hrs.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan.  Brush each bun with the egg wash, then sprinkle with a pinch of pearled sugar.
Bake for 15-18 minutes, or until the rolls reach your desired level of golden brown. Transfer to a wire baking sheet and let cool for 5 minutes.  Then serve warm and enjoy!

recipes.Title: Coquilles St Jacques
recipes.Ingredients:
24 roe-free scallops

FOR THE SAUCE:
25 g butter, softened
25 g plain flour
75 ml white wine
125 ml fish stock
100 ml double cream
2 medium egg yolks

FOR THE CRUMB:
25 g fresh white breadcrumbs
25 g butter, melted
3 thyme sprigs, leaves picked
Finely grated zest ½ lemon

TO SERVE:
8 large, curved scallop shells
recipes.Preparation:
Prepare the scallops: peel off and discard the tough white muscle from each scallop (if present). Pat scallops dry with kitchen paper. Set aside.
For the sauce, melt the butter in a medium pan. Add flour and cook, stirring, for 30sec. Take off heat and gradually stir in the wine, followed by the stock, to make a smooth sauce. Return to heat and cook, stirring, until thickened (it will need to bubble). Take off heat, stir in the cream and yolks and check the seasoning. Set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the crumb ingredients with some seasoning.
Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) mark 6. Arrange 3 scallops in each shell, then sit the shells on a large baking tray. Spoon over the sauce and top with the crumb mixture.
Cook in the oven for 15-17min, or until golden and bubbling. Serve immediately with buttery mashed potatoes, if you like.

recipes.Title: Pork pie 2
recipes.Ingredients:
Pastry:
260g plain flour
60g butter
70g lard
1 tsp salt
110ml water
Filling:
400g pork mince
150g pork loin steaks
½ tsp salt
½ tsp thyme
½ tsp parsley
½ tsp paprika
1 tbsp chives, finely chopped
¼ tsp cayenne pepper
¼ tsp nutmeg
1 tbsp worcester sauce
1 egg, beaten to brush pastry

Gelatine:
2 leaves gelatine
200 ml chicken stock
recipes.Preparation:
Put 100ml water into a saucepan and set over a medium heat. Add the butter, lard and salt, melt and then add the flour and fold in to make a dough, Continue mixing until the dough has thickened and is smooth. Turn out onto a floured surface and knead into a smooth ball. Cover in cling film and refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours.
Mix all the meat ingredients in a bowl, mould into a ball and wrap in cling film; refrigerate for 2 hours.
Weigh out 200g of the pastry and press into a roughly 150mm circle. Flour a jam jar and press into the pastry and then work the pastry about half way up the sides of the jar. Weigh out 50g of pastry for the lid and roll out to a circle a little larger then the base. Cut out the lid with the jam jar and pierce at the centre with a straw.
Weigh out about 140g of the meat mix and roll into a ball. Place in the pastry base and tease it out to fill. Wet the sides of the base and the underside of the lid and drop the lid onto the base. Press the lid and base together and crimp securely. Brush the sides and top of the pie with the beaten egg and run the pie over some flour before setting on a baking sheet covered with baking parchment. Bake for 20 minutes at 200°C then raise to 150°C for a further 50 minutes. Check that the centre temperature is above 70°C. Allow to cool for an hour.
Meanwhile, make the chicken stock, briefly soften the gelatine leaves in cold water for 5 minutes, then add the gelatine to the stock. Syringe the gelatine mix into the hole in the lid slowly until the pie is filled. An air escape hole may be required to fill easily.
Refrigerate until the gel has set.

recipes.Title: Crab and sweetcorn soup
recipes.Ingredients:
For the stock:

1.2l good chicken stock
6 thin slices of root ginger
3 bunches of spring onions, roughly chopped
½ tsp whole white peppercorns

For the soup:

2 fresh sweetcorn cobs
225g fresh white crab meat
5 tsp cornflour
1 tsp very finely chopped root ginger
2 spring onions, cut into 2.5cm pieces and finely shredded lengthways
1 tbsp light soy sauce
1 tbsp Chinese rice wine or dry sherry
1 egg white, lightly beaten
Salt and black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Begin with chicken stock in a saucepan, enriching it with ginger, spring onions, and peppercorns.
Bring it to the boil and allow it to simmer for 20 minutes to let the flavours combine.
Whilst the stock develops, handle the sweetcorn cobs, cutting them on a chopping board and removing the kernels with a large, sharp knife.
Add the sweetcorn to the stock and leave it to cook gently for five minutes. Ensure to meticulously check the crab meat for any shell fragments, keeping the flesh in the largest pieces possible.
Next, mix the cornflour into a smooth paste with a dash of cold water, whisk it into the soup, and allow it to cook for an additional two minutes.
Introduce the crab meat, ginger, spring onions, soy sauce, and the rice wine or sherry, then season the soup with salt and a bit of pepper to your liking. Let it simmer for a minute.
Following that, stir the soup, remove the spoon, and slowly add the beaten egg white until it forms long, thin strands within the soup. Allow everything to simmer for roughly 30 seconds before serving.

recipes.Title: Jansson's frestelse
recipes.Ingredients:
10 medium-sized potatoes
2 tbsp butter
1 onion, finely sliced
20 tinned sprat fillets
salt and pepper
150ml single cream
150ml  whole milk
1 tbsp dried breadcrumbs
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to around 200°C.
Peel the potatoes and chop them into small 0.5cm - a bit thinner than French fries.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the onion and cook until soft. Take care not to burn the onion - it should be cooked, but not turning brown.
Add the potatoes and cook for a few minutes.
Layer half of the onion and potato mixture in the bottom of an ovenproof dish, then top with 10 sprat fillets evenly across. Season with salt and pepper.
Add another layer of onion and potato, then another 10 sprats on top. Pour the remaining sprat juice over the dish.
Pour two-thirds of the milk and cream over the dish, then sprinkle the breadcrumbs on top. Season again.
Bake for about 45 minutes, or until the potatoes are cooked. Halfway through the cooking time, add the rest of the milk and cream. If the dish is looking dry, you can add more milk - the aim is to get a creamy consistency.

recipes.Title: Toast skagen
recipes.Ingredients:
225g shrimp, peeled, cooked and chopped
115g mayonnaise
125g soured cream
2 tbsp chopped fresh dill, plus sprigs to garnish (optional)
2 tbsp finely chopped red onion
1 tbsp freshly squeezed lemon juice
1 tbsp horseradish
4 slices rye bread
1 tbsp unsalted butter
salt and freshly ground black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Mix the shrimp, mayonnaise, soured cream, dill, onion and lemon juice together in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Toast the rye bread slices until crispy. Spread a layer of butter on each slice of rye bread.
Spoon a generous amount of the shrimp mixture onto each slice of bread. Garnish each serving with a dill sprig, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.Title: Red cabbage, German style
recipes.Ingredients:
1 head red cabbage  (shredded)
1 apple  (grated, you can leave the skin, just remove the seeds)
1 onion
120 ml apple cider vinegar
120 ml water
80g sugar
½ teaspoon black pepper
pinch ground cloves
salt
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
4 tablespoons butter
recipes.Preparation:
Cook the onion and apple in butter in a saucepan for 5 minutes. Add shredded red cabbage, vinegar, water, sugar, pepper, and cloves. Cover the pot with a lid and bring mixture to a boil over medium heat. Cook about 55 minutes or until tender, but still with a small bite.
Drain extra liquid from the cabbage. Brown butter in a small saucepan by cooking it over medium-low heat until foamy and golden. Remove from heat and stir into cooked cabbage mixture with the lemon juice.

recipes.Title: Aubergine and tomato curry
recipes.Ingredients:
600g aubergine, or baby aubergines sliced into rounds
3 tbsp olive oil
2 onions finely sliced
4 garlic cloves crushed
¼ tsp cardamom seeds
¼ tsp ground cumin
¼ tsp ground cloves
¼ tsp nutmeng
¼ tsp cinnamon
¼ tsp black pepper
1 tsp turmeric
1 tsp ground coriander
Pinch of sugar
1 red chilli, finely chopped
1 x 400ml can chopped tomatoes
1 x 400 ml coconut milk
recipes.Preparation:
Heat oven to 180°C fan. Boil the aubergines for 10 minutes then drop into cold water for 5 minutes. Toss the aubergines in a roasting tin with 2 tbsp olive oil, season well and spread out. Roast for 20 mins or until dark golden and soft.

Heat the remaining oil in an ovenproof pan or flameproof casserole dish and cook the onions over a medium heat for 5-6 mins until softening. Stir in the garlic and spices, cook for a few mins until the spices release their aromas.

Tip in the tomatoes, coconut milk and roasted aubergines, and bring to a gentle simmer. Simmer for 20-25 mins, removing the lid for the final 5 mins to thicken the sauce. Add a little seasoning if you like, and a pinch of sugar if it needs it. Stir through most of the coriander. Serve over rice or with chapatis, scattering with the remaining coriander.

recipes.Title: Baguettes
recipes.Ingredients:
250 g strong white flour
185 g warm water
5 g dried yeast
5 g salt
recipes.Preparation:
Blend the flour and salt in a stand mixer with a dough hook. Add the yeast to the warm water in a jug and allow to stand until a foam develops. Pour the yeast/water into the flour and mix until a homogeneous dough has just about formed. Cover the bowl with cling film and allow to double in size.

Tip out the dough and flatten into a rectangle about 350-400mm long. Fold and pinch the dough from the outsides into the middle  and place onto a baking sheet lined with floured baking paper. Push the sides of the paper up and place some ceramic beads on the paper to hold the shape of the dough. Cover with a tea towel and allow to rise for 1 hour or until doubled in size. Sprinkle with flour then water then score the dough diagonally 4/5 times.

Preheat the oven to 230°C with an empty roasting dish on the bottom rack. When up to temperature, add water to the roasting dish and quickly place the dough pieces on the middle rack. Bake for 20 - 25 minutes until golden.

recipes.Title: Lamb and beetroot curry
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp. vegetable oil
400 g lamb neck, fat trimmed and cut into 4cm chunks
250 g bunch beetroot, peeled, halved and cut into 2cm half moons
150 ml chicken or vegetable stock
2 cloves
3 green cardamom pods, bashed

FOR THE MARINADE:
1 tsp. cumin seeds
1 tsp. Sichuan peppercorns
1 tsp. ground coriander
1 tsp. ground fenugreek
1 tsp. fennel seeds
100 g natural yogurt
1small onion, roughly chopped
1 tbsp. tomato puree
4 large garlic cloves, roughly chopped
2 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
1 tsp. ground turmeric

FOR THE MINT SAUCE:
15 g each mint and coriander leaves
1 tbsp. natural yogurt
1 tbsp. lime juice
1 tsp. caster sugar
½ a green chilli, deseeded and roughly chopped (keep the seeds in, if you prefer)
1 small garlic clove, crushed
recipes.Preparation:
To make the marinade, put the cumin seeds, Sichuan peppercorns, coriander, fenugreek and fennel seeds in a small dry frying pan over a medium heat for 1-2min, until fragrant. Transfer to a pestle and mortar or spice grinder, and grind until fine. Tip into a food processor with the remaining marinade ingredients, except the turmeric (this can stain the plastic) and whizz until smooth. 

Spoon the marinade into a large bowl with the turmeric and lamb. Mix well and then leave to marinate for at least 1hr, or covered overnight in the fridge, if you have enough time. 

Shake off any excess marinade into the bowl, then heat the vegetable oil in a large casserole over a high heat and brown the lamb pieces in batches, until golden brown all over. Transfer to a bowl and set aside. Drain off any excess fat left in the pan. 

Add the remaining marinade to the pan and stir well, making sure to scrape up any brown bits from the bottom of the pan as these will add to the flavour. Return the browned lamb pieces to the pan with the beetroot, stock, cloves and cardamom; season generously. Bring to a simmer then reduce the heat and cover and cook for 1hr 30min until almost tender. Remove the lid and continue cooking for 1hr-1hr 15min, until the sauce begins to thicken. The lamb should be tender and the beetroot cooked through. 

Meanwhile, make the mint sauce. Put all the ingredients into a small food processor with a generous pinch of salt and 4tbsp water and blitz until very finely chopped. Set aside. 

Taste and adjust seasoning, then remove cloves and cardamom before serving with the mint sauce and your choice of sides.

recipes.Title: Green apple and tomato chutney
recipes.Ingredients:
1 kg tomatoes, chopped
250g green apple, cored, peeled & chopped
125g raisins, chopped
315g shallots, chopped
8g root ginger
3-4 fresh chillies
1tsp salt
1/4 tsp allspice
250g brown sugar
285 ml  cider vinegar
recipes.Preparation:
Chop all apples, tomatoes, raisins and shallots.  Place in a large pot together with the other ingredients and bring to the boil.  Stir until all the sugar has dissolved, then turn the heat down to leave it on a low simmer until the desired consistency is reached.  I left mine till most of the liquid had cooked away, probably an hour or so.

To sterilise the jars:
Wash the jars and lids in hot, soapy water.  Place the damp jars upside down in a cold oven and turn it to 160°C.  Once the oven has heated up to 160°C the jars are ready to be used.  In the meantime, place the lids in a small saucepan of water and bring to the boil.  Boil for 5 minutes, after which the lids are ready to use.

Carefully remove the HOT jars from the oven and fill each with chutney.  Screw the lid on tightly.

recipes.Title: Chicken ball skewers
recipes.Ingredients:
455g chicken, shredded
35g spring onion, thinly sliced
1 tbsp ginger, minced
1 tsp sesame oil
3 tbsp vegetable oil
10g panko breadcrumbs
sesame seed, to garnish

SOY GLAZE:
235ml soy sauce
60ml rice vinegar
60ml sake
50g sugar
recipes.Preparation:
In a medium pot, combine all ingredients for glaze and bring to a boil until the bubbles start to become sticky and glossy.
Combine the shredded chicken, green onions, ginger, sesame oil, 60 ml of the soy glaze in a bowl until evenly mixed.
If the mixture does not hold its shape when rolled into a ball, add in panko breadcrumbs, mix evenly, and re-roll the meatballs to test their structural integrity.
Roll into 2½ cm meatballs, then thread 3-4 meatballs on a skewer. Repeat with remaining mixture.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Sear 3-4 skewers at a time and flip when the undersides are golden brown.
Brush the glaze on the skewers evenly and cook for about 5 more minutes, flipping every minute and brushing additional glaze as necessary.

recipes.Title: Cheese and bacon straws
recipes.Ingredients:
375g puff pastry
plain flour, for dusting
1 tbsp English mustard
100g mature cheddar, grated
freshly ground black pepper
14 slices good-quality streaky bacon
1 free-range egg, lightly beaten
recipes.Preparation:
Line a baking tray with greaseproof paper.
Roll the pastry out on a lightly floured work surface to a large rectangle of 0.5cm/¼in thickness.
Turn the pastry so that the longest side is facing you, spread over the mustard, sprinkle with the cheese and season with freshly ground black pepper. Place the pieces of bacon onto the pastry, leaving a small gap between each piece.
Cut the pastry between each slice of bacon. Carefully twist each piece of pastry 4-5 times so it looks like a curly straw, then place on the baking tray.
Repeat the process until all of the bacon has been used up. Chill the pastry twists in the fridge for 15-20 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 220°C
Remove the twists from the fridge and brush with the beaten egg.
Reduce the oven to 200°C and bake the twists for 20-25 minutes, or until the pastry is well risen and golden-brown. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool.

recipes.Title: Curry sauce base 1
recipes.Ingredients:
1tsp black pepper
2tbsp coriander
4 cardamom pods
1tsp cinnamon
½ tsp clove
2 red onions, sliced
6 cloves garlic, minced
25mm piece ginger, minced
1½ tbsp turmeric
1½ tbsp cumin
1 tbsp coriander
4 red chillies, sliced
8 medium tomatoes
salt
recipes.Preparation: Toast the pepper, coriander, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves in a little oil until fragrant. Add the onion and caramalise over low heat for about 40 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for a minute. Deglaze with a little water then add the turmeric, cumin, coriander and chillies. Juice the tomatoes and add to the sauce then cook for 45 minutes to thicken. season with salt.

recipes.Title: Seed cake
recipes.Ingredients:
450g butter
450g flour
350g caster sugar
2 tablespoons caraway seeds
6 eggs, whisked
200 ml brandy or 200 ml madeira wine
ground mace 
grated nutmeg, to taste
50g chopped candied citrus peel (optional)
recipes.Preparation:
Pre-heat the oven to 170°C and grease and line an 18-20cm round cake tin.
Cream the butter with the sugar and then sift in the flour.
Add the mace, nutmeg and caraway seeds and mix together well. (Add the chopped candied peel if using at this stage as well).
Stir in the whisked eggs and the brandy.
Beat the cake again for 2 to 3 minutes, until very smooth and with no lumps.
Pour the mixture into a tin lined with buttered paper.
Bake it for 1½ to 2 hours, until a skewer comes out clean when tested, and the cake is well risen, firm and golden brown.
recipes.Keywords: flour, butter, sugar caraway seeds, brandy, eggs

recipes.Title: Parliament cakes
recipes.Ingredients:
225g plain flour
115g butter
115g brown sugar
1 egg
2 tablespoons black treacle
2 and a half teaspoons ground ginger
recipes.Preparation:
Mix the flour, ginger and sugar thoroughly in a bowl.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and add the treacle and bring to the boil, stirring continuously.
Add the hot butter and treacle to the bowl holding the dry ingredients and mix a little to allow the mixture to cool, add your egg and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until you get a dough.
When it has cooled enough to handle, scoop up about a tablespoon amount and drop this onto a baking sheet lined with greaseproof paper. Flatten it a bit so it looks more biscuit like.
You should get about 12-15 biscuits, depending on how big you make them, but remember they will expand a little in the oven, so leave space.
Bake at 160°C for 25 minutes then leave to cool on a cooling rack. They are properly crunchy (like ginger snaps when cool).

recipes.Title: Ukrainian borscht
recipes.Ingredients:
1 kg bone-in meat of choice (I used 4.5lb of pork trotters) bones are for broth, omit if using premade broth
175 g cabbage
1 medium-large onion
2 medium carrots
2 medium beets
2 bay leaves
1 large or 2 small potatoes
3-4 cloves garlic
4 tbsp cider vinegar
2 tablespoon tomato paste
1 tsp salt, more to taste
1 tsp ground black pepper, adjust to taste
1 tablespoon sunflower or olive oil for frying
recipes.Preparation:
Place the bone-in pork into a large casserole and add enough water to fully submerge it. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 1-2 hours or until the meat is tender and cooked through. While the broth simmers, you can prepare the vegetables - (cabbage, onions, beets and carrots). Peel them, chop the cabbage, finely dice the onion, cut the beets into thick sticks, and slice the carrots into circles.
Once the broth is ready, remove the meat and add a teaspoon of salt and bay leaves. Then place the chopped cabbage into the pot with the broth and simmer for 20 minutes.
Preheat a frying pan over medium heat for a couple of minutes, then add the oil. Add the chopped onion, beets, and carrots to the frying pan and saute over medium-high heat for 5 minutes. Stir in a teaspoon of salt, along with the tomato paste and vinegar. Fry for another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In the meantime, peel and chop potatoes into medium-sized cubes peel and mince the garlic, and slice the cooked meat into bite-size pieces.
20 minutes after adding the cabbage, stir in the sauteed beets, carrots, and onion, along with the peeled and chopped potatoes, minced garlic, and cooked chopped meat. Add more salt and pepper to taste.
Cook for another 15-20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender and easily pierced with a fork. Do a taste test and add more salt if needed. Turn off the heat and serve! Enjoy!
recipes.Keywords: beef, pork, cabbage, onion, beetroot, potato

recipes.Title: Coffee and walnut cake
recipes.Ingredients:
225 g unsalted butter, plus extra for greasing
225 g caster sugar
4 medium eggs
60 ml strong espresso coffee
250 g self-raising flour
75 g walnut halves

For the buttercream:
125 g unsalted butter
200 g icing sugar, sieved
50 ml strong espresso coffee

To decorate:
10 walnut halves
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to 200C/180C fan. Grease and line two 20cm sandwich cake tins.
In an electric processor, beat the butter and sugar together until pale and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time to the mixture, beating well between each one. It will look a little sloppy when all the eggs are in - but don't worry; it will soon transform!
Add the espresso to the mixture and stir well, preferably with a wooden spoon (we don't want to beat too much air out of the batter). Sieve in the flour and add the walnuts, then mix again with a wooden spoon.
Spoon the cake mixture into the prepared tins and bake in the middle of the oven for 25-35 minutes, until golden and springy on top, or until a skewer inserted into the centre of the cake comes out clean. Try not to open the oven door during cooking time.
Remove the cakes from the oven and leave to cool on a wire rack.
For the butter cream topping, beat the butter and icing sugar together in an electric mixer until pale and light (slow at first, to prevent the icing sugar from going all over the place). The more you mix it, the lighter and fluffier it will become. Just keep going until you get the desired consistency.
Add the espresso to the frosting and mix well. The amount you add depends on how coffee-ish you want it to taste - I use 50ml, but you could try 70ml. Although if you up the espresso quantity, you may have to add a little more icing sugar, to prevent it from getting too runny.
Sandwich the two cakes together with buttercream, then use what's left to cover the top of the cake. Decorate with walnut halves.
recipes.Keywords: butter, sugar, eggs, coffee, flour, nuts

recipes.Title: Sigara börek
recipes.Ingredients:
120g feta cheese crumbled
225g mozarella cheese
60g parsley chopped
8 pieces phyllo sheets (filo pastry)
1 tbsp water to brush the phyllo sheets
120ml oil to fry the boreks
recipes.Preparation:
In a bowl, combine crumbled feta cheese, mozzarella and chopped parsley. Set aside.
Cut each phyllo sheet lengthwise into 4 equal strips.
Place one strip in front of you and keep the remaining strips covered with a tea towel so they don’t dry out.
Put about 1 tablespoon of the filling on one end of the strip.
Fold the two long edges slightly inward to cover the filling.
Roll the strip tightly toward the other end.
Brush a little water on the tip of the strip to seal, then place it on a plate. Cover them with a towel.
Repeat the same process with the remaining strips, always keeping the unused ones under the towel.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat until hot.
Fry the rolls in batches, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy.
Transfer them onto a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.Keywords: feta cheese, mozarella cheese, phyllo pastry

recipes.Title: Involtini alla Romana (Beef braciole)
recipes.Ingredients:
450g flank steak, cut into 4 thin slices approximately 1/3 inch thick
4 slices of prosciutto
1 tablespoon pine nuts
1 lemon zest
2 tablespoons grated pecorino or parmesan
4 garlic cloves, chopped
2 tablespoons parsley, chopped
2 tbsp basil, chopped
2 tablespoons olive oil
Sauce:
1 medium yellow onion, chopped fine
2 carrots, peeled and chopped fine
2 celery stalks, chopped chopped fine
1 cup dry red wine
2 x 400g cans Italian tomatoes
2 bay leaves
3 fresh basil leaves, torn into small pieces
flour spread on a plate for dredging
salt & pepper to taste
recipes.Preparation:
Place each slice of beef between 2 sheets of clingfilm and pound with a meat pounder until 1/4 inch thick. Sprinkle with salt & pepper. Lay a slice of prosciutto on each one.
Mix together the pine nuts, cheese, lemon zest, garlic, chopped basil and parsley and sprinkle evenly on top of the beef slices with prosciutto. Put a basil leaf on top and then a fillet of anchovy. Roll up the slices, tucking in the ends and tie with kitchen string.
Heat the olive oil in a large sauce pan over medium heat. Dredge the braciole in flour shaking off any excess, then place in the pan. Cook until browned on all sides, about 15 minutes. Remove from pan with a slotted spoon and keep to the side.
If needed add some more olive oil to the pan then add the onion, carrots, and celery. Cook, stirring until tender but not browned, about 10 minutes.
Add the red wine and cook, stirring up any browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pan until reduced by half, about 2 minutes.
Crush the tomatoes with your hands and add, with their juices, into the saucepan. Fill one of the tomato cans 1/2 way with water and pour in. Add the bay leaves and season with salt and pepper.
Place the braciole back into the sauce, turn heat to low and cook at a simmer until beef is tender 1.5 to 2 hours.
Sprinkle the basil over the rolls, and cook for 2 minutes longer. Transfer to serving plates, spoon the sauce over the top and serve at once with pappardelle or other pasta or gnocchi.

recipes.Title: Chicken sate meatballs
recipes.Ingredients:
500g minced or finely chopped chicken
2 shallots, finely chopped
1-inch piece of ginger, grated
4 garlic cloves, crushed
1 tsp corriander
2 tsp fish sauce
1 tsp red pepper flakes
1 tsp soy sauce
1 egg
60g panko breadcrumbs

For the satay peanut sauce: 
86g peanut butter
1 tbsp gochujang paste
2 tsp fish sauce
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp sweet chilli sauce
400g can of coconut milk
240ml water
recipes.Preparation:
Mix the meatballs. Add the chicken, shallots, ginger, crushed garlic, corriander, fish sauce, red pepper flakes, soy sauce, egg and panko breadcrumbs to a large bowl. Use a spatula or hands to mix the ingredients together well.
Form the meatballs. Set a clean tray, or plate on your work surface and wet your hands (this will stop the meatballs from sticking to them). Scoop up a spoonful of the chicken mixture and roll into a golf ball-sized ball in your hands. Place on the prepared plate or tray and repeat with the rest of the ingredients. Place the meatballs into the fridge for about 30 minutes to firm up before cooking them.
Brown the meatballs. Place a large, high-sided pan over medium-high heat, then add olive oil. Once hot, add the meatballs and cook until browned all over. This will take about five minutes.
Make the peanut sauce. Wipe any excess oil from the pan, then reduce the heat to medium. Add peanut butter, gochujang paste, sweet chili sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, coconut milk and  water. Use a wooden spoon or whisk to mix the ingredients into a smooth sauce. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer the sauce. Once the sauce is simmering, add the meatballs into the sauce and simmer for a few minutes. Remove from the heat and thread the balls on to wooden skewers. Fry the skewers in a pan for a few minutes to finish.

recipes.Title: Nettle soup
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp olive oil plus extra for drizzling
1 onion, chopped
1 carrot, diced
1 leek,,washed and finely sliced
1 large floury potato, (Maris Piper or similar), thinly sliced
1l vegetable stock
400g stinging or Dead nettles, washed, leaves picked 
50g butter, diced
50ml double cream
recipes.Preparation:
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, leek and potato, and cook for 10 mins until the vegetables start to soften. Add the stock and cook for a further 10-15 mins until the potato is soft.

Add the nettle leaves, simmer for 1 min to wilt, then blend the soup. Season to taste, then stir in the butter and cream. Serve the soup drizzled with extra oil and scattered with dead nettle flowers, if you have them.

recipes.Title: Thai chicken noodle soup
recipes.Ingredients:
450 gram Chicken Breast Fillet diced
Butter for frying
1 Onion, sliced into rings
2 cloves Garlic, crushed
800 gram Water
2  Vegetable stock cube
1 x 400 ml can Coconut Milk
36 gram Fish Sauce
15 gram Lime Juice
2 gram Ground ginger
1 Red bell pepper, sliced into strips
150 gram Cherry Tomatoes, halved
1 Chili, cut into thin slices
noodles 
Salt and Pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Sauté the chicken pieces in a bit of butter in a pot or deep pan, stir until they are slightly colored on all sides.
Add onions and garlic to the pan, sauté until the onions are soft.
Add all other ingredients (except the noodles) to the soup and let it simmer for 8-10 minutes.
Then add the noodles and let the soup simmer for another 5 minutes until the noodles are tender.
Season the soup with salt, pepper, and optionally more fish sauce or lime.
Serve with fresh coriander and sesame seeds on top

recipes.Title: Roasted vegetable soup
recipes.Ingredients:
Soup:
2 Carrots
2 Red bell peppers
500g Tomato
2 Onions
3 cloves Garlic
45ml Olive Oil
Salt and Pepper
½tsp Thyme dried
500ml Vegetable Broth
100ml Cream

Roasted chickpeas:
2 cans Chickpeas
30ml Olive Oil
Chili, finely chopped
1tbsp Paprika ground
1tsp Cumin
Salt and Pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Soup:
Preheat the oven to 200°C, regular oven
Remove seeds from bell pepper and cut into large pieces.
Cut tomatoes into quarters.
Cut onions into wedges and chop garlic coarsely.
Put all the vegetables in an ovenproof dish and toss them with oil, salt, pepper, and thyme. Roast for 25 minutes in the oven until the vegetables are tender.
Take the vegetables out of the oven and put them in a blender with broth, blend into a creamy and smooth soup. Add cream and blend a few more times.

Chickpeas:
Drain the chickpeas and put them in a hot pan with oil and spices. Roast for 3-4 minutes until they are golden and crispy.

Top your soup with sour cream, chickpeas, and possibly some parsley – serve.
recipes.Keywords: vegetables, red peppers, tomato, cream, chickpeas

recipes.Title: Clootie dumplings
recipes.Ingredients:
110g fresh suet, or dried suet
225g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
½ tsp baking powder
½ tsp fine salt
1 tsp cinnamon
1 tsp mixed spice
1 tsp ground ginger
¼ tsp ground allspice
¼ tsp nutmeg
110g soft brown sugar
75g fine fresh breadcrumbs
25g coarse oatmeal
200g currants
100g sultanas or raisins
1 large green apple
1 carrot
Finely grated zest of 1 unwaxed orange or lemon
1 egg, beaten
2 tbsp treacle
About 60ml milk
recipes.Preparation:
Half-fill a large, lidded saucepan with water, then bring to a boil. Soak a clean tea towel or cheesecloth in water. And have ready some butcher’s string, or similar.
Put the flour in a large bowl with the baking powder and salt. Whisk in all the spices. Then, whisk in the sugar.
