Add the breadcrumbs, oatmeal and dried fruit to the dry ingredients and whisk through until evenly combined. Coarsely grate in the suet, if necessary, the apple (no need to peel it) and carrot, then add the grated citrus zest and stir in.
Put the treacle in a small bowl, add the egg and beat with a fork (this will make it easier to distribute the sticky treacle through the dumpling mix). Stir this into the large bowl. along with just enough milk to create a mixture that drops off a spoon without being runny.
Wring out the soaked tea towel well, then lightly dust one side with flour. Drape the tea towel over a medium bowl, then spoon the dumpling mixture into the centre. Bring the edges of the towel together up and over the top of the dumpling mix, to make a little round bundle a bit like a money bag, then tie the top of the bundle tightly with string, leaving long tails at each end.
Put a heatproof saucer or heat diffuser in the base of the pan of boiling water, then lower in the pudding parcel; the water should come about halfway up its sides. Tie the tails of string taut around the handles at each side of the pot (or around the lid), so it doesn’t tip over, then cover the pan and leave to cook at a rolling simmer for three hours, topping up the water as required.
Carefully lift out the dumpling, then unwrap on to a serving dish or tray. For the full clootie dumpling experience, leave it to cool slightly while you heat the oven to 180°C fan, then put the dumpling in the oven for 15 minutes. Serve with custard, cream or ice-cream.
recipes.Keywords: suet, flour, oats, currants, sultanas, apple

recipes.Title: Kedgeree 2
recipes.Ingredients:
2 fillets smoked haddock
2 bay leaves
250ml milk
Black pepper
Knob of butter
3 measures of basmati rice
3 eggs
1 onion or bunch of spring onions, sliced
4 cloves of garlic, minced
1 small chilli, finely sliced
1 small piece of ginger, finely chopped
1 tbsp ground cumin
1 tsp ground corriander
1 tbsp lemon juice
1 tbsp parsley, chopped
Second knob of butter
recipes.Preparation:
Pour the milk into a large frying pan and add the butter and plenty of black pepper. Bring to the boil and add the fish; poach for about 8 minutes, turning over half way through. Remove the fish from the liquor. Meanwhile, cook the rice with a tsp of salt amd black pepper. Boil the eggs for 12 minutes then chill in cold water.
Sauté the onion for a few minutes until softened, add the garlic and spices and cook for another minute. Add the rice and stir in then add the fish, stir in and then some of the cooking liquor a little at a time to moisten the rice. Finally, chop and add the egg, lemon juice and parsley with another knob of butter.

recipes.Title: Tortellini stuffed with gorgonzola
recipes.Ingredients:
For the pasta
90g of 00 flour
2 egg yolks
20g egg white
1 tsp olive oil
pinch of salt

100g gorgonzola

For the sauce
1 red pepper
12 cherry tomatoes
2 shallots, finely chopped
6 cloves garlic, minced
pinch of smoked paprika
basil
2 tbsp single cream
salt
black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Make the pasta in a stand mixer, kneading until smooth. Roll out the pasta until thin. Cut into 8cm squares and place a tsp of gorgonzola cheese on each square. Fold the square over the filling to make a triangle and press around the edges to seal.

Quarter the red pepper and de-seed. Place on a baking tray with the tomatoes and drizzle with olive oil. Roast at 200°C fan until blackening, about 25 minutes. Remove the skins. Blend the red pepper and tomato flesh. Sauté the shallots in olive oil until softened, then add the garlic and cook for 1-2 minutes. Add the pepper and tomato mix and season with salt, pepper, smoked paprika and basil, cook for a minute. Finally add the cream, stir in to warm and remove from the heat. Put all into a blender and add a little pasta cooking water before blending to a smooth sauce.

Pour the sauce over the paste and top with shaved pecorino or parmesan and some basil leaves. Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

recipes.Title: Figs baked  with a balsamic glaze
recipes.Ingredients:
4 figs
4 pieces of Parma ham
35g montalgno affine cheese
2 tbsp balsamic vinegar glaze
Splash of dry white wine
Fresh basil
recipes.Preparation:
To make the balsamic glaze, pur 90ml balsamic vinegar into a small saucepan and simmer for about 20 to 30 minutes until the volume has reduced to around 50%, Heat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan. Cut the figs into quarters, slicing most of the way through but keeping the base intact. Squeeze the base of each fig to open it up, then wrap each one in a piece of parma ham, leaving the top open.
Put in a baking dish, then push the cheese into the centre of each fig. Drizzle with the balsamic vinegar glaze and a splash of dry white wine, then bake for 20-25 minutes until oozing. Scatter with fresh basil and serve.

recipes.Title: Mussels with chickpeas au gratin
recipes.Ingredients:
700g of large mussels
1 small can of chickpeas, drained
60ml white wine
6 cloves garlic
Parmesan cheese, grated
1 sprig rosemary
30ml extra-virgin olive oil
salt
pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Place mussels in a saucepan with 120ml of water and 60ml white wine. Bring to a boil, cover and cook for 3 minutes or until shells open. Filter the cooking liquid and set aside. Discard empty shells and top shells from cooked mussels. Arrange mussels in their bottom shells on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. 
Place chickpeas in a food processor or blender with filtered mussel cooking liquid. Heat 30ml olive oil with 1 sprig of rosemary and  crushed garlic. When oil starts to sizzle, pour it over the chickpeas. Remove the rosemary. Add salt and pepper and blend. 
Spread chickpea purée over mussels, covering them well. Sprinkle with grated cheese, drizzle with a bit of oil, and grill until golden brown.

recipes.Title: Sauerkraut
recipes.Ingredients:
1 white or red cabbage
1-2 carrots (optional, speeds up fermentation)
1 tbsp caraway seeds (or juniper berries)
salt
recipes.Preparation:
Trim the base of the cabbage and peel away the outer leaves; set these aside for use later. Cut the cabbage into quarters and use a mandoline, food processor, coarse grater or sharp knife to finely shred the cabbage and carrot (if using).
Tip the cabbage into a large bowl, add the caraway seeds and make a note of the total weight. Add 2 per cent salt of this total weight, so if the total weight is 600g, you will need 12g salt.
Using your hands, massage the salt really well into the shredded cabbage for a couple of minutes until it starts to soften. Cover the bowl with a clean cloth or plate and set aside for at least 30 minutes and up to three hours until the cabbage is very soft and has released water.
Scoop the cabbage and any resulting liquid into a clean one-to-two-litre jar and really pack it down hard so that the shredded cabbage is submerged under the briny liquid and you have a clear 5cm gap between the cabbage and the top of the jar. Cover the top of the cabbage with the reserved outer leaves and place a weight on top. Close the lid but leave it slightly loose – if the jar is sealed tight it runs the risk of exploding!
Place the jar on a plate in a dark cool cupboard out of direct sunlight and leave for two to three days for fermentation to start. Burp the jar daily to release any collected gas. After seven days the sauerkraut should be fermenting nicely so it can now be stored in the fridge. Use within one to two months, depending on how soft you like it.

recipes.Title: Pasta alla Tarantina
recipes.Ingredients:
500g fresh mussels
200 g spaghetti or linguine
250 g cherry tomatoes, halved
1 red chilli, finely chopped
6 garlic cloves peeled and chopped
1½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil
2 tbsp fresh parsley chopped
75 ml white wine
salt for pasta
ground black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Clean the mussels thoroughly, removing any debris and the fibrous beard. Sauté half the garlic and chili in olive oil, add the mussels and wine, cover and cook for about three minutes. Remove the mussels and take out from the shells leaving a few for decoration. Strain the cooking liquor. 
Fry some more garlic in olive oil and add the tomato halves. Toss for about 30 seconds and then add the mussel liquid, season with pepper, and bring to the simmer. 
Half-cook the pasta , drain, and add to the tomatoes. Continue cooking until al dente and finally add the mussels, finishing with fresh parsley.

recipes.Title: Pasta, Ravioli with prawns and cream sauce
recipes.Ingredients:
Pasta dough:
'00' flour, enough to make a firm dough
2 large eggs
1 tbsp olive oil

Filling:
12 prawns, shelled, de-veined
Butter
1 large egg
salt pepper
1 lemon zest
2 heaped tbsp drained ricotta cheese or cream cheese
2 tbsp chives, chopped

Sauce:
Butter
2 shallots
150 ml dry white wine
1 tsp fennel seeds
100 ml single cream
salt
pepper
chopped chives
recipes.Preparation:
Put flour on a plate and add the eggs and olive oil. Combine with a fork adding flour until a firm dough has formed. Knead the dough until smooth then cover with cling film and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Cook the prawns in butter until just pink then chop finely. Break an egg into a bowl, season and add the lemon zest. Now add the ricotta cheese and the chives, then combine into a firm mix.
Break and egg into a small pan and sweat the shallots until soft. De-glaze the pan with wine then add the fennel seeds and reduce until almost dry. Season with salt and pepper and then add the cream and heat foe a few minutes then add the chives. The sauce can be strained if desired.
Divide the dough into two pieces. Roll the dough out on the coarse setting, fold into three and repeat until smooth. Gradually reduce the thickness until minimum. Repeat for the other ball of dough. Place one sheet over the ravioli mould and add a tsp of filling to each mould. Brush the other sheet with water or beaten egg and place it, wet side down over the mould. Use the cutting roll to cut the ravioli and remove onto a floured plate.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and add the ravioli. Cook for 2-3 minutes until they float. Remove with a slotted spoon and serve with the sauce; decorate with some chives.

recipes.Title: Fish Pie, Hairy Bikers
recipes.Ingredients:
300ml whole milk
1 small onion - peeled and cut into six pieces, keeping the root intact
1 bay leaf
250g white fish fillets like haddock, cod or pollock
250g salmon
250g smoked haddock
3 free-range eggs
50ml double cream
40g butter
40g plain flour
2 tbsp white wine
Fresh dill with the leaves removed
salt and freshly ground black pepper

For the mashed potato:
650g peeled potatoes
40g butter
40ml double cream
75g grated mature cheddar cheese
recipes.Preparation:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Put the milk in a large saucepan before adding the chopped onion and bay leaves. Season with the salt and pepper before adding the fish fillets and bringing the mixture to a gentle simmer. Cover the saucepan and cook for two minutes on a low heat before setting it aside and leaving it to stand for five minutes. Use a colander to drain the fish into a bowl and pour the liquid into a jug.
Start making the topping by chopping the potatoes into even pieces and boiling them in simmering water for 15 minutes until they are soft. Drain the potatoes and then add them back to the pan with the double cream, butter and three quarters of the grated cheese. Mash the potatoes and add salt and pepper to taste.
Boil the eggs in water for nine minutes before draining in a colander under water for between one and two minutes. Add the eggs to a bowl of very cold water and put to the side.
Melt 75g of butter in a saucepan before stirring in the plain flour. Gradually add the milk mixture from when you cooked the fish and keep stirring it over a medium heat until it thickens and is nice and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Take the pan off the heat and add the fronds of dill. Peel the boiled eggs and cut them into quarters.
Add a third of the sauce to a large ovenproof dish and then add half the fish fillets, breaking them up into chunks and getting rid of any skin, onion and bay leaves. Put half the eggs in a layer on top of the fish before adding another third of the sauce. Continue adding layers until you have used up your fish, eggs and sauce.
Add the mashed potato mixture to the top, adding it to the edges first before working your way to the centre of the dish. Use a fork to add texture to the mash and then sprinkle the rest of your grated cheese on top. Bake the fish pie for around 45 minutes or until the top is golden brown.
recipes.Keywords: fish, haddock cod, pollock, potato, pie

recipes.Title: Steak and onion pie
recipes.Ingredients:
For the pastry:
450 g flour
150 g butter
90 ml milk (warm)
90 ml water (warm)
1 teaspoon salt

800 g braising steak (chuck steak)
3 potatoes, chopped into small cubes
Olive oil
2 heaped tbsp plain flour
2 bay leaves
1 medium onions
1 medium red onion
370ml beef stock
1 glass red wine
2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
2 tbsp Red wine vinegar
Salt & pepper
6 garlic cloves, crushed
1 tsp Marmite
Sprig of fresh thyme (chopped) (or 1 tsp dried thyme)
recipes.Preparation:
Bring water and milk to boil. Add the butter and melt. Mix the flour and salt separately and add the liquids. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface and form a smooth, soft dough. Cover the dough and refrigerate for 1 hour.

Coat the beef in seasoned flour and fry in olive oil in batches until browned on all sides, and set aside on a plate. 
Chop the onions and fry them in olive oil in your casserole for about 3-4 minutes. Add the beef back to the casserole, the beef stock, the bay leaves, the Worcestershire sauce, the Marmite, the red wine vinegar, the crushed garlic and the red wine. 
Throw in any remaining flour left from coating the beef and season to suit. Stir well. Put the lid on the casserole and put in the pre-heated oven at 160°C. In the meantime peel and chop the potatoes.

After 3 hours remove the casserole from the oven. Carefully remove the lid and add the potatoes and the thyme. Stir to cover the contents (if the fluid level is too low then just add some more water). Replace back in the oven for another 1 hour. 
The slow cook will help tenderise the meat and make it delicious. Allow to cool.

Final cooking:
When you are ready to cook, fill your chosen pie dish with filling, roll out the pastry and cover the pie.
Place pie in the oven at 180°C for about 30-40 minutes until the pastry is cooked and browned.

recipes.Title: Papardelle with vodka sauce
recipes.Ingredients:
140g dry papardelle
30ml olive oil
½ teaspoon crushed red chile flakes
4 cloves garlic, grated
4 rashers bacon, cut into strips
4 shallots
400ml canned crushed tomatoes
35ml vodka
90ml double cream
50g grated parmesan, plus more for garnish
salt and pepper to taste
garnish: fresh chopped basil, grated parmesan
recipes.Preparation:
Begin cooking pasta to al dente stage according to package instructions.
Heat oil in large frying pan over medium heat. Add the bacon, cook until bacon is beginning to crisp then add the shallots. Cook until softened then add the chilli flakes and crushed garlic, cook until fragrant, 1-2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and vodka, bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally for 5-10 minutes.
Stir in cream, parmesan cheese, plus a little pasta water until smooth. If needed, add more pasta water a little at a time until smooth. Salt and pepper to taste.
Drain pasta, add to pan with sauce and toss until coated.
Serve with fresh basil and grated parmesan.

recipes.Title: Tamil black pepper curry
recipes.Ingredients:
Marinade:
1kg chicken thighs
8 cloves garlic, crushed
15g ginger, grated
4g turmeric
salt

Spices:
2 tsp black peppercorns
1 tbsp coriander seeds
1½ tsp cumin seeds
1½ tsp fennel
4 cloves
1 small stick cinnamon
1 small red chilli, dried

10 curry leave
2 medium onions, chopped
4 medium tomatoes, chopped
375ml chicken stock
10g cilantro, chopped
2 long green chillis, sliceds
recipes.Preparation:
Mix the marinade ingredients together and refrigerate for 2 to 24 hours.
Put all the spices in a frying pan and toast for 2 minutes until fragrant; allow to cool and then blend to a fine powder.
In a lidded casserole, fry the curry leaves for a minute then add the onion and fry for 10-12 minutes. Add the chillis and fry for 2 minutes. Add the marinated chicken and fry for 5-6 minutes then add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes.Add the spice blend and cook for a couple of minutes then add the chicken stock, salt and pepper. Put the lid on and cook for 30 - 40 minutes. Add the cillantro leaves, mix and cook for 1 minute.

recipes.Title: Chicken and fennel pie with parmesan pastry
recipes.Ingredients:
For the Pastry:
250g Plain, strong flour
½ tsp salt
1 tsp Caraway seeds
40g Strong Cheddar cheese, grated
25g Parmesan cheese, finely grated
126g Cold butter
1 Large egg, separated
2 tbsp Cold water

For the Filling:
2 - 3 Large cloves garlic
4 Large skinless chicken breast fillets
2 large fennel bulbs
2 tbsp groundnut oil
42g butter
¼ nutmeg, grated
42g Plain flour
3 Rounded tbsp Plain yoghurt
427ml Milk
335g Small tomatoes
Salt
Black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Make the pastry first. Sift the flour and salt into a bowl and add the caraway seeds and cheeses. Cut the butter into small pieces and rub into the flour using fingertips until the mixture is crumbly. Using a fork, whisk the egg white lightly (reserving the yolk) with the water and add gradually to the flour mixture. Then press the dough into a ball, wrap it in clingfilm and refrigerate.
For the filling, cut the chicken breast fillets across into half inch pieces and slit the fennel bulbs lengthways. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and toss the chicken and fennel pieces separately, transferring them to a plate on one side with a slotted spatula.
Now melt the butter in a large iron casserole, add the chopped garlic and the grated nutmeg and stir briefly. Remove from the heat and stir in the flour with a wooden spoon. Stir in the yoghurt, followed by the milk a little at a time. Return to a fairly high heat and bring to the boil for 2 -3 minutes, stirring all the time. Remove from the heat and season to taste. Add the chicken and fennel slices.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Return the dish to a fast boil, stirring constantly then cover and put in the centre of the oven. Put the tomatoes in boiling water for a minute, then drain and skin. When the casserole has cooked for 45 minutes, add the whole tomatoes and return to the oven for another 15 minutes. Remove, check the seasoning and pour into a 3½ - 4 pint pie dish and leave until cold.
Roll the pastry on a floured board to just bigger than the pie dish. Dampen the edges of the dish and lay the pastry on top, pressing the edges with the back of a knife. Cut off the excess pastry, roll out the trimmings and use to rim and decorate the pie. Poke two holes for the steam to escape. Brush the pastry with the egg yolk and bake in the centre of the oven 200°C for 30 - 40 minutes until brown.

recipes.Title: Fettuccine alla papalina
recipes.Ingredients:
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
25g butter
1 small onion, finely chopped
60g frozen peas
100g cooked ham, thickly cut, cut into small cubes
160g egg fettuccine (or tagliatelle)
3 egg yolks
30g grated Parmesan cheese
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Place a pan over a gentle heat, melt the olive oil and butter and steam-fry the onion for about 10 minutes until softened. Turn the heat up to medium, add the frozen peas and ham with a little salt and pepper and cook for about four minutes or until the peas are cooked.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the fettuccine until al dente (check the instructions on the packet for precise cooking times).
In a bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and grated Parmesan with a little black pepper.
When the pasta is cooked, drain and transfer to the pan with the peas and ham, along with a little of the pasta cooking water. Mix together and cook over a high heat for a minute, so that everything is well combined.
Remove from the heat, pour in the egg mixture, mix well and serve immediately with a sprinkling of black pepper.

recipes.Title: Pasta e fagioli
recipes.Ingredients:
125g tubetti pasta (can use fresh penne cur into two)
225g canned borlotti or cannellini beans
180g fresh tomatoes, quartered
4 rashers bacon, chopped
1 carrot, finely chopped
2 shallots, finely chopped
2 cloves garlic
4 tbsp EV olive oil
fresh parsley, finely chopped
fresh basil, coarsely chopped
salt
black pepper
recipes.Preparation: Drain the canned beans. Sauté the carrot and onion and bacon until softened and then add the lightly crushed garlic and cook for a minute. Add the tomatoes, stir well and cook for 2 minutes. Add the beans and a tbsp of finely chopped parsley and simmer for 1 minute. Mash the tomatoes a little, add a cup of water and turn the heat down to cook for about 10 minutes. Finally, add a cup of water, bring to the boil and add the pasta. Let the pasta cook over a low heat, adding more water as required. Cook until al dente and add the basil. The secret is to not add all the water at once.

recipes.Title: Garganelli alla norcina
recipes.Ingredients:
For the pasta garganelli:
4 large egg yolks
150g ‘00’ flour
semolina flour, for dusting
For the alla Norcina:
1 tbsp olive oil
½ white onion, finely chopped
2 garlic cloves, chopped
¼-½ fennel bulb, cored and finely sliced or chopped
2 Italian fennel sausages, removed from their skins
½ tsp dried red chilli flakes
½ tsp fennel seeds
1 sprig fresh rosemary, leaves removed and chopped
50-75ml white wine
75ml double cream
25g Parmesan, grated, plus extra for garnish
salt and freshly ground black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
To make the pasta garganelli, place the egg yolks and flour into a food processor and blend until it comes together as a dough. Remove and wrap in cling film and allow to rest in the fridge for at least an hour.
Roll the pasta dough through a pasta machine, dusting it with semolina flour, until you get to number 5 on the thickness.
Line a tray with baking paper or a dusting of the semolina flour. Cut the pasta sheets into 4-5cm squares and place one onto a gnocchi board so it’s a diamond shape.
Place a wooden dowel, pencil or handle of a wooden spoon at the bottom of the diamond and curl the bottom corner over the handle and start to roll up. Continue to roll until it creates a tube and press down so the corner sticks down. Each one should slide off once complete. Repeat for the remaining squares and place on the tray. Allow to rest for 30 minutes to 1 hour before cooking.
To make the alla norcina, heat a sauté pan on a medium heat and add the oil. Once hot add the onions, garlic and fennel and cook for 5 minutes or until soft.
Add the sausage meat and cook until golden brown, then add the chilli flakes, fennel seeds and rosemary and cook for 2 minutes.
Deglaze the pan with the white wine and allow to reduce by half. Add the cream and cook for a further 1-2 minutes, then finish with the Parmesan and season with salt and pepper.
To serve, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta for 3 minutes.
Once the pasta is cooked add a little of the pasta water to the sausage pan to create a sauce. Add the cooked pasta to the sauce, stir until all the pasta is coated in the sauce and then serve into warm bowls.
Garnish with the extra Parmesan.

recipes.Title: Beef mince pie
recipes.Ingredients:
1 onion, sliced
1 carrot, grated
2 garlic cloves, finely sliced
chilli flakes to taste
450g minced beef
salt
black pepper
1 tsp garlic powder
sprig of thyme
1½ tbsp red wine vinegar
2 heaped tbsp flour
720ml beef stock
150g frozen peas
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
180ml double cream
Handful of parsley, chopped
50g parmesan cheese
1 egg
shortcrust or puff pastry
recipes.Preparation: Melt some butter in a pan and fry the onion for a minute then add the carrot and cook for 4 minutes. Add salt and cook for a minute. Push the veg to one side and add the minced beef. Season with salt and pepper then put in the garlic powder,  then add the vinegar to deglaze. Add the flour and fully mix, then the beef stock. Bring to the simmer, stirring continually, then add Worcestershire sauce, cream and parsley. Simmer for 5 minutes until thickened then add the cheese, stirring until fully mixed. Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning as necessary. Pour the sauce into a pie dish, cover with either short crust or puff pastry, brush with egg and bake in the oven at 200°C for 20 - 30 minutes

recipes.Title: Chicken cacciatore
recipes.Ingredients:
1.5 kg chicken 
450 g peeled tomatoes or tomato passata 
1 onion
2 carrots
1 stick celery
2 cloves garlic
150 ml red wine
4 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil
3 sprigs rosemary
50 g black olives - pitted (taggiasca)
salt - to taste
black pepper - to taste
recipes.Preparation:
To make chicken cacciatore, start by preparing the chicken. If you bought it whole, cut it into quarters and then separate the chicken thighs, breast and wings. Remove excess fat but do not remove the skin completely.
Place the chicken pieces in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper, then add rosemary, garlic, half a glass of wine and two tablespoons of oil. Stir and cover. Allow to marinate for about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare the soffritto. Peel and finely chop the onion, carrots and celery. In a saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons of oil. It doesn't take long for the skin of the chicken to release its fat during cooking. Now put in the chicken pieces well drained from the marinating liquid (but keep it aside because we will need it for cooking). Cook over high heat for a few minutes, turning it on all sides.
When the chicken has browned in all its parts, especially the skin, add the chopped vegetables and the marinating liquid with the garlic and rosemary. Stir everything well and cook for about 5 minutes over medium heat.
Now raise the heat and deglaze with the remaining red wine. Let the alcoholic part evaporate completely. Then turn the heat down.
Remove the garlic and rosemary, add the peeled tomatoes with their juice for a rustic tomato cacciatore sauce and stir.
Cover with a lid and cook over moderate heat for about 45 minutes. Add the pitted black olives (optional). Obviously the cooking time depends a lot on the size of the chicken pieces. However definitely not less than 30 minutes from now. The chicken is ready when the meat pulls away from the bones and the sauce has set. If the sauce is too runny, cook for another 5 minutes without the lid, turning up the heat.
When cooked, add salt and pepper to your taste. Then let the chicken rest for a few minutes before enjoying it. Add a little fresh rosemary and serve this traditional chicken cacciatore hot.

recipes.Title: Chicken tandoori
recipes.Ingredients:
6 chicken pieces, 2 bone-in thighs, 2 drumsticks, 2 breasts, all skinless
6 garlic cloves, peeled
1 tbsp grated ginger
1-1½ tsp salt
6 tbsp lemon or lime juice, or white-wine vinegar
1 tsp cumin seeds
2 green chillies
250g thick, greek-style plain yoghurt
4 tsp garam masala
Black pepper
2 tbsp sweet paprika, or 1 tbsp mild chilli powder
2 tbsp ghee or oil
recipes.Preparation:
Cut a couple of deep slashes into each piece of chicken. Peel the ginger and garlic, then mash both to a paste with the salt in a mortar or mini chopper, then stir in the lemon juice. Rub this mix all over the chicken, cover and leave for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan until aromatic, then crush to a powder. Finely chop the chilli and mash to a paste, then add it to the mixer with the cumin. Stir both into the yoghurt, then mix in the garam masala and a good grind of black pepper.

Smear the paprika all over the chicken, followed by the yoghurt, making sure to get this as far into the cuts as possible, then cover and chill for four to six hours. Take the chicken out of the fridge half an hour before you want to start cooking it.

Light the barbecue or heat the oven to 240°C (230°C fan) (or as high as it will go). Once the barbecue or oven is ready, grease the barbecue grill or a baking tray with ghee or oil, then lay on the chicken pieces, shaking off any excess marinade back into the bowl.

Grill or roast for 15 minutes, then brush all over with the extra marinade and turn over the chicken pieces. Cook for 10-15 minutes longer, or until cooked through and beginning to char; check on the breasts after 10 minutes, just to be on the safe side.

recipes.Title: Butter chicken
recipes.Ingredients:
1kg chicken thighs, skinned and cut into small pieces

For the marinade:
Juice of 1 large lemon
2 tbsp  oil
1 tsp  salt
1 dsp garlic paste
1 dsp ginger paste
1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp ground coriander
½ tsp ground turmeric
1 dsp tandoori masala

For the sauce:
15 raw cashews, soaked in water for 15 minutes
250ml passata
2 tbsp ghee or butter
2 medium red onions, blended with 2 tbsp water if needed
1 tbsp garlic
1 tbsp ginger paste
1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder or hot paprika
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp ground coriander
½ tsp sugar, or to taste
100g butter
200ml double cream, whisked
1 tbsp kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves)
½ tsp garam masala
salt, to taste

For the garam masala (makes 170g):
6 tbsp coriander seeds
6 tbsp cumin seeds
5 tsp black peppercorns
4 tbsp fennel seeds
3 tsp cloves
7.5cm real cinnamon stick
5 dried Indian bay leaves
20 green cardamom pods, lightly bruised
2 large pieces of mace

For the tandoori masala (makes 120g):
3 tbsp coriander seeds
3 tbsp cumin seeds
1 tbsp black mustard seeds
5cm real cinnamon stick
Small piece of mace
3 dried Indian bay leaves
1 tbsp ground ginger
2 tbsp garlic powder
2 tbsp dried onion powder
2 tbsp amchoor
1 tbsp (or more) red food colouring powder (optional)
recipes.Preparation:
For the garam masala: Roast all the spices in a dry frying pan over a medium-high heat until warm to the touch and fragrant, moving them around in the pan as they roast and being careful not to burn them. If they begin to smoke, take them off the heat immediately. Tip the warm spices onto a plate and leave to cool, then grind to a fine powder in a spice grinder or pestle and mortar. Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place and use within two months for optimal flavour.
For the tandoori masala: Roast the whole spices in a dry frying pan over a medium-high heat until warm to the touch and fragrant, moving them around in the pan as they roast and being careful not to burn them. If they begin to smoke, take them off the heat. Tip onto a plate to cool. Grind to a fine powder in a spice grinder or pestle and mortar, then tip into a bowl. Stir in the ground ginger, garlic powder, onion powder and amchoor. Stir in the red food colouring powder (if using). The masala will not look overly red like the commercial brands. Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place and use as required, within two months for optimal flavour.
For the butter chicken: Whisk all the marinade ingredients together in a large mixing bowl.
Add the chicken pieces and stir them in to coat. Allow to marinate for 30 minutes or up to four hours but no longer! Strain the soaked raw cashews and blend them with the passata for the sauce together until smooth. Set aside.
When ready to cook, heat the ghee or oil in your slow cooker using the sauté/searing mode or in a pan over a medium–high heat. When it begins to bubble lightly, remove as much of the marinade from the chicken as you can and retain all the marinade. Sauté the chicken in one layer for about five to seven minutes to lightly char the exterior. Transfer to a plate using a slotted spoon. The chicken will not be cooked through at this point.
Now stir in the blended onions and fry for about five minutes to cook out the raw flavour. Then stir in the garlic and ginger paste and fry for an additional minute. Stir in the chilli powder or paprika, cumin, ground coriander and sugar, then pour in the blended passata and cashews and bring to a simmer. Stir in the chicken and all the marinade. Bring back to a simmer.
In your slow cooker, put on the lid and cook for three hours on the high setting or six to eight hours on low until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the butter and let it melt into the sauce. Then add the whisked cream (you don’t have to add it all if you don’t want to).
Add the kasoori methi by rubbing it between your fingers over the sauce, then stir in the garam masala. Season with salt to taste just before serving.

recipes.Title: Dal Makhani
recipes.Ingredients:
300g black urad dal, soaked overnight in cold water
750ml boiling water, plus extra if needed
5 tbsp oil
2 onions, finely chopped
1 tbsp garlic paste
1 tbsp ginger paste
2 tomatoes, diced
2 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
1 tsp ground turmeric
1 tbsp garam masala
1 tsp paprika
250ml single cream
2 tsp salt, or to taste
3 tbsp butter, or to taste
4 tbsp chopped coriander leaves, to garnish
For the garam masala (makes 170g):
6 tbsp coriander seeds
6 tbsp cumin seeds
5 tsp black peppercorns
4 tbsp fennel seeds
3 tsp cloves
7.5cm real cinnamon stick
5 dried Indian bay leaves
20 green cardamom pods, lightly bruised
2 large pieces of mace
recipes.Preparation:
For the garam masala: Roast all the spices in a dry frying pan over a medium-high heat until warm to the touch and fragrant, moving them around in the pan as they roast and being careful not to burn them. If they begin to smoke, take them off the heat immediately. Tip the warm spices onto a plate and leave to cool, then grind to a fine powder in a spice grinder or pestle and mortar. Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place and use within two months for optimal flavour.
For the dal makhani: For best results, rinse and then soak the urad lentils for eight hours. Rinsing is required but you could get away with not soaking them. It might just take longer for them to cook.
Place the lentils in your slow cooker, pour in the water and cook on low for eight hours. Sometime during the day, when it is convenient, heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and add the chopped onions. Fry for 10 minutes, or until the onions are soft, translucent and lightly browned and then add the garlic and ginger paste and fry for a further minute. Turn off the heat and stir in the tomatoes, chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala and paprika. Stir for a minute into the hot oil, then set aside.
Check the lentils after eight hours to ensure they are fall-apart soft. If not, continue cooking. Once soft, mash them with a potato masher or blend using a stick blender.
Pour in the prepared onion and spice mixture. You want the dal makhani to be good and hot, so if serving later you could reheat it using the sauté/searing mode of your slow cooker or in a pot on your stove.
Just before serving, stir in most of the cream and season with salt to taste. Top with the butter, which will melt into the dal. I usually swirl a little cream on top at the end before garnishing with the chopped coriander.
recipes.Keywords: lentils, onion, tomato, cream, curry, spicy

recipes.Title: Lamb niharil
recipes.Ingredients:
70ml rapeseed oil or ghee
2 onions, thinly sliced
1 tbsp garlic
1 tbsp ginger paste
2-4 lamb shanks, about 1kg
½ tsp salt, plus extra to taste
For the spice blend:
1 whole nutmeg, crushed into small pieces
1 blade of mace
2 tbsp fennel seeds
3 Indian bay leaves, shredded
2.5cm real cinnamon stick or cassia bark, broken into small pieces
1 tsp black peppercorns
1 tsp nigella seeds
1 tsp cloves
2 tsp cumin seeds
1 tsp paprika
1 tsp hot chilli powder
1 tsp ground ginger
2 generous tbsp chapati flour
To serve:
Rice, chapatis or rumali roti
5cm piece of root ginger, peeled and julienned
2-3 hot fresh green chillies, finely sliced
1 handful of coriander leaves
Lemon wedges
recipes.Preparation:
Place all the whole spices for the blend in a spice grinder and grind to a fine powder. There is no need to roast them first when making a nihari. Add the paprika, chilli powder, ginger and chapati flour and blend again to combine. Set aside.
Heat the oil or ghee in your slow cooker using the sauté/searing mode or in a pan over a medium–high heat and add the sliced onions. Fry for about eight minutes or until soft, brown and translucent.
Stir in the garlic and ginger paste and fry for another minute. Season the meat with the salt and add it to the pot. Stir regularly for about five minutes to brown the meat and then add the nihari spice blend. Stir well so the meat is completely coated with the spice blend and then add 500 millilitres of water.
Cover with the lid and set your slow cooker to the high setting for four hours or low for six to eight hours. Push the meat down as much as you can into the liquid. The meat will reduce in size as it cooks and there will be more gravy when finished, so don’t be tempted to add more liquid.
When the meat is fall-apart tender, lift the lid. If it is too watery, you can reduce it down using the sauté/searing function of your slow cooker with the lid off, or in a pan. The sauce should be quite thick thanks to the flour in the spice blend. Season with salt to taste and serve over rice or with chapatis or rumali roti. Serve with the ginger, green chillies, coriander leaves and lemon wedges, which can be added to taste at the table.

recipes.Title: Chicken, bacon and sausage pie
recipes.Ingredients:
2 rashers of smoked streaky bacon
2 chicken thighs (100g each), skin off, bone out
2 good sausages
2 leeks
2 small potatoes (100g each)
2 tsp (heaped) English mustard
2 tbsp (heaped) plain flour
500 ml chicken stock
500 ml semi-skimmed milk
85 g watercress
1 tbsp olive oil (for brushing the rim of the pie dish)
320 g ready-rolled puff pastry
1 large egg
recipes.Preparation:
Slice the bacon and place in a large shallow casserole pan on a medium heat. Chop the chicken and sausages into 3cm chunks, and add to the pan. Cook until lightly golden, stirring regularly, while you trim and wash the leeks, peel the potatoes, chop it all into 3cm chunks, then stir in with a good splash of water. Cook for 10 minutes, or until the leeks have softened, stirring occasionally, scraping up any sticky bits, and adding an extra splash of water, if needed. Stir in the mustard and flour, followed by the stock, then the milk. Bring to the boil, simmer for 15 minutes on a low heat, stirring regularly, then season to perfection, tasting and tweaking. Carefully pour everything through a colander to separate the filling from the sauce. Pour the sauce into a blender, add the watercress and blitz until smooth. Spoon the filling into a 20cm pie dish with 100ml of sauce. Let everything cool, then cover and refrigerate overnight.

TO SERVE Preheat the oven to 180ºC. Brush the rim of the pie dish with olive oil. Cut the pastry into 2cm-thick strips, using a crinkly pasta cutter if you’ve got one, then arrange over the dish – I like a messy lattice. Eggwash all the pastry, then bake the pie for 45 minutes, or until the pastry is golden and the filling is piping hot. Gently heat up the watercress sauce to serve on the side.
recipes.Keywords: chicken, bacon, sausage, puff pastry, pie

recipes.Title: Pork ribs with cabbage and celeriac pureé
recipes.Ingredients:
Ribs in beer:
1 kg Spare Ribs
2 bottles Porter beer
10 Peppercorns
4  Bay Leaves
Marinade:
Salt and Pepper
30 g Passata or chopped tomatoes
20 g Brown sugar
14 g Spice Mix Ankerkraut's Pull That Piggy. Includes paprika, salt, sugar, onion and garlic, black pepper, cumin, oregano, celery, bay leaves, jalapenos.
Celery/onion puree:
½ a Celeriac
1 Onion
2 cloves Garlic
200 g Cream perhaps a bit more if it doesn't cover
200 g Whole Milk perhaps a bit more if it doesn't cover
5 sprigs Fresh thyme
15 g Butter
Salt
Fried scallions:
½ a Pointed Cabbage
15 g butter
Salt and Pepper
Cayenne Pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Marinated Spareribs:
Start by removing the largest layer of fat and tendons from the meat. Next, remove the membranes. Place your spareribs in a pot or container with a lid. Cut them into smaller pieces if needed. Add beer, peppercorns, and bay leaves to the container along with the meat. Top up with extra water until the meat is covered. Let it sit for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, so they can soak up the beer for many hours.
Boiling the Spareribs:
Bring the liquid with your spareribs to a boil. There will be foam forming on the surface of the liquid, remove it with a spoon. Let it boil for 30-45 minutes, depending on how tender you want them. Take them out of the pot and rinse them under cold water so the last bit of foam is washed off. Put them in a bag and add the marinade mixture. Shake the bag well (be careful due to the sharp bones) to distribute the marinade evenly. The meat can now be refrigerated until it's ready for the oven, or let the marinade sit for at least 30 minutes before putting them in the oven.
Roasting the Spareribs:
Preheat the oven to 225°C fan. The oven can be substituted with a hot grill. Cook the meat for 15-20 minutes in the oven. The marinade on top should just get some color and caramelize a bit. Take the meat out of the oven and it’s ready to serve.
Celery/Onion Puree:
Wash, peel and halve the celeriac. Cut it into small cubes. Next, peel and chop 1 clove of garlic and 1 onion into small pieces. Put everything in a pot and add cream and whole milk until everything in the pot is covered. Place fresh thyme sprigs in a tea strainer so that it doesn't get dispersed in the mixture - just the flavor. Bring to a boil, stirring regularly, and lower the heat. Let it simmer for about 20 minutes until everything is completely tender. The key for me to getting a good puree is the following: Drain the liquid (save it in a jug/container) and (immersion) blend the tender vegetables with a bit of the cooking liquid and butter. Add a little liquid at a time until you are satisfied with the consistency. It should be fairly thick and smooth.
Taste the puree and season with salt (possibly white pepper) until you are happy with the flavor.
Transfer the puree to a new (and clean) pot and warm it over low heat for a few minutes.
Fried Cabbage
Cut your cabbage into 2 halves and use only one part for this meal.
Melt your ghee or butter and mix it in a bowl with salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Remove the outer leaf and brush the cabbage with the spice mixture.
Fry the cabbage on one side for 3-4 minutes (my cabbage was small - use 5 minutes for an average/large cabbage).
Turn the cabbage to the other inside and fry for another 3-4 minutes.
Finally, give it 3 more minutes on the outer side.
Take the cabbage off the pan.
Serving
Chop the salted almonds into smaller pieces.
Cut your spareribs into slices along the bones.
Serve spareribs with puree, cabbage, chopped almonds, and pickled red onions.

recipes.Title: Chicken cacciatore 2
recipes.Ingredients:
750 g chicken 
225 g peeled tomatoes or tomato passata 
1 small onion
1carrot
1 stick celery
4 cloves garlic
75 ml red wine
2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil
1 sprig rosemary
25 g black olives - pitted (taggiasca)
salt - to taste
black pepper - to taste
recipes.Preparation:
To make chicken cacciatore, start by preparing the chicken. If you bought it whole, cut it into quarters and then separate the chicken thighs, breast and wings. Remove excess fat but do not remove the skin completely.
Place the chicken pieces in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper, then add rosemary, garlic, half a glass of wine and two tablespoons of oil. Stir and cover. Allow to marinate for about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare the soffritto. Peel and finely chop the onion, carrots and celery. In a saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons of oil. It doesn't take long for the skin of the chicken to release its fat during cooking. Now put in the chicken pieces well drained from the marinating liquid (but keep it aside because we will need it for cooking). Cook over high heat for a few minutes, turning it on all sides.
When the chicken has browned in all its parts, especially the skin, add the chopped vegetables and the marinating liquid with the garlic and rosemary. Stir everything well and cook for about 5 minutes over medium heat.
Now raise the heat and deglaze with the remaining red wine. Let the alcoholic part evaporate completely. Then turn the heat down.
Remove the garlic and rosemary, add the peeled tomatoes with their juice for a rustic tomato cacciatore sauce and stir.

However definitely not less than 30 minutes from now. The chicken is ready when the meat pulls away from the bones and the sauce has set. If the sauce is too runny, cook for another 5 minutes without the lid, turning up the heat.

recipes.Title: Penne with smoked salmon
recipes.Ingredients:
300g penne rigata
200g smoked salmon, cut into strips
150g cream cheese (Philadelphia)
1 lemon
1 large or 2 small shallots, chopped
4 cloves garlic
bunch of parsley, chopped
Extra virgin olive oil
salt
black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Heat a casserole with olive oil to medium and add the onions. Cook for around 7 minutes and add the garlic and parsley. Now add the zest and the juice of the lemon.
Heat a large saucepan of salted water and add the pasta; cook for 11 minutes until al dente.
Drain and add the pasta to the casserole with the onions; reserve the pasta water. Mix thoroughly adding pasta water to make it creamy then add the cream cheese and mix, adding more pasta water as necessary,
Turn off the heat and add most of the salmon to the pasta and toss. Warm the remaining salmon and plate the pasta with a few pieces of salmon on top.

recipes.Title: balsamic chicken wings
recipes.Ingredients:
Around 12 chicken wings, cut into two
8 cloves garlic, minced
2 tbsp honey
60g tomato puree
2 tbsp rosemary, chopped
175ml white wine
300ml chicken stock
118ml balsamic vinegar
salt black pepper
garlic powder
olive oil + toasted sesame oil
recipes.Preparation: Dust the wings in salt, pepper and garlic powder then heat around 100ml of oil in a large pan. When the oil is very hot, fry the wings on both sides until golden brown. Remove the wings from the pan and place on kitchen roll. Drain off most of the oil from the pan and then fry the garlic over a low heat. Add the tomato puree and a tbsp of water and fry for about 5 minutes. Add the wine, stock, balsamic vinegar, honey and rosemary. Bring this to the boil and reduce to half the volume, about 5 minutes. Now add the chicken wings, cover and simmer for 25 minutes. Remove the lid and cook for another 10 minutes. Remove the wings and reduce the sauce until really thick and then add the wings again to coat in the sticky sauce.

recipes.Title: Chicken curry
recipes.Ingredients:
Marinade:
4 tbsp full fat Greek yoghurt
1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder
1 tsp turmeric powder
6 cloves garlic, minced
salt
2 chicken legs divided into drumsticks and thighs
Curry:
Butter, to fry
1 tsp cummin seeds 
1 stick cinnamon
2 bay leaves
2 green cardamom
2 black cardamom
1 clove
1 onion, chopped
salt, black pepper
2 tbsp sugar
1 tbsp ginger, finely chopped
green chillies, finely chopped, to taste
red chilli powder
tbsp cumin, ground
tbsp coriander
6 tomatoes, chopped
tbsp garam masala
coriander leaf
dash of cream
fenugreek leaves
lemon juice
recipes.Preparation:
Mix the marinade components in a bowl and add the chicken; massage well and leave in the fridge for 2 hours.
Heat the butter slowly in a wide cast iron casserole with a lid over a low heat and add the spices cooking slowly. Add the chopped onion and salt and cook over a high heat for 8 minutes until caramelised. Now add the sugar, ginger and green chilli and cook until the raw aromas have subsided. Add red chilli powder and cumin then add a splah of water to stop the spices from burning. Cook until a paste and then add the tomatoes. Cook for about 7 minutes at high heat then add the marinated chicken. Sear the chicken and heat until cooked. Wash the marinade bowl with water and add to the pan to make the sauce, adjust the seasoning, turn the heat down and put the lid on and cook for 20 minutes. When cooked, add the garam masala, chopped coriander leaf (and stems), cream, fenugreek leaves and lemon juice.

recipes.Title: Chicken adobo
recipes.Ingredients:
453.5 g chicken cut into serving pieces
1 dried bay leaf
30 ml soy sauce
33.5 ml white vinegar
5 cloves garlic crushed
177.5 ml water
30 ml cooking oil
2 g sugar
1 g whole peppercorn
Salt to taste
recipes.Preparation:
Combine the chicken, soy sauce and crushed garlic in a large bowl, mix well and marinate for at least 1 hour. The longer the chicken marinates, the better the flavor.
Remove the chicken pieces from the marinade using kitchen tongs. Scoop out the crushed garlic with a slotted spoon. Reserve the garlic and marinade separately.
Heat a cooking pot and pour in 3 tablespoons of cooking oil. Once the oil gets hot, pan-fry the marinated chicken for 2 minutes per side. Remove the chicken from the pot and set it aside.
Pour the remaining cooking oil into the same pot. Add the garlic from the marinade and sauté until it starts to brown. Return the chicken to the pot. Add the remaining marinade, whole peppercorns, and dried bay leaves. Pour in the water and let it boil. Cover the pot and simmer for 30 minutes, or until the chicken becomes tender.
Pour in the vinegar. Let it boil for 1 minute without stirring. Stir, then continue simmering uncovered for 15 minutes. Add the sugar and salt as needed. Stir, then turn the heat off.

recipes.Title: Fettucine with roasted tomatoes, garlic and basil
recipes.Ingredients:
For the base:
375g cherry tomatoes
15 garlic cloves, peeled
120ml olive oil
salt
For the sauce:
3 tbsp butter
1 tbsp balsamic glaze
1 handful fresh basil leaves
1 tsp chilli flakes
1 tsp oregano
Black pepper
To serve:
140g dried or 280g fresh fettucine
fresh basil
parmesan
recipes.Preparation:
Place the tomatoes and garlic in a covered casserole and cover with olive oil. Roast in an oven at 190°C until soft and lightly caramelised. Transfer to a blender with a few spoons of the oil and blend until smooth and thick. Mix in the butter, balsamic glaze, chilli flakes, oregano and black pepper, then blend again until mixed in.
Meanwhile, cook the fettucine in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving some of the pasta water, and add the sauce. Add some pasta water as required and toss to coat. Serve with torn basil leaves and grated parmesan.

recipes.Title: Chicken wing BBQ marinade
recipes.Ingredients:
3 tbsp honey
3 tbsp cider vinegar
2 tbsp olive oil
6 cloves garlic, crushed
1 tbsp paprika
2 tsp smoked paprika
2 tsp celery salt
salt
black pepper
Hot chilli sauce, to taste
recipes.Preparation:
Mix all the ingredients together. Stir in the wings and make sure all are covered in the marinade.
Leave in the fridge for 2 - 4 hours.

recipes.Title: John's Salmon Symphony
recipes.Ingredients:
2 salmon fillets

For the vegetable bed:

1 red pepper, sliced
1 onion
12 cherry tomatoes, halved
2 garlic cloves, crushed

For the topping:

½ ripe avocado
1 shallot, finely chopped
1 cherry tomato, chopped
chilli powder, to taste
lime juice
 
For the sauce:

60ml white wine
1 garlic clove, crushed
60ml double cream
10ml fresh lemon juice
1 tbsp very cold butter
salt
black pepper
recipes.Preparation:
Topping:
Mash the avovado with the tomato, shallot and lime juice until creamy but with some texture. Warm in the microwave until only just above tepid. Too hot and the rexture will change and it will brown.
Vegetables:
Season and roast the onions and red pepper for about 10 minutes then add the garlic and tomatoes and roast for another 5 minutes. Check that the tomatoes have softened but are still in one piece.
Sauce:
Put the wine and garlic into a small saucepan and bring to the simmer. Allow the wine to reduce by about 50% over 10 minutes. Whisk in the cream and simmer until it coats the back of a spoon. Stir in the lemon juice and cook for another 2 minutes. Remove the pan from the heat and whisk in the butter a small amount at a time until the butter has emulsified into the sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
Salmon:
Season the salmon and place on a baking tray sprayed with a little olive oil. Bake in the oven at 220°C for 15 minutes.
Serve:
Pour the hot sauce onto the plate. Place the vegetables over the sauce in a rectangular shape to match the salmon. Lay the salmon on top of the vegetables then top the fish with a layer of the avacado. Decorate with small inverted sprigs of basil.

recipes.Title: Banana roll
recipes.Ingredients:
Filling:
200g softened cream cheese use the other 1 ounce for the icing
100g sugar
1 egg
3 tablespoons milk

Cake:
63g plain flour
½ teaspoon baking powder
¼ teaspoon baking soda
4 large eggs separated
½ teaspoon vanilla
130g white sugar divided
1 large banana or 2 small, mashed
40g chopped walnuts
50g cup blueberries

Glaze:
30g cream cheese – softened
150g powdered sugar
1 teaspoon vanilla
2-3 teaspoons milk
recipes.Preparation:
Grease and line a 40 x 25 x 2.5cm baking tray with parchment. Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cream Cheese Filling:
Prepare filling first by mixing the cream cheese and sugar in a small mixing bowl until smooth with an electric mixer. Add the egg and milk and beat at medium speed until combined. Spread the filling in the prepared pan.
Cake:
Gather the walnuts and blueberries and place them on a cutting board. Using a chef's knife chop this mixture into smaller pieces. Combe the flour, baking powder, and baking soda. Set aside. In a large mixing bowl beat the four egg yolks and vanilla for 5 minutes with an electric mixer at medium speed until the mixture is thick and lemon colored. Gradually add the sugar and mix on medium speed until combined. Stir in most of the mashed banana and the chopped walnuts and blueberries. Reserve the remainder for the top of the cake. In another large mixing bowl beat the four egg whites at medium-high speed to soft peaks. Gradually add the other 65g of sugar, beating on high speed until stiff peaks form. Add the banana batter to the egg whites and gently fold them in until incorporated. Add half of the flour mixture and start folding it into the batter, then add the rest of the flour and continue folding in the flour until combined.
Gently pour the cake mixture over the cream cheese filling mixture, and spread the batter out making sure to get into the corners. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes. While the cake is baking prepare a towel sprinkled with powdered sugar to turn the cake out on. When the cake is done let it sit for 5 minutes. Run a knife around the edges of the baking sheet to loosen the cake. Pick up the pan with a towel or hot pads then position the pan next to the towel and quickly flip the cake out onto the powdered sugar-covered towel and peel off the parchment paper.
Start rolling the cake from the narrow end; use the towel to help roll the cake. When rolled, keep the seam side down on the cake so it doesn't unroll. Let the cake sit for about 10 minutes to firm up and cool. Transfer the cake to a serving platter and let cool completely before adding the glaze and toppings.
Glaze and Topping:
Make the glaze by beating together the softened cream cheese, vanilla, powdered sugar, and milk until it is a drizzling consistency. When the cake is cooled, spread the glaze over the top of the cake then sprinkle with remaining chopped walnuts and blueberries.

recipes.Title: Hokkaido baked cheese tarts
recipes.Ingredients:
For the mini tart shells:
45 g Icing sugar
115 g plain flour
15 g Almond flour
Pinch of salt
155 g Unsalted butter, cold, cut into chunks
½ Egg 

For the cheese filling:
115 g Cream cheese
25 g Parmesan cheese, finely grated
23 g butter
25 g Whole milk
25 g Heavy cream
23 g Icing sugar
1 Egg yolk
½ tablespoon Corn starch
recipes.Preparation:
For the tart shells:
Measure and cut butter into chunks and place it into the freezer for a few minutes. Sift together dry ingredients; flour, icing sugar, almond, salt. Add very cold butter chunks into the dry ingredients, and rub the mixture between your hands until it becomes a sand-like consistency. Add egg into the mixture and mix with your hands just until the dough comes together. Knead the dough with the palm of your hand for a minute or two, just until the dough becomes smooth. Do not over-knead the dough. Roll the dough out into 2mm thickness.
Place the dough into the freezer for 15 min in between cling film.
Prepare your muffin pan or 6 mini tart molds. Take the dough sheet out from the freezer, remove the top cling film, and cut out circles, using a cookie cutter. With your fingers, press the dough circles into the tin one by one. Make sure that you work with a dough that is cold enough to be able to handle. Pierce the dough with a fork, then freeze the dough for 1 hour before baking.
Pre-heat oven to 180°C (no fan). Bake for 15 min. After 15 minutes the pastry cases will somewhat contract within the pan so you will be able to easily remove them. Place upside down on a baking sheet and bake for further 10-15 minutes at 160°C (no fan). 
Filling:
In a bowl with a hand whisk, whip together sugar and egg yolk until slightly fluffy for about 1-2 minutes, then whisk in corn starch until thoroughly incorporated and have a smooth paste. Heat milk, cream, butter, Philadephia cheese, and grated parmesan in a saucepan on low-medium heat, then remove it as soon as the ingredients melt together. By this time, the mixture probably will be simmering. Pour the warm cheese mixture over the egg yolk mixture slowly while whisking vigorously with a hand whisk. Pour the mixture back into the saucepan and cook on medium heat for a few minutes until it thickens. Place the filling into a shallow bowl and cover the entire surface with plastic wrap to avoid skin forming on top. Chill it for an hour before using it.
Pre-heat oven to 220°C (no fan). Fill each tart shell with the cheese filling using a piping bag.
Whisk one egg with a splash of water and apply a light egg wash on top of the filling. Bake for 5-10 minutes or until the top slightly caramelizes. They can be made ahead of time and warmed to serve.

recipes.Title: Blueberry compote
recipes.Ingredients:
240g blueberries
1½ tbsp sugar
20 ml lemon juice
1 tsp vanilla extract
½ lemon zest
pinch of salt
1½ tbsp butter
recipes.Preparation:
Prepare the berries:
Rinse fresh blueberries and remove any stems or shriveled berries. Frozen berries can be used directly without thawing.

To cook: 
In a medium saucepan, combine half of the blueberries, sugar, lemon juice, and butter. Heat over medium-low heat until the sugar dissolves and the berries start to release their juices, about 8–10 minutes. Stir in the rest of the blueberries and cook for another 5–8 minutes until the mixture thickens slightly and the berries are soft but still hold some shape.

Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract, lemon zest and a pinch of salt to enhance the flavor.
